author: WoMin
title: From Mombasa to Yaoundé, the vision and the demand is for reparative justice
content:
Through WoMin’s work alongside African women organising against extractivism, against the drivers of the climate crisis and its impacts, the destruction of the commons through false solutions, unjust energy transitions (and generally a world order that serves a minority over the global majority), we have been asking: what is the full range of impacts and costs in the face of environmental and climate impacts? Who and whose work absorbs these impacts and costs? And what would repair mean from the perspective of women, their communities and the ecosystems they care for and are cared for at the frontline of the climate crisis, where centuries of continued systems of accumulation by dispossession and destruction meet?


Our experience shows us that reparations cannot simply be another form of compensation. They must confront the very systems producing the harm – extractivism, odious and illegitimate debt, colonial legacies, patriarchy, racism, and corporate power promoting more false solutions whose aim is not climate justice but profit. Reparations must indeed offer us all a real chance to build Pan African feminist futures that centre care, including the restoration of the commons, and the conditions that make life possible.


Connecting the “c-words” – colonialism to climate reparations


The recent

African Symposium on Climate Reparations

 in Mombasa, Kenya, started on that same note: “there is no “c-word” that we cannot bring into conversations on climate reparations”, argued a comrade in his opening remarks. And indeed, the current

climate disorder

1

 is a historical process, and Colonialism (the c-word that in other climate justice spaces some shy away from) is part and parcel of it. As is, we argue at WoMin, capitalism. What is more, not only do climate reparations need to address colonialism and neocolonialism, but also the solution to the climate crisis will not be found within capitalism. Or as Audre Lorde put it, “… the master’s tools will never dismantle the master’s house. They may allow us temporarily to beat him at his own game, but they will never enable us to bring about genuine change.”


Not only we need our own tools, but also a broad alliance, as broad, yet united in principles and analysis, as broad and urgent is the task ahead. And the symposium offered an important space to bring together many working for reparations across the continent and in the diaspora, in conversations navigated along four main tracks: rights of nature and ecosystems stewardship; finance, debt and tax justice; law and human rights; and lived realities from frontline communities.


And the timing matters. We are entering the Decade of Justice and Reparations for Africans and People of African Descent, while the debt crisis in Africa continues to exponentially grow and deepen climate vulnerability, false climate solutions continue to expand, further threatening the commons millions of Africans depend upon for their everyday subsistence, and the African Court considers an Advisory Opinion on States’ obligations in the climate crisis.


As powerful expressed in an

open letter

 which emerged from the symposium, a Pan African position and action plan for climate reparations is urgent, but it cannot be constructed only through states, legal and financial tools. Those at the frontlines absorbing the costs of extractivism, ecological destruction and climate disruption have to shape what counts as harm, what constitutes repair, and what must stop. And importantly, we need to organise at all levels the collective power to make repair possible.


African women united for climate justice and reparations


This was the task of the 4th

Women’s Climate Assembly

 (WCA) in Yaoundé, Cameroon, held in early October under the theme, “Our lands, our voices: African women united for climate justice and reparations!”. The Assembly convened over 75 women community leaders, activists, feminist organisations, civil society groups and allies from twelve countries including Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Guinea-Conakry, Liberia, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal, and Zambia.


Oh ancestors, watch over Africa and let everything return to Africa! If we are coveted today, if there are wars, it is because our ancestors bequeathed this land to us. They did not abuse its riches. They used them sustainably. So we ask our ancestors to guide us during this Assembly, so that peace and food …

author: Mada Masr
title: Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure
content:
Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah was fined LE3 million by the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, which convicted her on charges of managing an unlicensed website, issuing an order for the website’s closure. Attalah was taken into custody after the issue of the ruling.


Tuesday’s session at the ninth circuit of the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, presided over by judge Mohamed Mubarak, was temporarily suspended for deliberations after Attalah’s defense counsel requested time to review the case file.


After the court returned from deliberations, the judge ordered the courtroom cleared of everyone except Attalah and her defense counsel, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights’ executive director Hossam Bahgat, who was also present, told Mada Masr. The room then filled with plainclothes officers and guards, with a National Security Agency officer in attendance, he added.


The presiding judge and a Supreme State Security Prosecution representative returned to the session and the judge announced that the court has decided to stand by its rejection of all the procedural arguments presented by the defense, including requests to bring in any documentation or hear any witnesses.


The judge then asked the defense team to present its plea. The counsel insisted that it would not submit a plea as long as its requests were unanswered by the court.


The judge then abruptly asked for a lawyer unknown to any member of the defense counsel to be brought in, “in a move that astonished all those present,” said Bahgat, and announced that the court decided to appoint a lawyer for Attalah.


At that point, all members of the defense counsel cried out to reject the court’s appointment of a lawyer when the eight chosen lawyers were present. Attalah herself spoke to say she did not accept the court-appointed lawyer acting on her behalf, an objection the judge refused to have recorded in the session’s minutes.


“In an even more shocking move,” said Bahgat, the judge himself began to log down the requests of the court-appointed lawyer, without the lawyer having said a word. The judge then read out the conviction amid shouts and protests from the defense counsel.


The judge sentenced Attalah to the maximum possible penalty: a LE3 million fine, the closure of Mada Masr’s website and the confiscation of its property.


Security personnel then surrounded Attalah, lifted her off the ground and took her out of the courtroom, where she remains in custody in the courthouse.

Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure

 first appeared on

Mada Masr

author: Keelan Jacobs
title: First Nations Bank CEO says federal budget is a ‘generational’ opportunity for First Nations
content:
First Nations Bank of Canada (FNBC) president and CEO Bill Lomax says the federal budget offers a rare opening for First Nations to move from consultation into genuine ownership of the infrastructure and energy projects that will define Canada’s economy for decades.


Lomax framed the scale of planned investments in transportation, energy and electricity infrastructure as “a generational opportunity for First Nations to play a leading role in building Canada’s future.”


“When First Nations move beyond participation to become owners, we create lasting economic opportunities, build wealth for future generations and strengthen Canada’s economy as a whole. When First Nations succeed, Canada succeeds,” Lomax said in a statement following the budget. 


“But we need to think beyond consultation, employment and contracting opportunities. While these remain important, First Nations must also be recognized as business partners and owners, with the ability to build businesses, acquire equity and participate directly in the long-term economic benefits these projects generate.”


The FNBC is Canada’s only Indigenous-owned chartered bank, founded in 1996, operates 22 branches and service centres across six provinces and three territories, manages more than $1.6 billion in assets, and through its subsidiary FNB Trust, administers approximately $5.5 billion.


The federal budget, tabled Nov. 5, commits more than $50 billion over 10 years to Indigenous programs and services. The largest single piece is $32 billion over a decade for First Nations housing and on-reserve infrastructure. 


That includes the new First Nations On-Reserve Infrastructure Program, backed by $18.5 billion for infrastructure and $11 billion for housing that aims to maintain, renovate and build thousands of homes over 10 years. 


“This budget is an opportunity to invest in who we are,” Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty told APTN News in an interview Tuesday. “It’s an opportunity to better define who we are. It’s an opportunity to have a strategic approach to what our financial position is going to be, and I think the greatest opportunity of all is to demonstrate to Canadians the fiscal impact that Indigenous people have on the Canadian economy.”


Indigenous Services Canada Minister Mandy Gull Masty at a news conference on Parliament Hill in May. Photo: APTN.


The budget also introduces the new Canada Growth Incentive (CGI) for Canadian entrepreneurs, investors and employees, which is also open to Indigenous business people. The goal of the CGI is to keep investment money in Canada. 


It offers a new capital gains tax exemption for “Canadian builders” of up to $15 million earned from the Canadian businesses they invested in. 

To benefit, Canadians will have to reinvest and keep their money in Canada and Canadian businesses.  


“The Canada Growth Incentive (CGI) will be one of the most significant incentives to attract and retain builders here in Canada by creating the path for entrepreneurs, investors, and employees to reinvest in Canada,” the budget said. “This represents a level shift in the attractiveness of firms, large and small, to invest-and reinvest-in Canada, and deliver lasting prosperity for all Canadians.”  


The budget is also promising money for education, health, child welfare, policing and emergency management. 


The budget also outlines the government’s support for the Indigenous Loan Program that loans money to First Nations for projects. 


“I hope everybody listening or reading our interviews about the budget understands that I’m here to spend money; come to me with your proposals. I’m going to do everything I can to meet the needs, so work with me,” said Gull Masty. 


 Where’s the money?


Aaron Pete, chief of Chawathil First Nation in British Columbia, told APTN that he’s taking a cautious approach to the budget because the money “rarely finds its way to First Nation communities in a constructive way.” 


Chief of Chawathil First Nation Aaron Pete. Photo From aaronpete.com,


“It [the budget] sounds promising, but again, my concern is that it gets stuck in Ottawa and doesn’t actually reach these communities,” he said. 


Pete was a councillor in 2022 and became chief in 2025. He has a podcast where politicians of all stripes are invited to share their opinions on the state of the country and First Nations politics. 


He acknowledged that many of the government’s stated priorities — clean running water …

author: Daron Letts
title: Offshore Western Arctic oil and gas exploration could be back on the table
content:
The days might be numbered for the federal government’s decade-long

moratorium

 on oil and gas exploration in the Western Arctic — at least in its present form.


“There is a review happening,” said Northern and Arctic Affairs Minister Rebecca Chartrand during a news conference at Nunavut Arctic College in Iqaluit on Tuesday.


The moratorium, established in December 2016 by then-prime minister Justin Trudeau, remains in place as the Liberal government charts “the best path forward,” Chartrand said.


The moratorium agreement calls for a review every five years.

This includes ongoing meetings with Inuit organizations and territorial governments, Chartrand said.


At a news conference in Montreal at the same time, Prime Minister Mark Carney highlighted $11 million in funding to support “the governance and oversight of offshore oil and gas activities in the Arctic Ocean.”


“This is capacity funding for Inuit leadership. It is absolutely not in any way, shape, or form a decision about lifting the moratorium,” Carney said.


Chartrand’s comments came in response to questions after a media event about the federal government’s $4 billion in cultural spending outlined in Thursday’s

budget

.


In her opening address at the event, she highlighted the new Canada Creative Credit, an annual tax cut on up to $45,000 of arts-related net business income for artists.


Qikiqtani Inuit Association President Olayuk Akesuk says he and other Inuit leaders met with Northern and Arctic Affairs Minister Rebecca Chartrand virtually two weeks ago. They discussed lifting the decade-long moratorium on oil and gas exploration in the Western Arctic. (Photo by Daron Letts)


“We are also proposing stronger support for film, television, and digital production and a new productivity mega deduction to help eligible businesses invest in equipment and technology,” she added.


Chartrand met with staff at the Inuit Broadcasting Corp. on Monday.


The budget would provide an additional $300 million in funding to the CBC and Radio-Canada. The public broadcaster got $1.46 billion in the 2025-26 fiscal year. The budget also proposes $134 million over four years for the Local Journalism Initiative, a program that supports independent local news in rural, remote, and under-served regions, including the Arctic.


She also highlighted $393 million in spending in support of francophone cultural institutions.


As for the moratorium on oil and gas exploration, Qikiqtani Inuit Association President Olayuk Akesuk and fellow Inuit leaders expressed their perspective with Chartrand during a virtual meeting two weeks ago, he said in an interview Tuesday.


“It is important to go through the regulatory process in order for us to support anything that might impact the environment,” he said. “Let’s work together to ensure that we are doing it properly.”


Nunavut Liberal MP Lori Idlout said she is confident that discussions about any return to exploration will be made in collaboration with Inuit.


— With files from Nehaa Bimal

author: Sharon Zhang
title: “The Time Is Now for Change”: Sanders Says He Won’t Back Schumer for Leader
content:
Emerging leader Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he is refusing to fund the government next month until the war is defunded.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vermont) announced on Tuesday that he will not be supporting Sen. Chuck Schumer’s (D-New York) run for Senate majority leader in the new Congress and suggested that someone else will be running to replace him.

“I personally have known Chuck Schumer for 30 years, and I like Chuck — nobody works harder than Chuck Schumer,” said Sanders in a press conference. “But, in my view, the time is now for change. And I will not be supporting Chuck to be reelected as the Democratic leader.”

This marks the first major public defection in the caucus against Schumer. There hasn’t yet been a senator to formally nominate themselves to challenge Schumer. But Sanders suggested in his remarks that Schumer won’t be running unopposed and floated the name of progressive favorite Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland) for the role.

“I think one of the names out there is Chris Van Hollen. I think Chris has indicated some interest, but you’ll have to talk to him,” Sanders said. Sanders added in an interview that he would back Van Hollen if he ran.

Van Hollen is reportedly actively considering a run. On Tuesday, Van Hollen said at the Popular Mandate conference that he is “actively listening to people who are looking for” change, and called for a “bold agenda.”

“I am in the process right now of calling my colleagues,” he said. “Because at the end of the day, this is a vote in the Democratic caucus. So let’s just keep in touch.”

Further in his press conference, Sanders said that voters must be shown that the party is ready to respond to their demands after Americans entrusted them with a massive congressional majority, adding: “We need a process, we need a vigorous debate about the direction of the Democratic Party.”

Sanders was joined by Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Michigan), who agreed that lawmakers must come together to decide on their goals. Slotkin said that Democrats should withhold quorum if Schumer is the only candidate and doesn’t present a vision for the future of the party.

The two lawmakers had just come out of a meeting with Senate Democrats in which they said Schumer had not provided a clear goal for their upcoming majority.

Flanked by Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-New York), Ruben Gallego (D-Arizona), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-Rhode Island) in a press conference after that same meeting on Tuesday, Schumer said that he’s “confident” he will be reelected as leader.

Polling by YouGov for Indivisible released on Tuesday found that only 10 percent of voters say that Democrats should choose Schumer to be majority leader, while 57 percent said they should choose someone else.

Van Hollen has long criticized Schumer’s leadership as ineffective, especially in times when Schumer has ceded Democrats’ power during the first two years of President Donald Trump’s second term. Progressives have favored the Maryland senator’s actions on foreign policy, including on Israel and Palestinian rights. They have also pointed to Van Hollen’s visit with constituent Kilmar Abrego García after he was deported to El Salvador as a sign of his willingness to fight against the Trump administration.

Michigan Senator-Elect Abdul El-Sayed (D) has said for months that he would support Van Hollen for leader, and repeated that assertion last week after winning his election.

“We have two members in that room, duly elected senators, that would not be there if Schumer and the [Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC)] had had their way,” Van Hollen said at Popular Mandate on Tuesday, likely referring to El-Sayed and Troy Jackson. “Schumer and the DSCC sided with the crypto industry and AIPAC against these candidates.”

author: Mark Engler
title: Democrats should wield their power to return agency to ordinary people
content:
This article

Democrats should wield their power to return agency to ordinary people

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


Too often, we have seen a fundamental asymmetry at work: When Democrats win power, they might pass a modest minimum wage increase. When Republicans are in power, they do things like decimate public sector unions. In the long term, this is an imbalance that leads to ruin. 


Last week’s “blue tsunami” represented a resounding repudiation of the Trump agenda. While it is common that a sitting administration will lose seats in the midterm elections, swings of the magnitude that we have just witnessed are rare and important. For certain, Trump will still try to use the executive branch to wreak havoc on democracy and provide egregious giveaways for  the billionaire class. However, Democratic control of the Senate and the investigatory power of its majority in the House should provide an important check on his ability to do damage. 


Perhaps more importantly, progressive forces made critical gains at the state level. The Democrats

won six new “trifectas”

: in Arizona, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin. Now, if current leads in Kansas and Alaska hold, “about 75 percent of Americans will live in states with Democratic governors,” and roughly 53 percent will reside in places where Democrats control both chambers of the state legislature as well,

Newsweek


reports

.


Of course, we should not assume that Democrats will use their newfound power effectively if left to their own devices. There are significant blocs of the Democratic Party wherein centrist politicians have made careers of “playing to the middle” and embracing pro-corporate neoliberal politics. Should this tendency prevail, the Democrats will have squandered a historic opportunity, to the detriment of social movements and the broader American public alike.


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


Forging an alternative path will mean pushing newly empowered legislators to think and act differently. Passing policies that make a real difference in the lives of working people is critical; however, this is only a first step. For movements for social and economic justice to secure long-term wins, they need to be advocating for how they — and their allies in office — can pursue structural reforms. 


A few years ago, after the 2022 midterms, my brother Paul and I wrote an article

looking at the trifecta power

 that Democrats had gained in multiple states and asking, “Will they actually use it?” More specifically, it asked whether they would use their mandate “to enact changes that increase democratic participation and build progressive power” over the long haul.


When Republicans have gained majorities at the state level “they have used their power to push through reforms that weaken left-leaning constituencies and undermine the Democratic base,” we wrote at the time. “In contrast, when Democrats have been in the majority, they often have failed to reverse these changes or enact meaningful structural reforms — the kind of changes that both improve people’s lives and build power for the grassroots groups that can help them govern on an ongoing basis.” 


Structural reforms can come in many varieties: labor rights, campaign finance issues, measures to encourage and expand voting, redistricting, preemption laws determining whether issues are handled at the state or local level, free speech protections, regulatory modifications that allow for community involvement, and changes to the tort system, to name just a few. More than the specific issue or need addressed by a policy, being attuned to structural reforms means paying attention to how a change gives grassroots forces greater room to maneuver and reach for more in the future.


For social movements, structural reforms are a key mechanism of

inside-outside politics

, through which grassroots organizations work to elect champions into office who then, in turn, use the power of government to strengthen democratic participation and boost outside campaigns for social justice. Unfortunately, the right often has a better understanding of this process than liberals do.


A dramatic example of how Republicans used statewide governing power to alter the balance of forces was how Wisconsin Gov. Scott Walker, upon gaining a trifecta in 2010, sought to permanently kneecap unions. Recognizing the importance of …

title: Announcing Black Rose/Rosa Negra Locals in Austin, New York City, and Chicago
content:
We’re thrilled to announce the formation of three new Locals of Black Rose/Rosa Negra Anarchist Federation (BRRN)! From the Texas Hill Country, to the Great Lakes, to the Northeast, our organization is growing deeper roots and expanding our capacity to organize, struggle, and build popular power in communities across the country.


As you will read below, each new local grows out of its members’ deep involvement in the popular struggles of their neighborhoods, workplaces, and broader communities. What follows are brief introductions in their members’ own words — including their contact info and social media handles.


Austin, TX


The Austin Local has officially re-formed! Our members are primarily focused on labor and tenant organizing, as well as rapid response to ICE. We are also making preparations for an open reading group to discuss

BRRN’s Program

.


We welcome those with interest to contact us.


Email:

 austin@blackrosefed.org

Instagram:


@blackrose_atx


Chicago, IL


The Chicago local is back! Our logo honors the Haymarket Martyrs Memorial — a symbol of the organizers who made anarchism a powerful current in immigrant and women workers’ struggles of their time, as well as the place we gathered for our first event all together as a local. 


We carry their memory with us alongside others as we work in the social movements where we are rooted. These include tenant struggles on the South and Northwest sides, as well as labor organizing in the Chicago Teachers Union. We look forward to deepening our connections with comrades in our movements and others through collective study and struggle.


Email:

 chicago@blackrosefed.org

Instagram:


@blackrose_chicago

 


New York City, NY


Members of the New York City Local organize with tenants, neighbors, youth, coworkers, and parents to build Black, Brown, and working-class popular power throughout the city. Sites of social insertion include the Astoria Tenant Union in Queens, anticarceral youth and parent programs in Manhattan, immigrant defense coalitions in Brooklyn, the American Association of University Professors, and more. True to BRRN’s internationalist character, we also organize within the Palestinian and Sudanese solidarity movements.


From the Young Lords to Occupy Wall Street, we recognize the integral role that revolutionaries in NYC have played in past freedom struggles and look forward to reviving organized anarchism in the especifista tradition across the five boroughs.

BRRN’s Program

 serves as a blueprint for renewed efforts to confront imperial and capitalist violence as anarchist militants living at the nexus of US empire and global capital .


Email:

 nyc@blackrosefed.org

Instagram:

 @blackrose_nyc


Are you organizing at your workplace, on your campus, or in your neighborhood? Looking for a political home in which you can strategize with others about how to build power, force concessions, and push our mass movements in a revolutionary direction?


Black Rose/Rosa Negra could be right for you.

 page and send us a membership inquiry!

author: Aaron Hemens, Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: smǝlqmíx Youth lead rally against greenlit Copper Mountain Mine expansion: ‘They don’t care that their decision makes us sick’
content:
smǝlqmíx Youth and members of the nmlqitkʷ (Similkameen River) Defenders stand together at a gathering that they led in Keremeos on Nov. 8, where they continued to voice their opposition to the nearby Copper Mountain Mine’s New Ingerbelle Expansion project. From left to right: Chase Dennis, Isaac Dennis, Madeline Terbasket, Meadow Arcand, Kirsten Lindley, and Coven Terbasket.

 Photo by Aaron Hemens


A group of smǝlqmíx (Similkameen) Youth are continuing calls to stop a controversial mine expansion project in their homelands after it was greenlit by the province earlier this year. 


Members of the nmlqitkʷ (Similkameen River) Defenders, a group of syilx smǝlqmíx Youth “fighting for the water,” hosted an event on Sunday in the town of Keremeos, speaking about

their “refusal”

 of the Copper Mountain Mine’s New Ingerbelle expansion.


More than 50 people of all ages and backgrounds were in attendance, with many displaying signs with messages that read “No to the Ingerbelle Mine Expansion.” 


After years of deliberating,

the “B.C.” government greenlit the New Ingerbelle expansion in February

, issuing Mines Act and Environmental Management Act permits. The open pit gold and copper mine is located near “Princeton” in smǝlqmíx territory, which is about an hour northwest of Keremeos.


There have been years-long concerns from syilx communities and advocates about the impact that the expansion of the mine and its already towering tailings dam will have on the Similkameen River,

which some worry

 could have “catastrophic impacts” on the valley. 


The expansion will see the mine’s existing 192-metre tailings dam — roughly equivalent in height to a 58-storey building — increased by an additional 87 metres,

according to the province’s Environmental Assessment Office (EAO)

.


While acknowledging that she was “angry” and “upset” to have to stand up for the water; the land; and all the beings that rely on them, nmlqitkʷ defender Meadow Arcand said on Sunday that the Indigenous Youth “have a responsibility to do this work.”


“What we’re really looking out for is these young ones, the sacred ones that are going to come after us. Like our ancestors did before us, like our Elders did before us, like the old people did before us,” said Arcand.


“We’re standing here so people can’t say that we didn’t.”


She extended this same responsibility to anyone benefitting from Okanagan waters and territories – not just syilx smǝlqmíx people.


“We need people to care about our relationships with all life: with the water, with each other, and with the future generations,” she said.


“What we do here now matters. What our ancestors did matters.”


More than 50 people gathered in Keremeos on Nov. 8 to stand in solidarity with nmlqitkʷ (Similkameen River) Defenders, a group of syilx smǝlqmíx Youth who are opposed to the nearby Copper Mountain Mine’s New Ingerbelle Expansion project.

Photo by Aaron Hemens


‘They don’t care that their decision makes us sick’


Older generations of the smǝlqmíx community also spoke on Sunday, denouncing the mine expansion and sharing their support for the Youth. The organizers left handouts to resources – such as their online

petition

 and

declaration

 – and other information bulletins on what’s happening with mining in their homelands.


They also brought with them the syilx Okanagan Nation’s

siwɬkʷ (Water) Declaration

.


The expansion project is set to see the century-old mining operation revive its old Ingerbelle open pit gold and copper mine site near the Similkameen River. The expansion will extend the mining’s operation until 2047, according to the province.


After the province greenlit the mine’s expansion project in February, leadership at both Upper and Lower Similkameen Indian Bands (USIB, LSIB)

denounced the government’s decision

, saying that “no consent” was given.


y̓ilmixʷm (Chief) kalʔlùpaɋʹn Keith Crow of LSIB told IndigiNews in 2022 that the Similkameen River is the lifeblood of the valley.


“If we lose that, we lose our identity. We lose who we are,” Crow said.


An aerial view of the Similkameen River, flowing through the town of Keremeos in smǝlqmíx homelands in December 2024.

Photo by Aaron Hemens


Meanwhile, the mine’s owner Hudbay Minerals

issued a statement

 saying it “proactively engaged” with USIB and LSIB throughout the permitting process, and “finalized refreshed participation agreements” with both communities — “reinforcing the company’s commitment to …

author: Roderick Long
title: C4SS Panelists on the Intellectual Legacy of Don Lavoie
content:
There will be a Molinari/C4SS presence at the 10th annual PPE Society meeting, 12-14 November 2026, at the Westin New Orleans (100 Iberville St.).


I’ve organised a panel on “The Intellectual Legacy of Don Lavoie.” We’re in the very first session of the conference: Thursday, 12 November 2026, 9:00-10:30 a.m. (Central time) in River Room II.


The panel features Cory Massimino (C4SS) on “National Economic Planning: What is Right?” and Nathan Goodman (Mercatus; co-authoring with Molly Rovinski and Karla Segovia) on “Immigration Restrictions as Non-Comprehensive Planning.” Zak Woodman was also scheduled to speak at the panel, on “Ratcheting Up State Power: The Knowledge Problem, the Power Problem, and Legibility,” but will probably not be able to make it.


(This is not to be confused with the panel on the same topic at last month’s Mercatus Markets & Society conference, organised by Nathan Goodman and featuring Jason Byas, Akiva Malamet, and again Cory Massimino.)


Jason Byas, currently in his first year as Assistant Professor in Philosophy and Political Economy at Tulane, is also on the program; he’ll be speaking in a panel on “Anarchism as a Practical Philosophy,” Friday, 13 November 2026, 9:00-10:30 a.m. (Central time) in the Salon Room. Jason’s fellow panelists are Jesse Spafford, Jessica Flanigan, and Billy Christmas.

author: Valerie Anne
title: You Oughta Know That Alanis Morissette Is Pansexual
content:
feature image photo by Credit: NBC / Contributor via Getty Images

It’s official: 90s icon and present-day superstar Alanis Morissette is pansexual. The singer was a guest on the Handsome podcast, which is co-hosted by queer comedians Tig Notaro, Fortune Feimster, and Mae Martin, and they were talking about Alanis’s penchant for a post-breakup rage anthem. Fortune Feimster jokingly asked her, “Did it make you want to be a lesbian at any point?” to which Alanis replied, “I’m pansexual, so yeah.”

The energy in the room was perfect. At first, everyone thought it was a joke (or perhaps that she was being…ironic), but when they clarified that Alanis was serious, they all joked that she should have led with that. You walk into a queer podcast with the queer announcement!!

Granted, this is not the first time Alanis has said she isn’t straight. She has been talking about exploring her sexuality and being attracted to women as far back as 2008, and it was apparently at least partly her idea for her character to kiss Sarah Jessica Parker’s Carrie during her Sex and the City guest spot. It’s just the first time she’s used a specific label out loud.

I considered riddling this intro with Alanis-related puns (like the joke my friend made: she’s got one pan in her pocket…) but I’ll save you the cringe. I’ll just say this news has made me even more head over feet for her.

God is a woman, and she’s also pansexual.

You Live, You Learn (About More Gay News)

Cara Delevingne sent Reneé Rapp for a loop during a prank call in an Elle interview.

Speaking of Cara Delevingne, she also was at the red carpet premiere of Club Kid talking about the movie and also the “blue tsunami” in the midterm elections.

Beanie Feldstein and her wife welcomed a baby girl into their family (Beanie already made the “beanie baby” joke so I will refrain).

Amber Glenn took the lead in her Dancing with the Stars number on Disney night, dressed in shiny white pants, flexing her impressive-as-hell back muscles, and doing the quickstep to A Star is Born from Hercules.

Queer Swedish pop star Tove Styrke returns to music after having a baby with her partner Sanna Sikborn Erixon.

Cynthia Nixon was asked who her favorite lesbian is and she said Sappho (and also gave almost-definitely-bisexual Eleanor Roosevelt a shout-out).

The wait is almost over: Netflix’s The Body drops on Wednesday, November 11.

Queer Canadian icon Jann Arden is among the recognizable names on the guest star list for Jared Keeso’s upcoming comedy I Kill the Bear, alongside other queer-adjacent faves like Melanie Scrofano, Michelle Mylett, and Tricia Helfer.

ICYMI, WNBA players Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers have actually been broken up for quite a while, but don’t worry, they’re still friends.

author: By Clint Combs, Contributor
title: ICE Agent Falsely Accused Federal Defender of Helping Client Evade Arrest and Deportation
content:
Minneapolis, MN — It was supposed to be another routine court appearance.


Assistant Federal Defender Michael Deates and his Salvadoran client settled inside the Minneapolis courtroom on April 28. ICE Deportation Officer Michael O’Neal sat inside the gallery when he heard a familiar name: Ezequiel Portillo-Rodriguez.


He pulled out his government phone and then searched for the name. A Certificate of Nonexistence (CTNE) that he filed in April 2025 popped up. To O’Neal, this meant that there were no official records of Portillo-Rodriguez ever holding a visa, green card or U.S. citizenship. He texted agent Blake Willwerscheid, asking if he knew about the case. Willwersheid told him that Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Special Agent Brubaker was in charge of the case. A prosecutor later testified that this HSI Agent thought he was talking to an agent Witt in St. Paul.


Had O’Neal looked through court records he would have found something more relevant than a CTNE. On Sept. 2, 2025, Portillo-Rodriguez started his six-month stint inside the notorious Golden State Annex in McFarland, Ca. He filed an asylum claim while inside the private immigration jail run by GEO Group. Attorneys wrote that Portillo-Rodriguez had a “fear of persecution and torture” if he were deported back to El Salvador. Two weeks later an asylum officer denied this claim.


An immigration judge overturned that denial on November 7, 2025, finding his fears credible.


Portillo-Rodriguez filed a habeas corpus petition on Jan. 26, 2026. His attorney Deborah Czuba filed an emergency motion for a temporary restraining order on March 12. Four days later the government decided not to contest the review.


In California, U.S. District Judge Dale Drozd declared that the government had violated Portillo-Rodriguez’s Fifth Amendment Due Process rights by subjecting him to indefinite detention without a proper hearing.


On March 18, Judge Drozd issued an injunction releasing Portillo-Rodriguez and barring ICE from re-arresting him on immigration charges.


A month later, O’Neal was texting his boss, Supervisory Detention and Deportation Officer Nicholas Carey, looking for a green light to arrest Portillo-Rodriguez. He got no response while court was in session. Once the hearing adjourned, O’Neal cornered the prosecuting attorneys, asking if this was a case where Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) was barred from placing a detainer. The prosecutors told him they didn’t know.


O’Neal then approached U.S. Deputy Marshal Cassandra Stone, telling her he planned to take Portillo-Rodriguez into custody. Stone told him an arrest could be made at the U.S. Probation and Pretrial Services office. O’Neal claimed that Deates was standing close enough to eavesdrop.


“Deates was listening to the conversation I was having with Deputy Marshal Stone, made eye contact with me, then told his client Portillo-Rodriguez they needed to leave and follow him downstairs,” O’Neal wrote.


Deates denied this in his sworn declaration.


“I did not overhear, and had no knowledge at the time of, any conversation,” he wrote.


Deates and Portillo-Rodriguez walked downstairs to eat lunch at the Federal Defender’s Office. O’Neal rushed to the courthouse cellblock. He called Carey, demanding an immediate administrative warrant. Minutes later, Carey emailed a signed Form I-200 straight to O’Neal’s inbox.


The plainclothes task force scrambled to spring a familiar trap. O’Neal left the courtroom with Deputy Marshals Cassandra Stone and Gnika. Stone went to the Marshals Office to scan the live security video feeds, spotting Deates and his client in the public lobby.


By the time O’Neal and the marshals rushed down to the ground floor, the lobby was empty. The marshals searched the interior corridors while O’Neal glanced out a window. He caught sight of the pair walking along the sidewalk next to Minneapolis City Hall toward the light rail platform.


The three rushed outside before a red light stopped them at the intersection of 3rd Avenue and 4th Street. The light turned green. Trains departed in both directions. O’Neal saw Deates standing alone on the light rail platform. Portillo-Rodriguez was on his way back home to California.


After the failed trap, O’Neal contacted Special Agent Brubaker for an update. Brubaker informed him that Portillo-Rodriguez had been released in California on a habeas corpus petition.


The next day O’Neal sent a memo to Assistant ICE Field Officer …

author: Victoria Valenzuela
title: Incarcerated Los Angeles Youth Fought for the Right to Hug Their Parents — and Won
content:
This story was co-published with


Truthout

.


Mercedes Maradiaga sat across from her 19-year-old son in the Los Padrinos Juvenile Hall in Los Angeles in complete devastation. Her son had at that point been incarcerated at the prison for two years and she had visited him every weekend. But that day in September 2024 was especially hard because it was their first visit since he had been beaten by officers earlier that week in a space in the jail where there were no cameras. The guards had jumped on and kicked him, and he needed surgery for a torn ACL. All she wanted was to give him a hug and reassure him that she was there. However, because of the no-contact visit policies at Los Padrinos, she was unable to give him that comfort.


Even during birthdays and holidays, they weren’t allowed to embrace. The boy endured the jail’s horrible living conditions — including rat infestations and flooded toilets — but couldn’t hug his mom for a moment of escape.


“I couldn’t even let him know I’m here just with the little hug,” Maradiaga said. “It would have meant everything to him. It was sad, and I did that for four years.”


Los Padrinos had

reopened a year earlier

 in 2023, after being shut down in 2019 due to conditions that violated the Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC) standards, including abuses by staff. Six officers were criminally charged with

assault and child abuse

 for using pepper spray on several teenage girls. Reports

also cited a decreasing youth population

 as a factor for closure, yet staff

claimed to feel “outnumbered.”

 When Los Padrinos closed, youth were shuffled to another facility called Central Juvenile Hall — and then in 2023, that facility was closed down due to similar issues. Los Padrinos reopened, and just months later, the abuses restarted. In 2025,

30 officers were criminally charged

 by the California Attorney General with child endangerment and abuse, conspiracy, and battery for encouraging “gladiator fights” that pit youth against each other.


Olivia Shields, a justice transformation policy coordinator at Urban Peace Institute, described the constant closing and reopening of BSCC facilities as a “cycle of noncompliance.” Shields said the Los Angeles County Probation Department has ultimately failed with these maneuvers to address the core issue: unmet youth needs — which won’t be addressed through incarceration but through coordinated care in the form of individualized, robust support systems and resources.


“Rather than decarcerate these populations of young people and find community-based alternatives or step-downs for as many of them as possible, they basically shift the youth around from facility to facility to avoid noncompliance,” Shields said.


Long before the closing of Los Padrinos in 2019, the facility had a bad reputation among Angelenos. Maradiaga recalled hearing disturbing stories about the facility in the ’80s when she was a kid.


“I think it needs to be shut down,” Maradiaga said. “I think that there needs to be a better way for the youth. I don’t think locking them away from their family is the answer.”


The Appeal in Your Inbox


Subscribe to our newsletters for regular updates, analysis and context straight to your email.


          Sign Up


Barred From Basic Human Contact


When Ilana Parach, executive director and co-founder of

Hoops 4 Justice

, went inside Los Padrinos with a basketball and mentorship program, she quickly learned about what youth were facing inside. She felt it was important to give them a platform to express their needs directly, so she pivoted to working with them on legislation.


“They made a list of specific programs they wanted — resources for their families, reentry support,” Parach said. “At the bottom of that list, they wrote, ‘We want to hug our moms.’”


Incarcerated youth directly told her that one parent who hugged her son during a visit on his birthday then had her visit terminated and future visits suspended for two weeks. She said another youth was incarcerated for three years and had no choice but to watch his mother cry during the visits because she couldn’t hug him.


Contact visitation policies vary across California and are often left at the discretion of correctional officers. Parach said youth and staff both told her that Los Padrinos stopped allowing contact visits after the pandemic. Parach said that during meetings of the board of supervisors, she heard officers citing staffing shortages …

title: In the Crosshairs of the Far-Right Advance : An Update on Anti-Fascists and Anarchists in Greece
content:
Anarchist graffiti from Athens, Greece (2026)


The anarchist movement in Greece faces a new wave of repression. Urged on by the US and its obsession with combatting “far-left extremism,” the Greek state has targeted anti-authoritarians with new legal charges and attacked demonstrations, while fascists carry out street attacks and plot their return to the halls of power. Amidst a landscape of ongoing austerity, terrorism designations, lethal prisons, and ferocious wildfires, anarchists nonetheless continue to forge a combative culture of revolutionary solidarity.


In this article, we present an interview with an anarchist comrade in Athens assessing the current situation among anarchists and anti-fascists in Greece, along with analysis of the US’s role in advancing state repression and fantasies of Western supremacy.


The US and Greece: A Right-Wing Alliance to Defend “The West”


Earlier this month, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered a speech at the Pnyx in Athens. With the historic Acropolis and the Parthenon—that ancient symbol of Western democracy, constructed with slave labor—in the background, he delivered a warning message to Greece’s political and business elite.


“The course we take will determine whether the West maintains its place at the head of the world or resigns itself to a future of atrophy and servitude and decline,” Rubio cautioned. “We will either choose to act now or lose the choice to act at all.” Lamenting how “nationalism became a dirty word,” he called for renewed militarism, praised Christian faith and martyrdom, and announced a new counterterrorism information-sharing program between the two countries. His statements were calculated to reinforce the colonial legacy of Western dominance over the rest of the world, while urging the worst of Greek society to imitate America’s current political trajectory.


US Secretary of State Marco Rubio constructs an elaborate photo op for his defense of nationalism, militarism, and “the West” (October 7, 2026).


The speech came in the wake of a conference Rubio convened in July that aimed to coordinate intensified repression against “far-left extremism.” The following month, the US government imposed a “global terrorist” designation on the Italy-based

Autistici/Inventati (A/I) tech collective

, which operated the free publishing platform NoBlogs.org.


Greece’s right-wing politicians and business leaders benefiting from the country’s endless austerity measures are heeding Rubio’s call to preserve the hubris of the so-called West. Meanwhile, governments are collaborating to escalate repression against any truly revolutionary movements that challenge the world’s current status quo.


Greece’s strategic importance to Western powers is rooted in its symbolic status as the birthplace of “Western Civilization,” as well as its strategic location in the world today. The country offers the US access to four military sites, including a dedicated Navy base in Crete’s Souda Bay. Those with a longer memory have not forgotten how the US supplied napalm to Greece’s fascist forces, who worked with the Nazis during World War II and later with the British and US in a Cold War anti-communist alliance. Fascists dropped American napalm on Greek partisan resistance fighters during the civil war from 1946 to 1949, scorching bodies and charring forests, leaving the countryside scarred to this day.


More recently, the Greek people were pummeled by the 2008 global economic crisis, brought on in part by Wall Street firms such as Goldman Sachs that raked in immense profits while destabilizing the world’s economy and immiserating millions. The US then contributed to the austerity measures imposed on Greece in 2010 by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), leading to years of ferocious resistance to neoliberal capitalism and government complicity.


Today, Greece’s current New Democracy regime upholds

the legacy of the brutal military junta

 of 1967-1974, promoting the image of Greece as a symbol European supremacy as invoked by Rubio. Despite its nationalist rhetoric, the government continues to lick the boots of the US, crushing opposition in the streets and enforcing a never-ending precarity on the majority of Greece’s increasingly exhausted and numb population.

author: Marcelo Oliveira
title: Suposta ligação com o crime organizado pode barrar posse de 10 candidatos em 2027
content:
O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) pode impedir que 10 candidatos eleitos nas últimas eleições e investigados por ligações com organizações criminosas, tomem posse no ano que vem. Entre eles, dois tiveram suas candidaturas impugnadas pelo Ministério Público Eleitoral (MPE) e depois deferidas pela Justiça Eleitoral de seus estados: o ex-prefeito de Embu das Artes (SP), Ney Santos (Republicanos), candidato a deputado federal, e

Márcio Canella

 (União), ex-prefeito Belford Roxo (RJ), que se candidatou a deputado estadual.


Outras seis candidaturas que conseguiram votos suficientes para se eleger, cinco no Rio de Janeiro e uma no Mato Grosso do Sul, foram impugnadas pelo MPE e indeferidas pela Justiça Eleitoral regional, porém, entraram com recurso no TSE e puderam concorrer “sub-judice”. Ou seja, disputaram as eleições sabendo que a Justiça Eleitoral poderia barrá-los a qualquer momento. Nos oito processos, o MPE sustenta no TSE que as candidaturas devem ser impugnadas definitivamente.


Os dois últimos casos em análise no TSE por supostas ligações com o crime organizado são dos deputados federais eleitos Antonio Rueda (União/RJ) e Márcio Rezende (PSD/RJ). Ambos tiveram os registros das candidaturas deferidos pelos Tribunais Regionais Eleitorais, porém eles foram questionados por terceiros no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral.


Em 2026, 42 candidatos, de 10 estados do país, foram impugnados pelo Ministério Público Eleitoral (MPE) por vínculo com organizações criminosas.

 Do total, 22 deles tiveram os registros barrados pela Justiça Eleitoral ou renunciaram.


Duas candidaturas que tiveram o indeferimento defendido pelo MPE no TSE por terem sido permitidas pela Justiça Eleitoral não conseguiram se eleger. Uma delas é de Cristiane Brasil (DC/RJ), filha do ex-deputado federal Roberto Jefferson, que tentou retornar à Câmara dos Deputados em 2026 e teve 237 votos. A outra candidatura tem seu processo em sigilo.


Ex-prefeitos recebem milhares de votos, mesmo com investigações


Dois casos emblemáticos envolvem os Tribunais Regionais Eleitorais de São Paulo e do Rio de Janeiro, que liberaram as candidaturas dos ex-prefeitos de Embu das Artes (SP), Ney Santos (Republicanos), e de Belford Roxo (RJ),

Márcio Canella

 (União), a deputado federal e deputado estadual, respectivamente.


Tanto Santos quanto Canella foram eleitos com centenas de milhares de votos e a Procuradoria Geral Eleitoral contesta no TSE a validação de ambas as candidaturas para impedir que eles assumam os cargos.


Canella, inclusive, está preso preventivamente desde 15 de outubro. O deputado estadual, que busca a reeleição, foi o segundo mais votado do Rio de Janeiro este ano, e recebeu quase 200 mil votos. Ele é investigado na Operação Unha e Carne, da Polícia Federal, por suspeita de integrar uma organização criminosa armada que utilizava uma rede de postos de combustíveis na Região Metropolitana do Rio de Janeiro para esquemas de lavagem de dinheiro, que teria movimentado bilhões de reais.


Na política, ele é apontado pelo MP Eleitoral como responsável por ter aberto as portas da prefeitura de Belford Roxo para a milícia “Somos Comunidade” que teria um acordo com o Comando Vermelho. Há uma investigação sobre supostos membros do grupo armado que foram nomeados para cargos na cidade. Em julho deste ano, ele foi preso com um fuzil em seu carro e disse que a arma pertencia a um PM que fazia sua segurança. Por causa da prisão com o armamento, sua pré-candidatura ao Senado, com apoio de Flávio Bolsonaro, naufragou e o político optou pela reeleição à Assembleia Legislativa do Rio de Janeiro (Alerj). Rogéria Bolsonaro, mãe de Flávio, seria suplente de Canella.


Mesmo com esses elementos, o TRE entendeu, por 6 votos a 1, que os elementos juntados pelo MP contra a candidatura de Canella e sobre suas relações com as milícias não eram robustos o suficiente e deferiu o registro. A decisão foi proferida em 29 de setembro, duas semanas antes do ex-prefeito ser preso novamente.


Postos de combustíveis, também, seriam o principal meio empregado por

Ney Santos

, segundo o MP Estadual e o MP Eleitoral de São Paulo, para lavar dinheiro de crimes do PCC. Santos, que já esteve preso por roubo a carro forte, foi prefeito de Embu das Artes por dois mandatos entre 2017 e 2024. Há anos suas atividades são investigadas pelo Ministério Público.

author: Rizomatica
title: Sobre la propuesta de modificación al artículo 13 de la ley indigena 19.253
content:
La propuesta de modificación al artículo 13 de la ley 19.253 impulsada en el gobierno anterior a través de la denominada Comisión para la Paz y Entendimiento, fue una iniciativa transversal de la clase Política que incluyó a personeros de todo el espectro político Chileno como propuesta para el desarrollo en materia indígena.


Está propuesta ha sido fomentada por el actual gobierno de tinte ultraderechista con la finalidad de instalarla cómo política pública para el pueblo mapuche. Prueba de ello es que hace pocos días se reunieron en Temuco diversos personeros del gobierno con la finalidad de promover una consulta para dar implementación a esta medida.


El artículo 13 de la ley 19.253 es la normativa que regula y contiene restricciones respecto del dominio y uso de los terrenos indígenas. Este artículo contiene una protección exigida por el interés nacional del cual son sujetos los terrenos indígenas que impide que estos sean sometidos a enajenaciones, embargos, gravámenes, ni ser adquiridas por prescripción, salvo entre comunidades o personas de una misma etnia.


En términos generales, hasta ahora, el artículo 13 ha sido una salvaguarda para el dominio de la tierra indígena en manos de los pueblos originarios, por cuánto la ley en este aspecto tiene un carácter imperativo y obligatorio de protección.


No obstante aquello, esto no ha significado una protección completa ya que a través de diversos artilugios legales se han registrado casos en que a pesar de sus diversas prohibiciones, si se ha logrado enajenar (

vender

) terrenos indígenas a personas no mapuche. Esto ha sido en virtud de vacíos contenidos en la normativa que dejan espacios a artilugios legales que diversos abogados han utilizado para realizar esas ventas en vulneración al espíritu de la ley.


Un caso emblemático a este respecto fue el mediático caso de la venta realizada por la viuda chilena de un mapuche después de su muerte en la comuna de Pucón al ex subsecretario Ubilla durante el gobierno del expresidente Piñera.


Está venta de un terreno indígena a un chileno dejó de manifiesto lo frágil de la ley respecto de la real protección a los terrenos indígenas cuando hay intereses económicos importantes de por medio. Esta venta se pudo realizar en el contexto de lo que en derecho civil se conoce como liquidación de una sociedad conyugal y adjudicación por disolución de esta.


Volviendo a la propuesta de modificación al artículo 13, lo que preocupa es el aparente sentido inocuo de dicha medida, ya que directamente no habla de

enajenación

 o

venta

 de un terreno indígena a una persona o entidad no mapuche, sino que el énfasis ha sido puesto en la posibilidad de

arrendamiento

 de un terreno indígena a personas

no indígenas

 o

personas


jurídicas

 de diversa índole.


Está situación es más compleja de lo que parece a simple vista porque abre una posibilidad de vulneraciones difíciles de prever a futuro.


Lo que señala la propuesta de modificación es que los terrenos indígenas podrán ser arrendados a cualquier persona no indígena o persona jurídica por un plazo de hasta 10 años y 25 años con consulta al órgano técnico encargado en materia indígena que es la Conadi.


El argumento para esto, es que en las condiciones actuales de restricción que contiene la propiedad indígena ha sido muy difícil incorporar estos terrenos a los beneficios que contempla la ley y a diversas medidas administrativas de los órganos y servicios del Estado en materia de fomento productivo, acceso a vivienda, acceso a crédito, transferencia tecnológica y oportunidades de desarrollo en general. En la visión de los promotores de esta iniciativa se sostiene que esto ha sido el principal elemento de tope que han tenido los mapuche para hacer productivas sus tierras e incorporarlas eficientemente al circuito productivo de la economía local y regional.


Para ello se propone bajar el nivel de restricciones que contiene la ley en materia de protección y permitir arriendos en condiciones de mercado actuales y competitivos.


Esto en teoría significaría regular de forma más eficiente situaciones de arriendo irregular que hoy pudiesen existir y por otra parte mejorar los promedios de los valores de los precios de arriendo para el arrendador y conceder garantías tanto de tiempo como de condiciones jurídicas que permitan al arrendatario realizar una labor productiva con seguridad en un tiempo acorde a dicha inversión, pudiendo ser por un lapso de hasta 25 años.

title: Enzo Traverso: “La revuelta juvenil tiene una dimensión política evidente”

Enzo Traverso: “La revuelta juvenil tiene una dimensión política evidente”


Enzo Traverso

 


06/11/2026


En “Supervivencias de la revuelta”, el historiador pone de relieve la “vida póstuma” de las experiencias emancipadoras, a contracorriente de los relatos nacionales. En una entrevista con Mathieu Dejean para Mediapart, descifra los vínculos subterráneos que unen esta memoria rebelde y el movimiento social actual.


Contra la despolitización y la anestesia del pasado, el historiador Enzo Traverso, profesor de la Universidad de Cornell (Ithaca, Nueva York), revive las memorias rebeldes. Después de 

La melancolía de izquierda 

(2016) y 

Revolución 

(2022), su nuevo libro, 

Supervivencias de la revuelta. Ensayo sobre la dialéctica de la memoria 

(2026) -en francés en las ediciones La Découverte- cierra esta trilogía advirtiendo a los ciudadanos contra las políticas de memoria regidas por las instituciones e invitándolos a apropiarse de la tradición de los oprimidos.


“Esta memoria de las revueltas es subterránea, discreta, pero surge de forma imprevista”, 

escribe. El 17 de octubre de 2026 es una demostración de ello: varias capas de memorias rebeldes se entrecruzaron, desde el 17 de octubre de 1961 en la Comuna de París en 1871. Vuelve, en una entrevista con 

Mediapart

, sobre lo que el movimiento social actual lleva de recuerdos y sobre sus potencialidades, a pesar de la incertidumbre, para finalmente 

“dejar la época contemporánea”.


“Mediapart”: Un alto funcionario de la policía dijo, sobre el 

17 de octubre

: “Era la Comuna de París el día del Black Friday. ¿No es la memoria anti Comuna la que se manifiesta con fuerza desde esa fecha?


Enzo Traverso: 

Hay algo asombroso en la posteridad de la Comuna de París, que tiene tanto el estatus de paradigma para las memorias rebeldes -resurge constantemente, no solo en Francia, sino a escala global- como para el pensamiento reaccionario. Ha proporcionado un repertorio de figuras, referencias, símbolos, imágenes en la cultura reaccionaria, que se ha reactivado constantemente durante un siglo y medio.


De hecho, este es el caso desde el 17 de octubre, no solo en Francia sino también en Italia, donde se invocan los mismos motivos -la civilización amenazada por la barbarie, los salvajes que se apoderan de los centros de las ciudades-, con una dimensión xenófoba y racista particularmente importante. La juventud de los suburbios postcoloniales actúa como un nuevo chivo expiatorio. Un imaginario reaccionario global está tomando forma.


¿Cuáles son las referencias adoptadas precisamente de la memoria anti Comuna?


Si pensamos en la literatura anti Comuna, Théophile Gautier calificó a los protagonistas de la Comuna de París de 

“bestias”, 

“animales apestosos” 

y 

“venenosos” 

escapadas de un zoológico, que hacen estragos en la ciudad porque el guardián se olvidó de cerrar la jaula. Son los mismos clichés que se propagan hoy.


Una gran figura del pensamiento reaccionario de la época, Alphonse Daudet, dijo al día siguiente de la Comuna: 

«¡París estaba en manos de los negros!

 Es una racialización y una animalización de la revuelta y los rebeldes que, en una continuidad asombrosa, perduran hasta nuestros días.


En ambos casos, podemos destacar la negativa de los gobernantes -en este caso Emmanuel Macron, Sébastien Lecornu y Laurent Nuñez- a 

cuestionar las causas sociales y políticas de la revuelta

. Como en la Comuna de París, la revuelta es para ellos un fenómeno mucho más biológico que social. Lo que explica la revuelta es la naturaleza racial o religiosa de los rebeldes, aunque muchos jóvenes blancos fueron muy activos el 17 de octubre. En su imaginación, hay que ver al rebelde como un cuerpo ajeno a la nación.


En términos más generales, parece que el pueblo ha permanecido, en la mente de las élites gobernantes, una “multitud vil”, como dijo Adolphe Thiers.


Esta es una observación interesante, porque lo que también llama la atención es el relativo silencio de la extrema derecha, que a menudo se califica de “populista”. A menudo ha reivindicado la ira legítima de las clases populares contra el 

establishment

, del pueblo virtuoso contra las élites corruptas. Pero a diferencia de 2017 y 2022, Emmanuel Macron se encuentra en tal estado de derrota que Rassemblement national (RN) se ha ganado la confianza de las élites dominantes, de las que se ha …

title: Los testimonios que la Iglesia no escuchó: víctimas del Opus Dei y Próvolo reclaman justicia y una respuesta del papa León XIV
content:
Mónica Zambrano (i), Claudia Carrero (c), y Tita Villamayor participan durante la primera cumbre internacional de ECA (Ending Clergy Abuse) sobre ‘Los Abusos del Opus Dei en Argentina’, en Buenos Aires (Argentina). Imagen: archivo EFE/ Matías Martin Campaya.


Este martes 10 de noviembre, a las 15, se realizará en Buenos Aires una conferencia de prensa de Ending Clergy Abuse (ECA) para llevarle un mensaje al Papa León XIV ante la falta de respuesta a las 43 mujeres que denunciaron haber sido sometidas a explotación por el Opus Dei y a los sobrevivientes de abuso sexual del Instituto Próvolo. La convocatoria fue difundida por la periodista y escritora Paula Bistagnino, quien sigue el caso de las 43 mujeres y publicó un libro sobre sus denuncias. La presentación estará encabezada por las autoridades de ECA.

La actividad se produce luego de que el Pontífice mantuviera un encuentro con cinco víctimas de abusos cometidos por integrantes del clero y de instituciones eclesiásticas, seleccionadas por la Iglesia local. Entre quienes no fueron recibidas se encuentran las mujeres denunciantes del Opus Dei y sobrevivientes del Próvolo. ECA cuestionó que la jerarquía eclesiástica argentina haya quedado a cargo de decidir quiénes podían acceder a esa reunión y reclamó transparencia, reconocimiento y reparación. Por ANRed.


“

Hoy a las 15 en Buenos Aires habrá una conferencia de prensa para dar un mensaje al Papa León XIV ante la falta de respuesta a las mujeres sometidas por el Opus Dei y a los chicos y chicas del Instituto Próvolo

. Estará encabezada por las autoridades de Ending Clergy Abuse (ECA)”. Así lo anunció la periodista

Paula Bistagnino

, quien investigó y publicó sobre las denuncias de 43 mujeres que acusaron al Opus Dei de trata de personas y explotación laboral.


 


Ver esta publicación en Instagram


 


Una publicación compartida por Agencia de Noticias Red Acción (@anredaccion)


La convocatoria se produce después de que

León XIV mantuviera un encuentro privado con cinco personas víctimas de abusos cometidos por integrantes del clero y de instituciones eclesiásticas del país

. Según informó la Oficina de Prensa de la Santa Sede, las cinco personas fueron presentadas por la Iglesia local y el encuentro duró más de una hora. Sin embargo,

entre quienes no fueron recibidas se encuentran las 43 mujeres que denunciaron al Opus Dei y los sobrevivientes del Instituto Próvolo

. La noticia generó cuestionamientos por parte de organizaciones que reclamaban una audiencia para trasladarle al Pontífice sus denuncias y demandas.


Desde ECA cuestionaron que la selección de las personas que accedieron al encuentro haya quedado en manos de las autoridades eclesiásticas argentinas, sin que se informaran los criterios utilizados ni los casos a los que pertenecían las víctimas recibidas. “Respetamos profundamente a las cinco personas y lo que cada una de ellas fue a decirle.

Nuestro reclamo es con un mecanismo que dejó en manos de la jerarquía eclesiástica argentina la decisión de a quién escucha el Papa. Esa jerarquía es justamente la institución cuya respuesta frente a los abusos está en discusión

”, expresó

Sergio Salinas Giordano

, abogado de víctimas del Próvolo y director de ECA Global. También sostuvo: “

Un comunicado así no genera esperanza en la Iglesia: genera desconfianza

”.


El testimonio de las mujeres que sufrieron la servidumbre del Opus Dei


Uno de los casos que estará en el centro de la conferencia es el de las

43 mujeres que denunciaron haber sido captadas durante su infancia o adolescencia por el Opus Dei y sometidas a explotación laboral

. Según sus testimonios,

fueron incorporadas bajo promesas de educación, alojamiento y formación, pero terminaron realizando durante años tareas domésticas sin remuneración, con jornadas extensas, restricciones a su libertad y situaciones de encierro y violencia psicológica

. En septiembre de 2024 presentaron una denuncia formal ante la Justicia argentina. La Procuraduría de Trata y Explotación de Personas (PROTEX) impulsó medidas judiciales contra integrantes de la organización por presunta trata de personas y explotación laboral.

El Opus Dei niega las acusaciones

.


También reclamarán por

los niños y niñas que sufrieron abusos sexuales en el Instituto Antonio Próvolo de Mendoza

. Las víctimas eran personas sordas e hipoacúsicas que asistían al establecimiento religioso de Carrodilla, en Luján de Cuyo.

author: Darío Aranda
title: Día de la Maestra y el Maestro Rural: sembrar el derecho a la educación en cerros, llanuras y bosques
content:
Por Marcela Isaías


El primer día de su trabajo Leila quedó largas horas empantanada en el camino hacia la escuela. Ese fue su bautismo como maestra rural en el norte santafesino. Sandra enseña arte en secundarias rurales de Entre Ríos; todo el tiempo denuncia el mal estado de las rutas y la fumigación de los campos con agrotóxicos. El femicidio de la directora correntina Nancy Godoy le llegó muy de cerca. Adolfo da clases en un pueblo jujeño cercano a La Quiaca, en sus tareas diarias incluye la huerta escolar como un espacio de encuentro con las familias.


Ni heroínas ni apóstoles. Historias que hablan de cómo trabajan maestras y maestros rurales para garantizar el derecho a la educación.


Norte de Santa Fe


Leila Díaz vive en Tostado, cabecera del departamento 9 de Julio, bien al norte de la provincia de Santa Fe. Desde el año pasado es maestra reemplazante, siempre en la ruralidad. Su primera suplencia la hizo en una escuela rural ubicada a unos 44 kilómetros de Tostado. Una buena parte del trayecto hasta ese establecimiento es por un camino de tierra, y sí o sí lo tiene que hacer en un vehículo propio. “La primera vez que fui me llevó mi papá. Hacía dos días había llovido y en el primer charco nos quedamos”, repasa ese recuerdo que atesora.


Con ella viajaba la cocinera de la escuela. Llevaban las provisiones de comida para la semana, la garrafa, agua, además de los materiales y útiles para las clases. Debieron caminar varios kilómetros hasta el cruce con la ruta para buscar ayuda.


Leila había soñado con ese primer día de trabajo como maestra, “nunca con algo parecido” a lo que pasó. Igual siguió adelante y se enamoró de la enseñanza rural: “Lo maravilloso fue cuando llegamos a la escuela, conectamos el wi-fiy mandé un mensaje al grupo de las familias para que sepan que iba a haber clases. A los dos o tres minutos empezaron a llegar todos los niños y las niñas. Ahí entendí lo importantes que somos”.


Foto: Gentileza Leila Díaz


Vivir la semana en el lugar donde enseña es parte de su trabajo. Por lo general, quienes permanecen en estas experiencias son la docente, que hace también tareas de dirección al ser personal único, la portera o cocinera y la maestra de nivel inicial. “Las tres solitas en el medio de la nada”, dice recordando una noche de tormenta en la que además se cortó la luz.


Leila se explaya en la charla sobre su vida familiar, su hija pequeña, su marido. Del intercambio que tiene con sus alumnas y alumnos, que enriquecen la experiencia pedagógica y remiten al legado freiriano: “Siento que me escuchan, que se llevan algo de mí, como yo me llevo de ellos, porque siempre me están enseñando”.


En ese ir y venir de relatos, reconoce que no puede dejar de pensar en lo que le pasó a Nancy Godoy, la docente correntina víctima de un atroz femicidio. “Pude haber sido yo o cualquiera de mis compañeras. Todas nos sentimos identificadas con ella”, comenta ese sentimiento de espanto colectivo.


“Después de lo que pasó con Nancy —continúa— te preguntás hasta qué punto te podés exponer. Más cuando, en Santa Fe, un reemplazo lo cobrás a los 60 días”.


Las condiciones laborales, en particular la movilidad, se vuelve un tema ineludible, atraviesa todo el tiempo la conversación con quienes ejercen en la ruralidad. Si hay que hacer dedo “siempre tratamos de ser dos o más, ir en grupo”. Pide más empatía a quienes tienen a su cargo las escuelas y exigen llegar sí o sí a dar clases, “sin importar a costa de qué”.


Cierta vez viajaba en auto junto a otras maestras a dar clases a la localidad de Esteban Rams, a 77 kilómetros de Tostado. Por la imprudencia de otro conductor estuvieron a poco de un accidente: “Nos salvamos de milagro”. Es ineludible la mención a la tragedia del 27 de mayo de 2013, ocurrida en el norte santafesino y en la que perdieron la vida diez personas, entre ellas siete maestras. Pasaron más de diez años y el reclamo para que se atienda el traslado cuidadoso de la docencia rural sigue pendiente.


Daniela Spárvoli fue víctima de femicidio en 2003 - Foto: Amsafe Delegación Iriondo


Nancy y Daniela


El femicidio de Nancy Godoy puso en la agenda pública otra vez el trabajo de las docentes rurales. Nancy era de Esquina (Corrientes) y desde agosto pasado ejercía como directora suplente en la Escuela Rural N° 626, en el Paraje El Malezal. author: La Zarzamora
title: Lanzamiento de Black Onions, un listado de sitios web anarquistas y antiautoritarios con extensión .onion
content:
Publicado originalmente en Montréal Contre-information

Nos complace anunciar el lanzamiento de Black Onions, una nueva iniciativa que tiene como objetivo ofrecer una lista estable y actualizada periódicamente de sitios anarquistas y antiautoritarios con extensión .onion. Los sitios .onion son sitios web accesibles a través del navegador Tor mediante direcciones que terminan en «.onion».

En los últimos meses, algunos gobiernos han atacado las infraestructuras de comunicación de nuestros movimientos con renovado vigor; buena prueba de ello son la conferencia internacional sobre el «terrorismo de extrema izquierda» celebrada en Estados Unidos en julio, así como la inclusión del proveedor de servicios de alojamiento militante italiano Autistici/Inventati en una lista de sanciones relacionadas con el terrorismo a finales de agosto.

Para bien o para mal, la comunicación pública de nuestros movimientos tiene lugar en gran medida en Internet, lo que la hace vulnerable a los mecanismos tecnológicos de censura. A diferencia de los sitios web convencionales, los sitios .onion son menos vulnerables a la censura, ya que no utilizan nombres de dominio y permiten ocultar la ubicación del servidor, del mismo modo que el navegador Tor oculta tu propia ubicación al visitar el sitio. Consideramos que los sitios .onion son nuestra mejor baza para seguir comunicándonos en línea dentro del movimiento anarquista, especialmente si los intentos de censura se intensifican en el futuro.

El problema recurrente de los sitios .onion es que sus direcciones, compuestas por 56 caracteres aleatorios, son imposibles de memorizar. Black Onions tiene como objetivo resolver este problema. Te recomendamos guardar en los marcadores del navegador Tor, o en un archivo en tu ordenador, las direcciones .onion que utilizas habitualmente; pero si necesitas una dirección que aún no has guardado, ¡encuéntrala en Black Onions!

Accede a Black Onions a través de cualquiera de las siguientes direcciones:

– blackonions.gd – blackonions.li – blackonions.st – (próximamente, una dirección .onion)

Para establecer una base de confianza en esta nueva iniciativa, los siguientes proyectos anarquistas han avalado nuestra propuesta mediante declaraciones firmadas con PGP: Act For Freedom Now!, un proyecto de contrainformación activo desde 2008 , y el No Trace Project, un proyecto contra la represión activo desde 2021.

¡Utiliza sitios .onion! ¡Resiste a la censura!

author: Agência Diadorim
title: Partido de Trump apostou milhões em propagandas anti trans nas eleições nos EUA — e perdeu
content:
O Partido Republicano dos Estados Unidos apostou — e muito — em campanhas contra os direitos das pessoas trans para tentar conquistar votos nas eleições de meio de mandato no país.

Até 25 de outubro, o partido do presidente Donald Trump havia investido 183 milhões de dólares em anúncios de televisão sobre questões trans, segundo levantamento da AdImpact divulgado pela Associated Press.

 Foram cerca de 217 mil veiculações em todo o país.


O investimento contrasta com as prioridades dos eleitores.

Segundo pesquisa AP-NORC, apenas um em cada dez eleitores registrados considera as questões trans prioritárias. Já oito em cada dez apontam a economia ou o custo de vida como assuntos importantes.


A baixa prioridade atribuída ao tema, porém, não significa que ele seja irrelevante na escolha dos candidatos. Pesquisa do The 19th/YouGov, realizada em setembro com 2.357 adultos, mostra que 45% dos entrevistados afirmam ter maior probabilidade de votar em um candidato favorável à proibição da participação de atletas trans em equipes esportivas femininas.


Por outro lado, na mesma pesquisa, 42% consideram que os políticos não deveriam se concentrar em questões relacionadas às pessoas trans. As opiniões também variam conforme o direito em discussão: 45% são contrários à proibição ou restrição de cuidados de afirmação de gênero para menores de idade, enquanto 38% apoiam essas medidas. Outros 51% acreditam que pessoas trans enfrentam muita discriminação nos Estados Unidos.


A estratégia republicana, utilizada por Donald Trump em 2024, também foi desenhada para pressionar os democratas.

 Segundo a Reuters, enquanto alguns candidatos tentam deslocar o debate para a economia, outros adotam posições mais conservadoras.


Como a

Agência Pública

 mostrou, a tática parece não ter funcionado. Em

entrevista

, a socióloga e cientista política Gisele Agnelli apontou que a promessa central que elegeu Donald Trump em 2024 — a

affordability

, ou recuperação do poder de compra — “não se materializou na percepção de grande parte dos eleitores. Os democratas exploraram essa frustração com uma campanha essencialmente pragmática, concentrada no custo da alimentação, da moradia, dos combustíveis e dos serviços de saúde”, avalia.


Partido republicano utilizou propaganda anti trans para tentar pressionar democratas e conseguir votos nas eleições dos EUA


Da campanha eleitoral às propostas de lei anti trans nos EUA


A mobilização em torno dos direitos trans não se limita à publicidade eleitoral.

No Congresso norte-americano, propostas buscam restringir a participação de meninas e mulheres trans em competições esportivas femininas, o uso de banheiros conforme a identidade de gênero e conteúdos escolares relacionados à transgeneridade.


Uma dessas propostas, o H.R. 28, foi aprovada pela Câmara dos Representantes em janeiro de 2025, mas não se tornou lei. Outras seguem em diferentes etapas de tramitação.


Esporte, educação e acesso a espaços públicos também estão entre os temas de projetos apresentados por parlamentares brasileiros, especialmente ligados ao campo conservador.


A ofensiva anti trans no Brasil


O Partido Liberal (PL), legenda da família Bolsonaro, é apontado pela

Observatória

 como o partido que mais apresenta projetos de lei anti-LGBTQIA+ no Brasil.


Nas eleições deste ano, a sigla elegeu 121 deputados federais e se consolidou como a maior bancada da Câmara. Entre os eleitos estão Nikolas Ferreira (MG) e Lucas Pavanato (SP), ambos com mais de 3 milhões de votos e conhecidos por seus recorrentes discursos transfóbicos.


Entre janeiro de 2019 e maio de 2026, a Observatória identificou, nas Assembleias Legislativas, 81 projetos de censura escolar, incluindo propostas contra a chamada “ideologia de gênero”.


Outros 70 projetos tratam do uso de banheiros, com restrições ao acesso conforme a identidade de gênero. Há ainda 40 propostas que buscam limitar a participação de atletas trans em competições esportivas.


Na área da saúde, foram identificados 39 projetos relacionados ao processo transexualizador, com restrições ao atendimento de menores de idade. Outros 17 tratam da definição de gênero nas políticas públicas.


Na Câmara dos Deputados, foram apresentados outros 20 projetos sobre atletas trans, 19 relacionados ao processo transexualizador, 18 sobre censura escolar, 13 sobre definição de gênero e 12 sobre banheiros.
