author: Rizomatica
title: Declaración publica Lof Pillumallin Autónomo y Coordinadora Arauco Malleco
content:
«Marimari pu peñi pu lamgen, a los lof en resistencia y a toda la gente consciente de la digna lucha mapuche. Cómo lof en recuperación Pillumallin autónomo y Coordinadora Arauco Malleco, venimos a expresar lo siguiente:


Kiñe: El día sábado 07 de noviembre del presente año, llevamos a cabo un txawun Palin, dónde asistieron diferentes comunidades de wallmapu, logrando así una jornada familiar llena de nutxam hacia nuestros ppm y nuestros lamgen caídos en el weichan, cómo también un gran palikantun en honor a ellos.


Epu: En nuestro txawün palin también reivindicamos a nuestro peñi/lamgen Álvaro Quinchanao Hueche yem, weichafe de nuestra organización a quien conocimos apoyando y acompañando en distintos procesos de recuperación territorial, incluyendo el nuestro, así como en distintas actividades propias de la militancia mapuche como siembras, construcción de ruka e instancias espirituales.


Hoy a casi 6 meses de su partida queremos reivindicar la figura de nuestro weichafe como una persona profundamente humana que brindó su vida para cuidar y aportar al proyecto de reconstrucción nacional tanto desde su rol como weichafe así como en su vida personal donde pudimos dar fé de su integridad, su feyentun y apego a los valores del mapuche gen. A pesar de que el winka quiera reducir su persona y su convicción política y espiritual a la imagen de terrorista.

Nuestro peñi/lamgen dejó una profunda huella por su compromiso y entrega a su pueblo, legado que nosotros continuaremos reivindicando en el weichan y en cada recuperación territorial, su memoria, entrega y vida no serán en vano, sino que vivirá en cada militante de la causa mapuche autónomista, tal como él lo eligió en su vida.


Küla: Que el segundo objetivo de nuestro txawun Palin era reivindicar y visibilizar la causa de nuestros peñi/ lamgen ppm Jorge Caniupil Coña, Juan Carlos Mardones Saez, Luis Menares Chanilao y Pelentaro Llaitul Pezoa, quienes están agrupados en la denominada Causa Lautaro, por la que recientemente el día 4 de Octubre recibimos la negativa respuesta del sistema judicial de la Nulidad de sentencia en la corte de Apelaciones de Temuco, ratificando así la condena de nuestros weichafe a 14 y 16 años de cárcel. Los cuales este 22 de noviembre cumplen ya 4 años secuestrados por el Estado de $hile.

De esta manera se puede demostrar como el poder judicial una vez más se ensaña con nuestros ppmcamche, con sus políticas racistas hacia nuestros weichafe.


Meli: Así también queremos demostrar nuestro descontento del actuar racista, discriminatorio y clara persecución política por parte de Gendarmería, el poder judicial y el estado $hileno hacia nuestro Peñi/ lamgen Lonko Daniel Canio. A quien una vez más se le han negado sus derechos como ppm, en este caso su correspondiente Libertad Condicional, nuestro Lonko lleva ya 11 años y medio cumplidos de su condena, tiempo más que suficiente para otorgarle el derecho a su salida y «Beneficios» cómo es la salida a un CET. Así queremos enviar newen a todos nuestros peñi/lamgen que resisten al estado que nos persigue, nos encarcela y mata por recuperar nuestro territorio, nuestro feyentun, kewün ka mogen.

Un abrazo fraterno a nuestros ppm camche, y a todos los lof en recuperación, a las reñma que resisten junto a sus pichikeche para que siga brotando nuestra semilla, para nuestros nuevos choyün. También para los seres queridos del weichafeyem Kincha.


Desde nuestro lof en recuperación le decimos con la frente en alto, que mientras existan Presos políticos mapuche, mientras el winka y el yanakona siga usufructuando con nuestra mapu, mientras exista despojo territorial, seguiremos luchando.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Angry farmers dump rotten vegetables at DA
content:
Vegetable farmers from the Cordillera dumped rotten vegetables at Department of Agriculture’s (DA) main office in Quezon City on Tuesday, protesting the agency’s failure to solve the worsening crisis faced by local food producers.


The protesters said plummeting farm gate prices and continuously rising costs of agricultural inputs have forced many farmers in the upland region to refuse farming or selling their produce at bottom level prices.


Farmers led by the Kanatengan Network, Apit Tako, the Cordillera Peoples Alliance (CPA), and KATRIBU are demanding fair floor prices, affordable agricultural inputs, sufficient subsidies, improved farm-to-market roads, measures against vegetable importation and smuggling, and an end to usurious lending and excessive land rental costs.


“The rotten vegetables thrown at the agency were the very same produce that farmers could no longer sell amid intensifying competition with imported vegetables, plummeting farm gate prices, and continuously rising costs of agricultural inputs,” KATRIBU in a statement said.


The Indigenous Peoples’ group said the agriculture department allowed local farmers struggling to recover production costs and earn a decent livelihood.


“Instead of strengthening domestic agricultural production through genuine agrarian reform, adequate government support, and the development of local industries, the Marcos Jr. administration continues to allow agricultural importation and smuggling to undermine Filipino farmers. Local producers are left competing with cheaper imported vegetables while receiving inadequate support to sustain their own production,” the group said.


On Tuesday, the Bureau of Customs announced a planned investigation of a P524.27 million worth of reportedly smuggled agricultural products found in a warehouse in Valenzuela City last October 17. Tons of red onions, beans and legumes, ginger and carrots, as well as peanut products were allowed to pass through customs inspection and were seized outside port premises.


While Cordillera farmers complain of diving farm gate prices, meanwhile, retail prices for their produce have risen in lowland wet markets.


The Philippine Statistics Authority reported the following selling prices in Mimaropa region this week:

title: Women’s vigil in Amed commemorates 14 victims of femicide and unexplained deaths
content:
Women gathered outside the courthouse in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) on Tuesday for the sixth time to protest against femicide, gender-based violence and the failure to adequately investigate suspicious deaths. The vigil, organized by the Network Against Violence, focused this week on the names and life stories of 14 women who were murdered between November 2 and 10. Numerous women joined the demonstration alongside representatives of political parties and civil society organizations.


Under a banner reading “Women Stand Vigil for Justice and Memory,” participants carried photographs of women who had been killed. Chants such as “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom), “Femicide is political” and “Bijî tekoşîna jinan” (Long live women’s struggle) echoed throughout the gathering. With the slogan “Do not protect, do not whitewash, prosecute,” they denounced impunity for violence against women.


Remembering 14 women and their life stories


Speaking on behalf of the network, Irem Ilhan of the Association for Solidarity from a Women’s Perspective (DAKAHDER) stated that women refused to allow the victims’ fates to be forgotten. She emphasized the need to insist on thorough investigations in a society where women’s deaths are frequently classified as suicides, accidents or unexplained incidents. She described the systematic threat to women’s lives as femicide.


The participants then read aloud the stories of 14 women, explicitly distinguishing between confirmed homicides and deaths whose causes have yet to be determined.


Among the victims was 33-year-old Şefika Yeşildağ, who was stabbed to death by her former husband, Osman Oruç, in Aksaray on November 2. The couple had been divorced for six years. According to her mother, the man had continued to harass Şefika. Nazmiye Özer, 56, was also killed by her former husband on November 7, six years after their divorce. Women’s organizations called for an investigation into possible previous threats and failures by state authorities responsible for providing protection.


Latife Mengüç, 50, was shot dead on November 5 by a man from whom she wanted to separate. The perpetrator subsequently took his own life.


Domestic violence


Particularly distressing was the case of Huriye Çiçek and her daughter Zeynep Demircan. The 50-year-old mother and her 25-year-old daughter were killed in an armed attack in early November, carried out by Huriye’s son, who was also Zeynep’s brother. An eleven-year-old girl was seriously injured in the attack.


Hülya Aktaş, 73, was stabbed to death by her son on November 6. Another of her sons was also killed in the same attack.


Citing these cases, women’s organizations emphasized that family ties offered no guarantee of protection against patriarchal violence and that violence within the family must not be treated as a private matter.


Other victims included 31-year-old Hilal Mete and 46-year-old Ayşe Sena Demir. Both were shot dead inside a vehicle on November 5. A suspect was arrested. Satı Aydoğmuş, 68, was also killed in an armed attack that claimed the life of another person.


Unexplained deaths must be investigated


In several of the cases presented, it has yet to be established whether the women were victims of violent crimes. Participants therefore demanded comprehensive forensic examinations and transparent investigations.


These cases include the death of 18-year-old Havva Büşra Kural, who was found dead alongside her father in an apartment on November 2. The circumstances surrounding the deaths of 44-year-old Melek Altun, Olessya Shudrina, also 44, and Melek Kaval, who were found dead in their apartments in early November, also remain unclear.


The vigil also commemorated an unidentified woman whose body was discovered on November 4 off the coast of Izmir, in the Bayraklı district. Women’s organizations called for her identity to be established and the cause of her death to be determined.


The vigil thus also drew attention to women whose deaths have not yet been confirmed as homicides but whose fates could remain unresolved without effective investigations.


“Justice is needed for all women”


After the names were read aloud, Irem Ilhan emphasized the responsibility of state institutions to protect women, saying: “When a woman is killed despite having reported violence, applied for protection or already been granted protective measures, not only the perpetrators but also any public officials who may bear responsibility must be …

author: groundxero
title: 544 Scientists and Researchers Stand with Siang Valley Anti-Dam Movement; Demand Halt to Mega Project and Release of Detained Activists
content:
“We stand with the people of the Siang Valley in their struggle to protect their river, their lands, their rights and the ability to determine their future. We recognise that the people who call this valley home must have the primary say in determining its future.”


 


Groundxero

 Desk


 


In a strong show of solidarity with the indigenous Adi communities resisting the proposed 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh, a group of 544 scientists, researchers, and concerned citizens working in the fields of nature, wildlife, society and the environment has called on the Union and state governments to immediately halt all pre-feasibility activities, withdraw additional security forces from the valley and release anti-dam protesters detained and arrested under the stringent Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA).


 


The statement, issued on November 9, 2026, comes amid growing resistance in the Siang Valley to the proposed mega-dam and reports of intensified security deployment, restrictions on people’s movement, arrests and the use of force against protesters.


 


The signatories, many of whom have worked in Arunachal Pradesh and the Eastern Himalayas, describe the Siang Valley as an ecologically irreplaceable landscape of immense biodiversity, cultural significance and traditional knowledge. Referring to an earlier statement by 114 scientists issued on June 9, 2025, they point out that 48 new species and 140 new distribution records have been documented in the valley in the past 15 years alone.


 


The statement warns that large-scale construction in an ecologically fragile and highly seismically active river system could have irreversible consequences. It emphasises that the Siang River, its forests and surrounding mountains sustain not only rich biodiversity but also the livelihoods, cultural identity and traditional knowledge systems of indigenous Adi communities.


 


The scientists express particular concern over the Arunachal Pradesh government’s continued efforts to push ahead with the project’s Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) despite sustained opposition from affected communities. They condemned the militarisation of this otherwise peaceful region, restrictions on movement, arrests and detentions of local anti-dam activists, and the use of tear gas and force against protesters. They also denounce the alleged harassment and intimidation of lawyers, journalists and others standing in solidarity of the movement.


 


Invoking the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), the signatories assert that the project must not proceed without the free, prior and informed consent of the affected indigenous communities, whose lands, livelihoods, cultural heritage and relationship with the Siang are at stake. They also stressed on the constitutional guarantees of freedom of speech, expression and peaceful assembly.


 


The statement calls on the Arunachal Pradesh and Union governments to stop all PFR-related activities, withdraw additional armed forces from the region, release those detained for participating in the movement, and initiate an open and meaningful dialogue with the affected communities.


 


The signatories affirm that the people who have protected and sustained the Siang Valley for generations must have the primary say in determining its future.


 


The full statement along with the list of signatories is published below:


 


November 9, 2026


 


We, a group of scientists, researchers, conservation practitioners and concerned citizens, many of whom have worked in Arunachal Pradesh and in the Eastern Himalaya, stand in unequivocal solidarity with the people of the Siang Valley in their opposition to the proposed 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP).


 


The Siang Valley is not merely a site for a proposed mega-infrastructure project. The Siang River, its forests and the surrounding mountains sustain extraordinary biodiversity, livelihoods, traditional knowledge systems and the cultural identity of indigenous Adi communities.


 


A statement issued by a collective of 114 scientists on 9th of June 2025, noted that the Siang is a rich living landscape of immense ecological, cultural and biological significance. In the past 15 years alone, there have been 48 new species described, as well as 140 new distribution records from the valley.

author: Czyrene Farrales
title: Ang mga bata, ang kanilang sining, at ang kanilang pakikisangkot sa lipunan
content:
I believe the children are our future

Itanong mo sa mga bata, ano ang kanilang nakikita sa buhay na hawak nila? – Asin

Malamang ay bata. Iisipin nating wala silang pakialam sa kapaligirang ginagalawan nila. Na ang tanging ginagawa nila sa maghapon ay maglaro sa malawak na lupain sa kanilang Sitio, o kaya nama’y pumilas ng dahon sa mga puno, o ang magtampisaw sa ilog.

Malamang ay bata. Musmos at walang kamuwang-muwang silang nabubuhay sa mundo. Ngunit kung tutuusin, isa sila sa dapat tinatanaw para sa isang kinabukasan.

Sumama ako sa grupo ng mga kabataan para makipamuhay sa isang sitio sa probinsya ng Tarlac. Mahabang oras ang ginugol namin sa byahe bago namin marating ang lugar nang tanghaling tapat.

Ito ang sumalubong sa amin sa Sitio Binyayan, Brgy. O’Donnell sa Capas.

Ang Sitio Binyayan ay nakapaloob sa 9, 450 hectares na lupain sa dating Green CIty na kalauna’y tinawag na New Clark City. Bahagi rin ito ng 1, 600 hectares sa ambisyosong proyektong Pax Silica Hub sa Capas, Tarlac.

Dalawang araw lamang ang aming pananatili sa lugar kung kaya’t kailangan imaksimisa ang paggamit ng oras at panahon para sa mabungang pananaliksik at integrasyon sa mga naninirahan sa Sitio Binyayan..

Sa hapon ay nag-ikot kami sa ilang kabahayan, bago sa gabi naman ay naglaan ng oras para sa kultural na mga aktibidad.

Bahagi sa mga isinagawang aktibidad ang coloring activity na dinaluhan ng iba’t ibang mga kabataan. Isa ako sa naatasang manguna para dito. Marahil gawa rin ng kasanayan ko sa paglikha ng mga dibuho at sining biswal ay malugod kong ginampanan ang tungkulin.

Sa pagsusuyod namin sa komunidad para maghanap ng mga kalahok sa naturang aktibidad, unang lumapit sa akin si Raychelle. Nag-aya pa siya ng ibang mga kabataan, hanggang sa dumami na sila. Mabilis lamang silang yayain– gawa na rin siguro ng wala gaanong akses sa mga aktibidad tungkol sa sining ang lugar.

Makukulit. Maiingay. Hindi maiiwasan at natural sa katangian bilang bata. Ngunit kahit papaano, marunong silang makinig: kung kailan tatahimik, kung kailan sasagot.

Sa simula ay nagpakilala muna kami at dahilan ng aming pananatili sa kanilang komunidad. Mabilis naman nilang naunawaan ang kalagayan.

Wala pa kaming binabanggit ukol sa Pax Silica– pero isang bata agad ang nakasambit ng salitang ito. Nang marinig ko ang sinabi niya, namangha ako. Hindi pala lingid sa kaalaman ng mga bata ang usapin ng Pax Silica.

Kanya-kanya nilang mga sagot. Iba’t iba at alam nila mismo ang epekto sa kanila ng itatayong proyektong malapit sa komunidad nila.

Binigyan namin sila ng paksa para mapakita nila ang kanilang paglalarawan at pag-intindi sa kung paano pangalagaan ang kalikasan.

Lumikha sila ng dibuho. Dibuhong puno ng berde at asul.

Nakita ko ang repleksyon ng paligid namin. Ang malawak na sakahan at bundok na pinapaligiran ang Sitio Binyayan. Ang asul na kalangitan at araw na bumubuhay sa mga pananim. Ang ilog kung saan kumukuha ng patubig para sa irigasyon ang mga magsasaka.

Dito ay mas naunawaan ko ang mga bata.

Kilala nila ang kanilang sitio bilang isang masaganang lupain. Payak man ang buhay ay nagagawa pa rin nilang ngumiti. Subalit sa likod ng mga ngiting ito ay ang pangangamba sa kanilang katiyakan sa kinalakihang komunidad.

Sa aming pagbisita, tumambad sa amin ang ilang bahagi ng dating sakahan na sinimulan nang sementuhin ng BCDA para sa itinatayong kalsada na bahagi ng New Clark City. Maging ang mga itinuturing na sagradong burial grounds ng mga katutubo ay pinatag na para sa naturang daan. Sa tagong lugar rin sa Sitio Binyayan ay may itinatayong pumping station para sa Pax Silica Hub na nakakaapekto sa kanilang pinagkukunan ng tubig sa mga poso.

Kalsada na ang dating mga sakahan

Burial grounds na ginagawang kalsada

Masdan mo ang mga bata, ang aral sa kanila makukuha – Asin

Bagama’t musmos at tila walang kamuwang-muwang sa mundo ay nagagawa nang makisangkot ng mga kabataan. Ang kanilang mga ibinahaging mga sagot ay ang nakikita nilang magiging buhay na hawak nila sa takdang panahon.

Wala sa edad ang pag-unawa sa isyung kinakaharap ng lipunan. Ang kanilang kaalaman, sa kabila ng kamusmusan, kaugnay sa proyektong itatayo sa kanilang komunidad ay isang patunay na hindi sila hiwalay sa laban.

Dahil para sa kanila ang lupa, ang katubigan, ang kalangitan, ang nayon at kapatagan, at maging ang laban para sa isang kinabukasang malaya.

author: Mekong Review 2
title: The death of a scammer Tonggo Simangunsong
content:
Poipet, near the Thailand–Cambodia border. Credit: wattana / Shutterstock.com I t was the end of 2024. Almost five months after losing his job at a food and beverage company, thirty-nine-year-old Rasdy Fawzi told his wife, Kiki Tresia Ginting, that he was going to accept a job in Cambodia. Kiki was concerned, and for good reason. The man who’d offered him the job was part of a scam syndicate; the recruitment agency was unregistered and the work Fawzi would be undertaking was illegal. She’d heard stories of young Indonesians trapped in Cambodia, tortured and forced to work as scammers. “I worried and asked my husband about his safety if he worked there, but he said, ‘That’s okay, it’s fine, don’t worry’,” she recalls. Fawzi reassured her many times that his friend had been there, too, and he trusted him. He believed that he was too old for any company in Indonesia to want to hire him for the same role he’d had in mobile sales marketing with his previous employer. While going to Cambodia was risky, the salary offered would be more than enough to support their small family. It was an opportunity he didn’t want to pass up. In the end, there was nothing Kiki could do but let him go and pray for his safety. To read the rest of this article, and to access all Mekong Review content, please subscribe . author: Mong Palatino
title: The thrill of group bike rides
content:
Bikers have been bonded by the daily commute or the frequent group rides, and this ritual of biking together can be turned into an advocacy action. This should not be a surprise since the tribe of bikers who regularly ride together suffers from the same grave inefficiencies that plague our roads and communities.

Biking brings calm and exhilaration at the same time, and these feelings are amplified during a group ride.

Planning a group ride takes time and patience, and it is deservedly celebrated when it happens.

It is usually done for leisure, a chill time with fellow bikers. It can be a training session for a scheduled race. Or it can become the power of many if organized to promote a cause.

Whatever the intent that pedals the ride, it is necessary to have trust, coordination, and the unity to move forward in one direction.

Safety measures are learned, relearned, enforced, and adopted during the ride. Newbies take cues from fellow riders, hand signals are introduced, and road rules that apply to cyclists are highlighted in real time. The grounding experience allows bikers to map out routes, rediscover a place from a new perspective, and become familiar with the local scenery. If field trips immerse travelers in history and the tourism value of a town or institution, a group bike tour provides the same allure and they cover even the remote corners that cars and buses cannot reach. A bike tour always offers new ways of seeing and experiencing the peripheries in our communities.

The group ride is an educative activity for all – riders, motorists, commuters, and pedestrians. It makes the bikers more visible, and this is deliberate. A lone biker wishes to be seen for his or her safety, a group ride ensures it and compels the people on the road to acknowledge the space reserved for cyclists. And if a protected bike lane is missing, the bikers crowding the street effectively become the mobile barrier that serves as a reminder not just of the presence of two-wheeled vehicles but also the right of others (non-car drivers) to use the taxpayer-funded road infrastructure.

This is the principle guiding critical mass rides which have become a global movement. An intentional biking of the many to normalize the idea of biking, encourage people to go out and bike, and destigmatize the use of roads by bikers. It is through these collective efforts that a community of bikers is formed. Bikers sharing the joy of biking and pedaling together to remove the perils of the supposedly mundane human act of travelling on a non-motorized vehicle.

There is no single community of bikers, and the diversity of these networks highlights the power that can be harnessed to deliver a message to broader segments in society. Bikers have been bonded by the daily commute or the frequent group rides, and this ritual of biking together can be turned into an advocacy action. This should not be a surprise since the tribe of bikers who regularly ride together suffers from the same grave inefficiencies that plague our roads and communities. They all see, hear, and experience the same daily evils of bad governance that propel citizens to speak out and mobilize.

Imagine a long line of bikers occupying a road, this scene repeated several times until it becomes normal. It is an attempt to rewire our perceptions of what a car-dominated street should look like. Then imagine this determined group of citizens on the move who by their mere presence reveal the glaring inadequacies in urban planning. They can be rallied to challenge car centrism and its morbid manifestations in policymaking, public works, traffic regulations, and toxic road mindset and habits.

The potential of tapping bikers to be active advocates of sociopolitical causes is confirmed by their actual participation in protest actions against controversial issues from the flood corruption scandal in 2025 to Pax Silica this year. Frequent bike rides have been organized to raise public awareness of pressing social concerns such as the critical conditions of rivers, coastal habitats, and watersheds. Both young and old bikers have shown enthusiastic participation in rides that explore historical landmarks and celebrate the opening of parks and green spaces.

Biking alone will not change the world, but it is a brave individual defiance of the norms in our motorized megapolis. Every pedal is a plea for consideration, recognition, and basic kindness. Biking together provides greater visibility and faster …

author: Jordan Humphreys
title: The “two souls” of the Spanish general strike
content:
A 24-hour general strike is set to take place across the Spanish state on 11 November, sparked by recent struggles over housing. In the lead-up to the general strike, 

Red Flag

’s 

Jordan Humphreys

 spoke to Germán 

P. Montañés

, a member of the revolutionary organisation Anticapitalistas, about the unfolding situation.

Red Flag

:

 Rising rents and house prices are affecting people across the globe. Why has it become such a flashpoint in the Spanish state in particular? What is the housing situation like there?

Germán

 

P. Montañés:

 Housing in the Spanish state has been a structural problem for a long time. One of the most visible impacts of the 2008 financial crisis was a wave of mortgage evictions. Today, mortgage-related evictions are less common, but renting has become much more widespread.

Even so, renting remains less common in Spain than in cities like Berlin or New York, where tenant voting blocs have played a major political role. In Spain, home ownership is the norm even among much of the working class. This stems from a strategy popularised during the dictatorship—echoing Margaret Thatcher’s later policies in the UK—summarised by a government minister’s famous quote: “I want a country of homeowners, not proletarians”. This high level of home ownership has somewhat cushioned the crisis; without it, the social situation likely would have collapsed much sooner.

Still, the crisis remains severe for two main groups: young people, who are locked out of home ownership and forced to pay exorbitant rents; and low-income workers and migrants, who face the worst housing instability.

The modern housing movement began around 2008 with anti-eviction campaigns such as the Plataforma de Afectados por la Hipoteca (PAH). Later, tenants’ unions emerged from these struggles—founded in 2017 in hubs like Madrid and Barcelona, and expanding across the Spanish state over the past few years.

A major tipping point occurred in late September, when police evicted 87-year-old María del Carmen (Maricarmen) Abascal from her home in Madrid. She had lived there for nearly 50 years under a rent-controlled agreement, but after an investment fund bought the building, her rent drastically increased. On the fourth attempt, police successfully removed her. This high-profile eviction sparked widespread outrage across the country. In response to the growing public backlash, the prime minister brought the general elections forward to 29 November.

RF

: 

Could you give us a better idea about the tenants’ unions—what kind of organisations are they, and what relationship do they have with the revolutionary left?

GPM:

 The emergence of tenant unions reflects the limits of the previous housing movement, which focused almost exclusively on stopping evictions. The problem with focusing on evictions is that the movement arrives far too late: by the time a family is facing removal, the police are already at the door.

The founding principle of the tenants’ unions was to adapt the most effective elements of trade unions to housing—arriving early to conflicts and organising people sooner. Rather than a diffuse social movement, housing activism needed a formal union. Members pay a monthly contribution, providing a financial base that allows staff to work full time and maintains an ongoing presence.

They also drew heavily on US labour tactics, focusing on entire buildings or properties owned by the same investment fund or landlord family to intervene long before eviction day.

They’ve been very successful recently in Madrid. Around September, they had about 2,000 to 3,000 members, and over the last two months of conflict, that number doubled to roughly 6,000. To clarify: these are financial members, not dedicated militants—there are perhaps 100 to 150 core militants—but the growth is significant.

The mainstream political left has no militant presence inside these spaces and does not control them; it tries to exert influence from the outside through government institutions and political pressure.

The revolutionary left isn’t broadly present either, though our organisation is the only one with a real foothold inside the unions. Our influence extends beyond raw numbers: we’ve maintained a dialogue with the union leadership for ten years. While the leaders come from autonomist or anarchist traditions, key militants in leadership positions allow us to maintain a solid presence. Our goal is to build a revolutionary current inside the …

author: Jerome Small
title: Carroll’s royal commission: an attack on effective unionism in Victoria
content:
The Royal Commission into the Integrity of Major Public and Civil Infrastructure Construction Projects in Victoria was announced by Victoria’s Labor Premier Ben Carroll in August: his first act as the incoming premier. 

Carroll’s announcement was a response to a years-long media campaign against the CFMEU, the main construction union. It was also part of a wholesale lurch to the right by an already neoliberal Labor government. And it is a blatant attack on any idea that unions should act to raise wages. 

If proof is needed, just look at the first day of the current bloc of hearings. I attended the first day of the commission back in September and sat through the proceedings yesterday via livestream.  

Literally the main point of yesterday’s hearing was how terrible it was that the CFMEU stopped a major construction job—the Gap Road level crossing removal in Sunbury—for a day and a half in June 2022, and that this resulted in traffic controllers winning an increase in wages from the award rate (at that time $26 per hour) to around $49 per hour. 

The horror. This equates to a full-time wage of $1,862 per week, slightly above Australia’s average full-time wage of $1,835 in 2022. It’s an OK wage, though no king’s ransom. With allowances, shift and casual loading, and the plentiful overtime that construction sites run on, this can add up to a decent wage if you’re prepared to work long hours.

To listen to Chris Young, the counsel assisting the royal commission, a union winning this sort of wage for a blue-collar worker through industrial action in 2026 is a threat to all that is right in the world. So much so that two weeks of the royal commission’s rather expensive time is being devoted to investigating how this could possibly have come about, with the express intention of ensuring it never happens again. 

Young spent yesterday sifting through the circumstances leading up to this supposed affront to decency. The CFMEU had a lot going in its favour. 

Railway crossing removals happen on a tight timetable, planned up to a year in advance. The two companies doing the work—John Holland and CPB—wanted to deliver the job on time in order to secure further work. The labour market was tight in Victoria. The CFMEU had already been successful in securing enterprise agreements with most of the big companies doing this sort of work in Victoria. From the evidence led by counsel assisting, it sounds like the CFMEU judged the moment perfectly—just like any union which is serious about taking action to raise wages should, and historically has. 

Both the CFMEU and the Australian Workers’ Union (AWU) cover workers working on civil construction projects like level crossing removals, and since 2014 the CFMEU has been trying to expand its coverage at the expense of the AWU. The Victorian Labor government at that time was uninterested in helping the AWU maintain coverage over these jobs—like Gap Road—and over traffic control work in particular. 

This was a positive for the workers at Gap Road, and more broadly. The royal commission was told that Zoom Recruitment, one of the AWU-aligned labour hire companies providing traffic control at Gap Road, was operating on a long-expired enterprise agreement that paid only the legal minimum specified in the construction award. 

This is utterly consistent with the business model of the AWU for the past century or more in construction, which is to undercut the wages and condition of the CFMEU and its predecessor unions. And to their credit, for most of that time, the CFMEU and their predecessors generally ignored the AWU’s claims to coverage on “civil” infrastructure work (roads, rail, bridges and tunnels).

The commission heard yesterday that the Labor government’s largely hands-off attitude to this demarcation dispute in 2022, which effectively favoured the CFMEU over the AWU, may have been because of factional alignments within the ruling Labor Party. This is hardly a crime, or even a novel tactic in Australian union politics.  

The AWU has used exactly the same approach, of translating political clout in the Labor Party into industrial coverage (and vice-versa), for its entire existence. The conservative Shop, Distributive and Allied Union (SDA) follows the same path. The only difference is that the AWU and the SDA have an appalling record of lifting wages—in fact the SDA did the opposite, helping employers undercut legal minimums, until a path-breaking legal case in the Fair Work …

author: Odessa Bishop-McMurray
title: “If they won’t give us a future, we will build one right here” - why the French revolt should inspire high-schoolers everywhere
content:
As one of the organisers of the upcoming nationwide 

Students Say No to Hanson

 demonstration on 12 November, I’ve had to endure a lot of inanity from the media and the right. Amongst snide remarks about the stages of brain development and warnings of the mortal dangers of missing two periods of class, one accusation keeps coming up: that we’re plotting to bring “French-style riots” to Australian cities. 

Right-wing journalists seized on an Instagram post we made on 11 October, conveying the inspiration we draw from French student protesters fighting government austerity and the far right. 

Cue an avalanche of hysterical headlines and news segments: The Murdoch-owned Adelaide 

Advertiser

 warned readers to brace for “walkouts ‘inspired’ by violent French protests”. Pauline Hanson went on Brisbane’s 4BC Radio to rip into us:

“...They are saying they are inspired by what’s going on in France. What? The 

looting

? The 

burning

? The 

destruction

? They’re 

inspired

 by that?”

Well, we’re not sorry for being inspired by French students. Everyone who wants to see a better world should identify with their struggle. 

Young people everywhere are facing a dire future, and revolt is rightly spreading. It’s clear even to some in the establishment that what’s happening in France is part of a global wave of protest with deep roots. As former UK Prime Minister Gordon Brown wrote this week in 

The Guardian

: “A global youthquake is happening. Promises we made young people have been broken—and they know it.”

Both far-right governments and “sensible centrists” are taking us on the same trajectory: more racism, more militarism, and more austerity. 

When states aren’t attempting to re-introduce conscription, as in Germany, they’re funnelling billions into the military-industrial complex while schools crumble. In France, students endure classrooms infested with cockroaches, mould and overcrowding, sometimes numbering 35 students to a class. 

We’ll likely never be able to afford secure housing or sufficient healthcare. We’ve watched politicians choose fossil fuel companies over the habitability of our planet. For many of us, the establishment’s unanimous endorsement of Israel’s genocide in Gaza was the final nail in the coffin.

It’s obvious that the journalists’ and politicians’ pearl-clutching about a few broken Parisian shop windows is a means of avoiding discussion of these issues. And their condemnation of violence rings hollow when they decline to comment on the vastly greater violence that the system inflicts on people daily. 

There’s the violence that is inherent in running such an unequal society. French youth linger without a future in the slums while the richest 500 families own nearly half the country. Schools and hospitals in France are crumbling, but the latest budget announcement includes 54 billion euros in further cuts to public spending. The police systematically brutalise Black and Arab working-class migrants. The high-profile killing of 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk, which sparked a nationwide revolt in 2023, is part of a long history of racialised policing. 

When these injustices generate resistance, there’s one public service the government can guarantee: the bludgeoning of protestors, tear gas, and potentially lethal stun grenades; exploding a student’s hand, breaking another’s jaw and leaving two 16-year-olds blinded for life. 

This is an inherent admission that the ruling class has no genuine plan to improve society. They just want resignation from ordinary people, and when that fails, tear gas is their backup plan.

But French students have shown that resignation gets us nowhere; Our power comes from the streets, and that’s a lesson the ruling class desperately does not want students to learn.

Already, France has shown small glimpses of how these movements can win real gains. While still hoping to crush the movement, the government has already been forced to make concessions. They’ve announced plans to cap class sizes, hire more teachers, and create more university places. This is a tiny fraction of what the movement is demanding, but it proves a timeless truth: a month of rebellion can win more change than decades of asking nicely.

A grassroots student movement in Serbia just ended the 14-year rule of the repressive Vučić regime. In Brazil, thousands of students flocked to the streets to successfully halt the advance of far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro.

It seems like …

author: Sagar Sanyal
title: Emergency and autocracy in Modi’s India
content:
The far-right government in India led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been increasingly repressive and anti-democratic over recent months. Commentators are asking if the country is in the grip of an ‘

undeclared Emergency

’, a reference to the 1975-77 period of ‘Emergency rule’ by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in which activists and trade unionists were simply rounded up and jailed. 

The current repression is a response to the student and youth protests that erupted in the capital, New Delhi, in late July. They were sparked by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), a satirical movement that began on social media a couple of months earlier. The scale and intensity of the protests surprised the regime, as did the mocking anti-Modi tenor of popular chants. While the protest demand was for the resignation of the education minister over exam leaks, the protesters were motivated by visceral opposition to Modi, who has ruled since 2014. The police lashed out using the sort of 

force

 that they typically use in repressed regions like Kashmir. Police fired pellet guns, used nail-studded batons and sexually assaulted women protesters. 

Despite the repression, tens of thousands mobilised daily for five days—high school and university students, middle-class and working-class youth. Not only in Delhi, but in dozens of cities around the country. Alongside clips of police brutality circulating on social media, there are clips of youth chasing police off the streets with their sheer numbers and bravado. There are clips of cheeky middle-class youth approaching police who are away from the heat of the action to ask mocking questions like “Dear Mr. Officer, are you planning to tear gas protesters today?” The government is tracking down incriminating and embarrassing recordings of those events and asking social media platforms to 

remove them

.

Public opinion has turned strongly against Modi’s repression. Among the Hindi-speaking, middle-class, upper-caste Hindus who have been the most secure vote base of the BJP, parents now saw their own children being beaten—just for demanding a fair opportunity in college exams! Ultimately, the administration conceded the protest demand to sack the education minister, a humiliating 

defeat

 for Modi. It gave the lie to the “unstoppable strongman” image of him so carefully crafted by pro-Modi big media. 

Less than three months after the July protests, a new protest movement gripped the nation. It demands the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner of India, Gyanesh Kumar, who has been highly partisan to Modi and his 

Hindu nationalist

 Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and, according to some parties, rigged state elections in Bihar (May 2025) and West Bengal (April 2026). In West Bengal, the BJP won for the first time due in part to the chief election commissioner disqualifying millions of names from the eligible voters list. Deletions disproportionately targeted Muslims, who are an ideological enemy of Hindu nationalists, and who were also an important vote base of the party the BJP displaced—the Trinamool Congress (TMC). 

Following a late September 

expose,

 which revealed that the chief election commissioner had overruled the protestations of even his fellow election commissioners, the CJP and left student groups took up vote-rigging as a national campaign to channel the energy from the July student movement. Demands for the chief election commissioner to resign have been taken up by all opponents of the BJP. 

When a large protest was called for 

10 October

, the state responded by locking down New Delhi. Around 40,000 paramilitary and police laid siege to a sizeable area around the “designated protest site” of Jantar Mantar in the centre of the city. They blocked roads and shut down local internet mobile services (India is 

among the worst

 states for this). They closed over 40 metro train stations in Delhi and stopped over 200 inter-city trains from reaching Delhi. They threatened activists in their homes on the night before the march, this coming on top of regular arbitrary detention of prominent leaders of the protest movement (from the CJP and the left parties). 

Undeterred

, protestors appeared in their tens of thousands and were again met with batons and tear gas, and thousands were detained.

Sizeable protests have continued sporadically since 10 October, some called by the CJP or student organizations of the left, 

others

 by major opposition parties. The …

author: Rick Kuhn
title: Unemployment: a feature of capitalism, not a bug
content:
Today more than one in ten workers can’t find enough paid labour to live a decent life. And that’s only workers actively looking for a job or for more hours of employment. It doesn’t count those who have given up on finding a job, even though they want one, and survive thanks to friends, family or a measly government payment that isn’t an unemployment benefit.

In September

 the seasonally adjusted

un

employment rate was 4.7 percent;

under

employment was 6.3 percent. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, you’re not unemployed if you worked even an hour in the survey fortnight.

To get the Jobseeker Payment or Youth Allowance the un- and underemployed have to follow the Albanese government’s savage eligibility rules, inherited from its Liberal predecessors. If you earn more than a pitiful $75 a week, your payment starts to go down. You must follow the instructions of Workforce Australia and, if you’ve been directed to one, of an outsourced “employment services provider” agency, which profits from government funding.

That may mean applying for a certain number of jobs every “reporting period”, doing training they tell you to do, however meaningless courses about writing job applications or behaviour during an interview might be; or perform “work for the dole”, that would normally be done for much higher award wages. You have to “accept any offer of suitable paid work”, defined by the provider, whether the type of work or its location actually suits you or not.

If you’re single, without kids, the dole is

currently


a princely $413 a week. Certainly in Sydney, you’d be very lucky if less than half of that went on renting a room. And if you’re young, that’s unfortunate: unemployed aged 21 or younger are penalised and get less money than those over 21. Apparently young people don’t need as much shelter, food, clothing, etc. as older people.

Both the unemployment and underemployment rates are rising.

Unemployment is not a bug in capitalism, but a feature. The threat of un- and underemployment – descending into what Marx called “

the industrial reserve army

”—disciplines workers fearful of losing their jobs. The higher the level of unemployment, other things being equal, the less likely they are to take risks by fighting to defend or improve their pay and conditions.

The extent of the reserve army of labour changes in the course of economic cycles: lower during booms, higher in slumps.

Many central banks, like the Reserve Bank of Australia, are bumping up interest rates to slow their countries’ economies down. Their goal is not increased unemployment; that’s a side effect. Their main target is the rate of inflation. High inflation—lack of stability in the purchasing power of money—makes calculations by capitalists about their activities and especially investments more difficult.

In legislation

, the RBA has two goals: “price stability and the maintenance of full employment”. It says that “

[t]hese two objectives usually work together

”. In practice, the bank favours sacrificing jobs to keep a lid on inflation.

But today, high oil prices, due to the USA’s and Israel’s war on Iran, is the main driver of inflation. The RBA isn’t bumping up interest rates to discipline workers, although that’s a side-effect. Governor

Michelle Bullock

said at the end of September that “There is no wage price spiral going on in Australia. Rises in wages are not driving … cost pressures”.

In fact, it is workers who are mainly affected by inflation. Greg Jericho, in the

Guardian

, has illustrated how workers’ real pay has been falling since 2021, compared with the Consumer Price Index by 7 percent; compared with the more appropriate Employee Living Cost Index, by more than 12 percent.

The hostility of most union officials to leading their members in serious struggles to defend, let alone restore or improve their living standards, is mainly to blame.

In his 1972 report

Poverty in Australia

, Ronald Henderson, appointed by the Liberal government of Billy McMahon, calculated a poverty line, marking an “austere” standard of living below which people were in poverty. The Melbourne Institute of Economic Research frequently updates it.

JobSeeker

has consistently been below this line. Today that unemployment benefit is less than half the

Henderson poverty line

. Using 50, let alone 60 percent of median

household income

, common alternative international measures of poverty, the situation of people on JobSeeker …

author: Önder Algedik
title: Seven things you must never say about COP31
content:
COP31 opened in Antalya on November 9 and its two hosts — Türkiye and Australia — have been busy.

Australia’s Labor government, despite being elected on promises to act for the climate, has approved 37 new or expanded fossil fuel projects since 2022.

Since September 2025 it has signed 19 fossil fuel agreements: 20-year liquefied natural gas (LNG) contracts, oil and gas exploration pacts with ExxonMobil, Chevron and TotalEnergies, drilling rights from Syria to Somalia, and a deal with Australia’s Woodside.

On top of those come six nuclear and mining agreements, three of them were signed in Seoul on November 3, six days before the summit opened.

One host approves the projects. The other signs the contracts. Together they will run a summit whose Action Agenda does not name coal, oil or gas even once.

Everything is going smoothly. In Türkiye, censorship helps; at least 1270 X accounts were blocked in September alone and, over the past 20 months, trustees have been appointed to 10 television channels.

So, to keep the hosts comfortable, here are seven things you must never talk about.

1. Don’t talk about fossil philanthropy

In June, the foundations of the companies that change Türkiye’s climate the most, including a refinery, car factory, coal power plant, an electricity distributor and even the operator of Antalya airport, set up “Philanthropy for Climate”. They invited environmental groups to the table. The polluters bring the money; civil society brings the legitimacy. Australians who have watched gas companies sponsor festivals and sport will know the model.

2. Don’t talk about the COP31 bill

COP31 is expected to cost close to US$2 billion. When the host agreement came before Türkiye's parliament in July, one party wrote a dissenting opinion and then abstained. Only five MPs voted “No”. An agreement that cost to the public up to US$2 billion bill passed in near silence.

COP31 is, in a sense, a rubbish summit; “Zero waste” heads its list of themes. In August, as rubbish washed up along the Mediterranean coast, the national debate was only about waste imported from Britain. Meanwhile, according to Türkiye’s statistics office, more than 10 million tonnes of waste was burned in 2024. The sky became the landfill.

4. Don't talk about the fossil deals

Has anyone at COP31 mentioned the deals Türkiye signed while preparing to host it? The energy minister posed for photos at every ceremony. A 20-year LNG contract with Mercuria. Exploration in the Black Sea and Eastern Mediterranean with ExxonMobil and TotalEnergies. A global partnership with Chevron, from Iraq to Venezuela. A stake in Kirkuk’s oil fields. Rights to drill in Syria, Libya, Somalia and Pakistan. And Woodside’s LNG.

When I counted in October, there were 14. Now there are 19.

5. Don’t talk about cities without resilience

On October 14, Istanbul, Sakarya, Kocaeli, Yalova, Muğla and Antalya went under water on the same day. The minister of urbanisation, who is also COP31 president, called it a “disaster”, blamed climate change and moved the topic onto the summit’s “Resilient Cities” theme. Were these resilient cities or cities stripped of their resilience? Between 2002 and 2021, Türkiye laid 603 million tonnes of asphalt and poured close to a billion tonnes of cement. If you must, talk only about river beds and pretend the valley slopes above them were never paved. In three days, everyone forgets.

6. Say ‘conference’, not ‘fair’

COP stands for Conference of the Parties. But it has become a Fair of the Parties. The minister announced that 1.5 million visitors are expected! That is not a venue for negotiation; it is an exhibition ground. As I argued last month, the stands will be busy and the products green. Never call it a fair. Say “climate summit”, a phrase with no actor and no action.

Say “coal phase-out”, but never mention oil. Ask for a coal exit date, which buys the government time. Don’t touch the summit’s global business partner, Koç Holding, which owns Türkiye's oil refineries. Call gas a “bridge fuel”. Australians know this one: Labor’s Future Gas Strategy says gas will be needed to 2050 and beyond.

So here are the seven things we must not talk about: Fossil philanthropy, the public bill, a country turned into a dump, fossil deals, asphalt-and-concrete cities, a summit turned trade fair, and oil and gas.

Nobody has to ban any of this, because we already don’t talk about it. We don't talk about the groups that sit at the table with fossil …

author: Unknown
title: Evrensel'in HABAŞ gerçeğini katliamdan önce ortaya koyan haberleri TBMM gündeminde
content:
İzmir'in Aliağa ilçesindeki HABAŞ Demir Çelik Fabrikası'nda meydana gelen patlamada 18 işçinin yaşamını yitirmesi üzerine TBMM'de Yeni Yol, CHP, DEM Parti ve Yeni Parti gruplarının verdiği Meclis araştırma önergeleri, AKP ve MHP'nin oylarıyla reddedilirken milletvekilleri konuşmalarında sık sık Evrensel'in HABAŞ haberlerine atıf yaptı. Bazı milletvekilleri Evrensel'in İzmir bürosunun HABAŞ patronu hakkında attığı manşetin ardından kurşunlandığını hatırlattı, bazı milletvekilleri ise Çalışma Bakanlığının "gerekli denetimler yapıldı" açıklamasına Evrensel haberlerinde yer alan bilgilerle tepki gösterdi ve aslında şirketin kendi kendini ihbar ettiğini ortaya koyan "HABAŞ patronu katliamın geleceğini biliyordu" haberimizdeki bilgileri aktardı.

Konuşmasında Türkiye'nin dört bir yanında işçilerin yaşadığı sorunlara değinen DEM Parti İstanbul Milletvekili Cengiz Çiçek, "Bu ülkeyi patronlar kulübü yönetiyor. Evrensel gazetesi, ilgili şirketle ilgili manşet yaptığında gazete kurşunlandı" dedi.

Yeni Parti Ankara Milletvekili Gamze Taşcıer ise Çalışma Bakanı'nın HABAŞ'taki denetimlerde ciddi bir sorun bulunmadığı yönündeki açıklamasına karşın Evrensel'in daha önce yayımladığı haberleri gündeme getirerek "Oysa daha bir buçuk yıl önce Evrensel gazetesi bu fabrikayla ilgili haberleri manşete taşımıştı ve çok uzağa gitmeye gerek yok, şirketin kendi raporunda bile kendini ihbar ettiği çok açık bir şekilde gözüküyor ancak ciddiye alan bir Bakanlık yok" dedi.

Taşcıer, şirketin verilerine dayanarak ağır iş kazalarının bir yılda yüzde 56, taşeron işçilerin geçirdiği kazaların yüzde 120 arttığını söyledi. İş güvenliği eğitiminin 66 bin saatten 9 bin saate düştüğünü ve şirket raporunda haftalık çalışma süresinin 61 saat olarak yer aldığını belirterek “Çalışma Bakanlığı neyi denetledi?” diye sordu.

DEM Parti İstanbul Milletvekili Kezban Konukçu da HABAŞ’ın kayıp günlü iş kazası sayısının 2024’te 109’dan 2025’te 146’ya çıktığını belirterek Bakanlığın denetimlerini eleştirdi. Konukçu, "HABAŞ patronu Mehmet Rüştü Başaran 2025’te işçilerin ücretlerini yüzde 33 düşürerek 4,7 milyar lira kazanç sağlamıştı. Bunu haber yaptığı için Evrensel gazetesi silahlı saldırıya maruz kalmıştı yani organize suç örgütü olarak çalışan bir kuvvet görüyoruz karşımızda; iktidarından patronuna, yargısına kadar ve yer altı örgütüne kadar işçiler ölsün, patronlar kâr etsin diye çalışıyorsunuz" ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Carlos Pérez
title: “Esto no para”: Una perspectiva de base sobre la huelga indefinida por la educación pública en Madrid
content:
“Esto no para”: Una perspectiva de base sobre la huelga indefinida por la educación pública en Madrid


Desde el 14 de octubre, las docentes de Madrid, España, se encuentran en huelga indefinida en defensa de la educación pública. Tras años de deterioro de las condiciones laborales y una organización sistemática de las bases, las docentes han inundado las calles de la capital española en una movilización masiva que ha vinculado la lucha por la educación pública con la reciente revuelta en torno a la vivienda.


La lucha conjunta por la vivienda y la educación pública en España se encamina ahora hacia una huelga general el 11 de noviembre, en medio de un levantamiento más amplio que se extiende por toda Europa.


Carlos Pérez, maestro de estudios sociales en Carolina del Norte y miembro de la junta directiva de Labor Notes habló con María, profesora de secundaria de historia y geografía en Madrid y militante de Menos Lectivas, una de las principales fuerzas de base detrás de la huelga.


Pérez: Los docentes de la escuela pública en Madrid mantienen una huelga indefinida desde el 14 de octubre. ¿Cuáles son los motivos principales que les llevaron a usted y a otros docentes a convocar una huelga, y cuáles son sus reivindicaciones?


María:

 En la Comunidad de Madrid venimos arrastrando recortes en la educación pública desde el año 2011. Estos han ido deteriorando el estado de las aulas y la calidad educativa de los estudiantes madrileños.


La falta de recursos y de personal, la cantidad de alumnos en el aula, el aumento de horas lectivas (horas de clase directa en el aula) y la falta de mantenimiento y construcción de infraestructuras nos han dejado un escenario en el que impartir clase es muy complicado. Las docentes no llegamos a atender a todos nuestros estudiantes y hemos decidido plantarnos ante el maltrato institucional que sufrimos tanto nosotras como nuestro alumnado.


En mi caso, he dado clase a aulas de bachillerato con 33 alumnos, he tenido que buscar un aula donde meter a mis alumnos cada día durante un mes de lluvias intensas porque las aulas tenían unas goteras que provocan que estuviesen constantemente mojadas; mis alumnos con necesidades educativas (autismo o dificultades de audición y lenguaje) no han sido atendidos por las profesionales que hacían falta porque no había ni integradora social ni profesora específica para ellos, y por supuesto trabajo una cantidad de horas extra ingentes y no están remuneradas ni reconocidas.


Por eso reivindicamos y exigimos a la Comunidad de Madrid que reduzca las horas lectivas; reducir los ratios entre las docentes y alumnos; acabar con la segregación, dado que la Comunidad de Madrid es la región de España más segregada en educación; aumentar el salario para equiparlo a las necesidades económicas actuales; reducir la burocracia, entre otras cosas.


Menos Lectivas, una plataforma de base que agrupa a varios sindicatos, ha sido uno de los principales impulsores de la huelga. ¿Qué es Menos Lectivas y qué papel ha desempeñado en este conflicto?


Menos Lectivas nace en el 2023, inspirada por colectivos como Labor Notes en los EEUU, con la intención de organizar a las trabajadoras de la educación desde los centros de trabajo y devolver el poder sindical a las trabajadoras. Desde entonces hemos construido nuestro movimiento a través de asambleas de centro.


En estos años previos a la huelga indefinida se han convocado huelgas, manifestaciones y concentraciones que han servido para que cada vez el movimiento fuese más grande y, sobre todo, tuviésemos legitimidad institucional — tanto con los trabajadores que nos ven como un agente de lucha válido porque se sienten parte de él gracias a las asambleas, como para el resto de sindicatos, los medios de comunicación y en última instancia los gobiernos — para decidir cómo, cuándo y dónde queríamos luchar por el derecho a la educación y nuestros derechos laborales.


Desde los inicios sabíamos que la huelga indefinida sería la última herramienta de lucha sindical si nuestras demandas no eran escuchadas por la Comunidad de Madrid y, el pasado junio, se decidió en asamblea que las docentes iríamos a la huelga indefinida. Siendo ya un conjunto de asambleas con legitimidad el resto de sindicatos que no formaban parte de Menos Lectivas tuvieron que sentarse con nosotras en el Comité de Huelga a negociar la constitución de una mesa de negociación y las condiciones de la huelga. Este hito ya es un éxito, consiguiendo que el poder …

author: Julia Conley
title: In Letter, 600,000-Member Machinists Union Urges Schumer to Step Aside
content:
The “elections sent a clear message: Working people are demanding change,” wrote IAM Union’s international president.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s bid to continue leading the Democratic Party when it takes control of the US Senate in January continued to falter Monday night as a key machinists’ union asked the New York senator to step aside and allow “a new generation to lead Senate Democrats.”

In a letter, Brian Bryant, international president of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers (IAM Union) thanked Schumer for “many years of leadership, friendship, and unwavering commitment to working people” before telling him that “after thoughtful discussions,” the IAM Union Executive Council had opted not to support Schumer’s push to remain as the Senate leader.

“With the utmost respect and appreciation for your service, we respectfully urge you not to seek another term as Senate Democratic leader,” Bryant wrote. “We also encourage all returning and newly elected Democratic senators to join together through a fair and open process to select a consensus leader who can unite the party, build on your legacy and carry forward a bold vision for working people.”

Schumer losing support of unions now. Big development. https://t.co/dvG1MNMefz

The letter came hours after Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) told reporters that he was considering a challenge to Schumer, after initially saying he was not interested in running for the Senate majority leader post following the party’s electoral sweep last week.

Candidates who won Senate seats include several outspoken proponents of Medicare for All, such as Sens.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.), Troy Jackson (D-Maine), and Peggy Flanagan (D-Minn.), and others who centered in their campaigns the need to decisively take on billionaires and worsening economic inequality.

A decision by Schumer to step aside in favor of “new leadership,” said Bryant, would allow the party to “turn this moment into lasting progress.”

He wrote that the party must push to pass the Protecting the Right to Organize (PRO) Act, restore collective bargaining rights to all federal workers, reinstate Affordable Care Act and give “every American the healthcare they need, and pass ”meaningful rail safety legislation.“

“Our country is at a critical crossroads and a moment of extraordinary opportunity. This week’s elections sent a clear message: Working people are demanding change,” said Bryant. “The IAM Union’s Workers vs. Billionaires movement reflects a growing desire for an economy and political system that puts working families ahead of wealthy special interests. We have a tremendous opportunity to build on this momentum, but doing so will require fresh ideas, new energy, and a new generation of leadership.”

Bryant’s message made clear that “it’s time” for Schumer to step aside, said author and commentator Don Winslow.

“The Democratic Party will make a catastrophic mistake if they lock out all of these voters for a man who has been in political office for 51 years,” said Winslow.

The letter came after Schumer’s support among senior Democrats appeared to crack on Monday, with Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) telling reporters, “We need a conversation about leadership going forward because we need new energy and ideas.”

But later that evening, the senator said that he expected Schumer to become Senate majority leader and plans to back him.

Van Hollen, who has reportedly received a steady stream of phone calls since last week from voters calling on him to take the helm of the party in the Senate, reiterated Monday evening that he believes there should be “a full caucus discussion” about the path forward.

title: Künstliche Intelligenz: KI-Einsatz in der Arbeitswelt – Folgen und Mitbestimmung
content:
Dossier


„… Der Einsatz Künstlicher Intelligenz löse derzeit bei vielen Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmern Sorgen und Ängste aus, so Schmitz weiter. „Selbststeuernde Prozesse führen zu einer neuen Arbeitsteilung zwischen Mensch und Maschine, ohne dass diese bisher ausreichend erforscht ist.“ Drängende Fragen der Kontrolle, der Ent- oder Belastung, der Qualifizierung und der Beschäftigungssicherung müssten geklärt werden. (…) „Künstliche Intelligenz ist Werkzeug, Mittel zum Zweck. KI-Anwendungen müssen der Verbesserung von Arbeits- und Lebensqualität dienen.“ KI-Systeme seien so zu gestalten, dass die Handlungs- und Gestaltungsspielräume der Erwerbstätigen erweitert werden. „Tätigkeiten sind durch gezielte Qualifizierung aufzuwerten. Dies kann durch Tarifverträge flankiert und durch neue Stellenzuschnitte unterstützt werden.“

„

Künstliche Intelligenz soll Arbeit erleichtern. Doch Zeitgewinne können zusätzliche Aufgaben bedeuten. Wer entscheidet, was Beschäftigte davon haben?


Im Nachbarland ist manches ähnlich: Ein Drittel der Beschäftigten in Frankreich überschreitet regelmäßig seine üblichen Arbeitszeiten. Bei Führungskräften sind es rund 60 Prozent. Das zeigt eine

Untersuchung des Forschungszentrums CEET


, die Angaben von rund 30.000 Beschäftigten aus den Jahren 2019 bis 2023 auswertet.

Wer länger arbeitet, berichtet auch häufiger von weiteren Belastungen. Überstunden und Arbeitsverdichtung kommen zusammen. (…)


Wird gewonnene Zeit zur Erholung genutzt, mit zusätzlichen Aufgaben gefüllt oder für Personalabbau verplant? Darüber entscheiden Personalstärke, Leistungsvorgaben und betriebliche Aushandlung. Doch wenn Unternehmen bereits mit den erhofften Effizienzgewinnen rechnen, stellt sich eine weitere Frage: Wird die Zeit schon verplant, bevor sie überhaupt eingespart ist?

“

Beitrag von Andrej Simon vom 09. November 2026 in Telepolis

 


„Manche haben ihr Team in weniger als einem Jahr mehr als halbiert“: KI durchrüttelt die Arbeitswelt


„

KI produziert Filme, schreibt Code, führt Unternehmen – und vernichtet Jobs in Rekordtempo. Was das für Arbeit, Gesellschaft und Demokratie bedeutet. (…)


Im Silicon Valley entstehen Unternehmen mit Dutzenden oder Hunderten KI-Agenten und einer Handvoll Beschäftigten. Screenpipe.com, das hilft, Computerfunktionen zu automatisieren, hat seinen Umsatz in kurzer Zeit mit nur zwei Beschäftigten von 60.000 Dollar auf 1,5 Millionen Dollar gesteigert und plant keineswegs, weitere einzustellen. Der Traum von San Francisco im Jahr 2026 ist ein Unternehmen mit Millionenumsätzen und nur einem Beschäftigten. Und dieser Traum rückt näher. Ein durchschnittliches Unternehmen in den Vereinigten Staaten oder Italien erzielt rund 250.000 Euro oder Dollar Umsatz pro Beschäftigtem.


Anthropic hingegen kommt auf neun Millionen Dollar pro Beschäftigtem, OpenAI auf 5,6 Millionen. Nicht etwa, weil beide finanziell glänzend dastünden – OpenAI läuft Gefahr, seine gesamten liquiden Mittel innerhalb von neun Monaten zu verbrennen –, sondern weil beide um ihre oberste Führungsebene herum organisiert sind, mit sehr wenigen Untergebenen. Vielleicht sind es schlicht Systeme, die darauf ausgelegt sind, Geld nach oben zu saugen, an die Spitze der Pyramide. Derweil erledigen die KI-Agenten fast alles. (…)


Vor allem unter den Jüngeren und in den Berufen, die der künstlichen Intelligenz am stärksten ausgesetzt sind, bricht die Beschäftigung in Amerika bereits ein. Bei den 22- bis 25-Jährigen in den am leichtesten automatisierbaren Berufen liegt die Zahl der besetzten Arbeitsplätze schon 19 % unter dem Wert, der sich bei einer Entwicklung entsprechend dem Durchschnitt des Arbeitsmarktes ergeben hätte.


Dieser Teil der Auswirkungen kann auch Italien unmittelbar und als Erstes erreichen: Man entlässt niemanden, stellt aber nicht mehr ein und überträgt die Arbeit einer KI. title: De la bendición de Devoto al calvario de Marcos Paz: Milton Tolomeo, preso por luchar contra la reforma laboral, inició una huelga de hambre
content:
Milton Tolomeo se encuentra detenido desde hace casi nueve meses en el Penal Federal de Marcos Paz. Sufre esta detención al igual que Eneas Gallo por haber participado en la movilización en contra de la reforma laboral. Los acusaron de terroristas y les dictaron prisión preventiva. E

l acto humanitario del Papa de visitar la Cárcel de Devoto significó una bendición para los poquitos que quedaron allí y un calvario a 50 km de distancia para los que fueron trasladados a Marcos Paz. A los malos tratos recibidos se suma que les han suspendido todas las actividades educativas, no cuentan con médico de planta, no se les entregan los medicamentos recetados, se les han secuestrado efectos personales y hasta su ropa. Están suspendidas todas las actividades recreativas y los talleres, tampoco existe el servicio de cantina y el régimen de depósito de alimentos permitidos cambia continuamente, siempre haciendo prevalecer las prohibiciones.

Las visitas se han acortado y las demoras reducen el tiempo formalmente asignado de tres horas semanales.


Y por primera vez en décadas el Servicio Penitenciario Federal obstaculiza las visitas de los organismos de DD.HH. Esta suma de elementos es lo que llevó al compañero Milton a declararse en huelga de hambre a partir de las cero horas del día domingo hasta obtener una respuesta a sus reclamos.

Por Coordinadora de Presxs Políticxs.


Milton Tolomeo se encuentra detenido desde hace casi nueve meses en el Penal Federal de Marcos Paz. Sufre esta detención al igual que Eneas Gallo por haber participado en la movilización en contra de la reforma laboral. Los acusan de los disturbios que produjo la policía (como lo hace siempre), durante esa marcha el 11 de febrero pasado.


Ni siquiera los detuvieron en el lugar de los hechos, los «identificaron» mediante el ciber patrullaje, que analiza imágenes buscando patrones comunes. Y los fueron a detener en su domicilio o en su trabajo en el caso de Milton. La verdad es que los tenían «marcados», porque tanto Eneas como Milton siempre acompañaron las luchas de jubilados, discapacitados, trabajadores en lucha o despedidos, estudiantes y trabajadores de la eduación.


Los acusaron de terroristas y les dictaron prision preventiva. El mismo aparato judicial que acaba de dictaminar que Adorni no se robó nada y lo deja libre de culpa y cargo, condena de antemano con la prisión preventiva a trabajadores precarizados que no tienen ni donde caerse muertos y los amenaza con dictarles condenas de hasta treinta años de prisión.


De este modo, el acto humanitario del Papa de visitar la Cárcel de Devoto significó una bendición para los poquitos que quedaron allí y un calvario a 50 km de distancia para los que fueron trasladados a Marcos Paz, a lo que llaman Nueva Unidad Carcelaria, que en realidad es una cárcel sin terminar, con un diseño edilicio que tiene por objeto inocultable producir una sensación de agobio durante todo el tiempo.


A los malos tratos recibidos se suma que les han suspendido todas las actividades educativas, no cuentan con médico de planta, no se les entregan los medicamentos recetados, se les han secuestrado efectos personales y hasta su ropa. Están suspendidas todas las actividades recreativas y los talleres, tampoco existe el servicio de cantina y el régimen de depósito de alimentos permitidos cambia continuamentesiempre haciendo prevalecer las prohibiciones.


Las visitas se han acortado y las demoras reducen el tiempo formalmente asignado de tres horas semanales. Y por primera vez en décadas el Servicio Penitenciario Federal obstaculiza las visitas de los organismos de derechos humanos, rompiendo con una práctica histórica.


Esta suma de elementos es lo que llevó al compañero Milton a declararse en huelga de hambre a partir de las cero horas del día domingo hasta obtener una respuesta a sus reclamos.


Pedimos la mayor difusión a este comunicado y también sumar su voz para exigir la inmediata libertad de Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo.

author: CNT Galiza
title: Cuando el lucro marca el rumbo
content:
Leer en

Castellano

Galego


Castellano

Cuando el lucro marca el rumbo


Este año 2026 será recordado, entre otras razones, por la siniestralidad ferroviaria. No será el único motivo, pero sí el más lamentable. Desde la Confederación Nacional del Trabajo, y comenzando por nuestra parte como Coordinadores Ferroviarios de la CNT, queremos mostrar nuestro sincero apoyo a las familias y víctimas del accidente ocurrido el 28/10/26 cerca de Urda, Toledo.


Nuestro trabajo como sindicalistas aborda la denuncia de situaciones críticas para los trabajadores del sector desde una perspectiva radical. Con ello, queremos llegar al fondo del problema. A la hora de analizar los problemas y las graves deficiencias de la red de transporte ferroviario a nivel nacional, debemos ser muy concienzudos. Hablamos de un sistema complejo con un gran número de factores interconectados que dependen unos de otros en diferentes niveles.


Afortunadamente, tenemos presencia en todos estos niveles. Somos quienes conducimos, quienes ajustamos las tuercas o quienes mantenemos en funcionamiento los sistemas digitales. Aun así, el propósito de estas líneas no es enumerar ni realizar un análisis exhaustivo que constituya la declaración del estado de la red. No podemos ser tan ambiciosos, no contamos con los medios. Pero sí podemos generar la contrapartida del discurso mediático para que llegue a las personas afectadas: las víctimas, los trabajadores y los pasajeros.


Pero primero, analicemos los antecedentes. En lo que respecta a la gestión de una infraestructura cuyo peso relativo en la economía es muy elevado, hablamos de políticas públicas.


La administración de empresas estatales ha sustituido al modelo anterior de grandes empresas públicas. Por lo tanto, los servicios básicos a la ciudadanía se han transformado en ofertas para el consumidor. Al transferir este usufructo a manos privadas, junto con la propiedad de bienes ilimitados, se está despojando a la sociedad en su conjunto.


Con la siguiente lista de elementos, buscamos destacar la formidable fuerza laboral y los medios de producción que han sido desmantelados y entregados a especuladores mediante políticas de liberalización y privatización. La enorme relevancia que tiene para la actividad económica e industrial del país se evidencia en el volumen e importancia de los procesos y sectores que abarca. Para empezar a comprender el volumen de negocios involucrado, debemos clasificarlo por actividades:


Industria pesada > Producción fabril: altos hornos, fundiciones y mecanizado…


Infraestructura y obras civiles > Empresas de construcción e ingeniería (obras públicas, canteras y minas, siderurgia, cemento y productos químicos, hormigón…)


Energía > Distribución eléctrica, sistemas electrotécnicos y de control, automatización industrial…


Tecnología > Fabricación de trenes y material rodante, telecomunicaciones, software y plataformas digitales, patentes e I+D…


Logística > Puertos secos y terminales intermodales, muelles de carga, almacenamiento general…


Servicios de transporte de mercancías > Contenedores, empresas madereras, sector marítimo, combustibles y petroquímicos, automoción, agroalimentación, proveedores…


Empresas de transporte turístico, transporte urbano, transporte de media y larga distancia…


Servicios de consultoría ambiental, topografía, geotécnica…


Servicios financieros Contratación, compañías de seguros, gestión laboral y tributación, formación e investigación, inspecciones técnicas y ensayos clínicos, gestión de residuos y limpieza…


Servicios comerciales, comercio exterior, almacenamiento, turismo y hostelería…


Es importante tener en cuenta que una infraestructura crítica como el transporte ferroviario constituye una vasta red de sistemas, un pulmón productivo sobre el que se asienta uno de los pilares fundamentales de la actividad económica del país. Se trata de un microestado con capacidades paralelas. Tiene la facultad de privar de derechos y enajenar activos de propiedad pública, es decir, de modificar la situación jurídica relativa al uso de un bien o servicio y formalizar el traspaso de la propiedad a otra persona o entidad. Nos encontramos, por tanto, ante uno de los instrumentos más poderosos de los que dispone el sistema capitalista para perpetuar la reproducción de su modelo económico.
