author: Daron Letts
title: Dialogue about Inuit-specific housing funding underway, says Indigenous Services Minister
content:
Inuit-Nunangat’s share of billions of dollars in federal housing and infrastructure funding announced in

Thursday

‘s budget

 remains undetermined, but that could change soon, Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty said Saturday in Iqaluit.


“I think that we’ll have greater clarity in the next few days,” Gull-Masty said during a news conference at the Inuusirvik Community Wellness Hub. It marked the start of a two-day visit to the territory, her first trip to the eastern Arctic. In addition to her role as Indigenous Services minister, Gull-Masty is the Liberal MP for Abitibi—Baie-James—Nunavik—Eeyou, the sprawling Quebec riding that includes Nunavik.


The Liberal government’s budget allocated $30 billion for First Nations housing and infrastructure as part of Prime Minister Mark Carney’s new commitment to eliminate homelessness within a decade.


But the budget did not mention comparable investments for Inuit communities.


However, discussions with Inuit organizations about how to fund housing and infrastructure in Inuit communities are ongoing, Gull-Masty said.


“It’s imperative that we take the time, that we take that space and really have that conversation to reflect the uniqueness of the North,” she said. “It’s important for us if we want to reach that target in the North that we shape it according to the realities of what it means to live here and deliver services.”


She met with representatives from Nunavut Tunngavik Inc., the organization that represents Inuit beneficiaries under the Nunavut Agreement, on Saturday.


On Thursday, she met with Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami president Natan Obed, the head of the national organization for Inuit in Canada.


Gull-Masty said the dialogue about Inuit-specific funding for housing and infrastructure will continue later this year during a meeting of the Inuit-Crown Partnership Committee, a bilateral forum that brings together Inuit leaders and federal cabinet ministers to advance shared priorities.


Nunavut MP Lori Idlout and Iqaluit Mayor Solomon Awa also met with Gull-Masty on Saturday.


Idlout said she is confident Nunavut will be included in Carney’s commitment to eliminate homelessness across Canada within a decade.


“What this government will need to do is make sure that it works respectfully with the Inuit organizations to ensure that Nunavut’s needs are being met,” Idlout said.


Awa shares Idlout’s optimism.


“It can be done if we work really hard,” he said.

author: Emma Honeybun
title: Prime minister announces $1B for housing, new hospital to ‘tackle’ homelessness in Winnipeg
content:
Prime Minister Mark Carney joined Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew and the mayor of Winnipeg to announce a joint funding venture to build more than 2,000 new homes and an addictions treatment centre in the middle province’s capital.

The federal government will be allocating $1 billion overall, with $800 million going to the homes and the remaining $200 million going to the proposed Winnipeg Mental Health and Addictions Centre, as well as the refurbishment of similar facilities.

“There’s no simple answer,” Carney said. “This is a hard problem. And hard problems demand the humility to learn from previous well-intentioned efforts that have fallen short.”

Funds will also go to supporting local, grassroots organizations that are already involved in addressing the homelessness crisis, including End Homelessness Winnipeg, the North End Women’s Centre, and Chalmers Neighbourhood Renewal Corporation.

Carney said the partnership is one project in an “unprecedented” $30 billion allocation in the 2026 budget, with the end goal of ending homelessness in Canada in 10 years.

“Help works,” he said, which extends to housing and healthcare.

Alongside federal, provincial and municipal governments, funding for these Winnipeg-based projects will also be provided by First Nation governments such as the Southern Chiefs’ Organization (SCO), as well as private funders such as True North Sports and Entertainment, owner of the Winnipeg Jets and the primary investor in several major infrastructure projects downtown.

“It’s the first time in our country’s history where every level of government has come together to tackle homelessness,” Kinew said. “Including First Nations and Métis governments.”

“The reality is that a huge part of what we see is that [in the past] failed policies like residential schools left a disproportionate number of Indigenous people vulnerable to the ravages of addictions. And the only way for us to find a solution is to have the full participation and engagement of the leaders of those people.”

He said, “A challenge for Indigenous Peoples in Canada has never been that Indigenous Peoples don’t know the solutions. Absolutely we do. The challenge has been that we didn’t have access to the resources and to the decision-making tables to make that happen.”

Carney said that previous government and community efforts to address homelessness have been “inadequately resourced, poorly co-ordinated, and not sustained.”

He said it’s “imperative” that this new strategy succeeds.”

“In Canada, we know we’re not perfect, but we always strive to be good,” Carney said. “We do things because they’re right, not because they’re easy. Ending homelessness is hard; it’s good, and it’s right. And it will require more than compassion.

“It will require ambition, execution, and partnership amongst all levels of government with contributions from philanthropy and business,” Carney added.

There was no determined answer when it came to where most of the 2,000 planned units will be built, but the first 373 are currently being developed inside of Wehwehneh Bahgahkinahgohn, formerly known as the Hudson’s Bay Building, just down the street from the Manitoba Legislature.

The building was acquired by the SCO in 2022, and is scheduled to be complete in 2028. Funding is supported through a partnership with True North.

Jamil Mahmood, the executive director of Main Street Project, a major non-profit addictions treatment centre and homeless shelter, said that additional housing would be useful anywhere in the downtown core.

The organization’s emergency shelter on Main Street has been affected by several fires in 2026, beginning in January. The most recent was on Oct. 31.

Money from this announcement will help refurbish the building, which housed over 2,900 people in 2025, according to its annual report.

“We know that’s where people are, we know that’s where the resources are, so the more you can put housing up where resources are is great,” he said.

“I think over time we can definitely expand that … from the core area to different areas, but then you also need to move resources to those places,” he added. “So we believe a decentralized model would work over time, but right now we have resources downtown.”

Mahmood said “the big thing,” however, is the inclusion of wrap-around support on-site, and staff who can remain there to help.

“I think that helps a lot of people really feel more comfortable with this housing,” he said. “And also, the reverse …

title: Misiones: intimidación policial a la comunidad Mbya Guaraní Kuaray Amba
content:
Denuncian un accionar continuo de hostigamiento de la fuerza policial sobre la comunidad del pueblo Mbya Guaraní Kuaray Amba, en Puerto Iguazú, y advierten que puede ser la preparatoria de un nuevo desalojo ilegal como el que sufrió Puente Quemado II, en la misma provincia.


Compartimos el comunicado del Equipo Misiones de Pastoral Aborigen (EMiPA):


Kuaray Amba: la intimidación como mecanismo de control


La persecución a Kuaray Amba, en Puerto Iguazú, sumó este martes un nuevo capítulo. Alrededor de 15 efectivos policiales llegaron a la Comunidad, bajo la misma modalidad que en las ocasiones anteriores: sin previo aviso y solicitando información.


Resulta llamativo el despliegue de tantos efectivos policiales si lo que necesitan es solamente recabar algunos datos. ¿O será que buscan intimidar a la Comunidad y preparar el terreno para un posible desalojo forzado, como ocurrió en Puente Quemado II?


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Intimidacion-policial.mp4


Video: EMiPA


“Trajeron una nota, pero no estaba dirigida a la Comunidad ni a mí”, explicó Lidio Rivarola, mburuvicha. El documento que exhibieron era un oficio judicial dirigido al jefe de la Comisaría Seccional Primera de Puerto Iguazú. Allí se hace referencia a una denuncia por una presunta intrusión en terrenos del Estado provincial y se ordena realizar una inspección policial para relevar la ocupación actual e histórica del territorio.


“Querían datos de la gente, pero se los negamos. ¿Para qué los quieren? Dicen que es para llevar al juez. Nos amenazan con el desalojo”, aseguró Lidio.


Hasta el momento, no existe una orden de desalojo ni una imputación contra integrantes de la Comunidad. Además, ya se presentó un escrito ante la Dirección de Asuntos Guaraníes, en el que la Comunidad dejó clara su postura: no va a abandonar el territorio.

title: Students in Rojava protest for education in Kurdish
content:
Students in several cities across the Cizîrê region of Rojava demonstrated against restrictions on Kurdish-language education imposed by the Syrian transitional government. In Qamişlo, Girkê Legê and Rimêlan, they took to the streets to demand recognition of Kurdish as a language of instruction and guarantees for the right to education in their mother tongue. The protests were sparked by a decision made by the Syrian Ministry of Education in late August to limit Kurdish-language instruction in schools to three hours per week.


In Qamişlo, students from the Hetîn and Şehîd Jîr schools participated in a demonstration that began at the Şehîd Osman Sabrî intersection in the Hilêliyê neighborhood. From there, the protesters marched to the regional administrative headquarters in the city center. During the march, they chanted slogans demanding recognition of their mother tongue and opposing restrictions on education.


Students: Our language is our identity


Outside the regional administrative headquarters, Diyana Sonchan and Viyan Mehmûd read out a joint statement in Kurdish and Arabic on behalf of the students. In the statement, they condemned the Ministry of Education’s decision to reduce the number of hours allocated to Kurdish-language instruction.


“Kurdish is not merely another school subject, but an expression of the identity, culture, history and existence of the Kurdish people. Restricting Kurdish-language instruction therefore goes far beyond a change to the school timetable. It directly infringes upon the linguistic and cultural rights of the Kurdish population,” the statement read.


The students called on the Ministry of Education and the Syrian transitional government to recognize the linguistic and educational rights of the Kurdish people. They also demanded guarantees of equal rights for all communities in Syria.


Protests in Girkê Legê and Rimêlan


Students in Girkê Legê and Rimêlan also organized joint protests. The demonstrators marched to the school administration building in Rimêlan, chanting slogans demanding the right to education in Kurdish. Participants declared that education in one’s mother tongue was a fundamental, non-negotiable right. They announced that they would continue their protests as long as restrictions on Kurdish-language education remained in place.


The latest demonstrations mark a continuation of protests against the education policies of the Syrian transitional government. Since early September, students and families in various cities across Rojava and Northeast Syria have been protesting against the reduction of Kurdish-language instruction to three hours per week.

content:
Dossier


„

Seit Dienstag besetzen knapp 30 Anhänger der Gruppe „Shut Elbit Down“ eine Grünfläche am Safranberg in Ulm. Angereist aus dem gesamten Bundesgebiet, haben sie ihre Zelte unmittelbar vor der Niederlassung des israelischen Rüstungskonzerns „Elbit Systems Deutschland“ aufgeschlagen. Wie lange sie dort verharren werden, lassen die Aktivisten bewusst offen. „Wenn es sein muss, bleiben wir einen Monat“, kündigt eine Teilnehmerin an. Das Ziel der Demonstranten: die Schließung der Ansiedlung des Großkonzerns in Ulm

…“

Bericht von Dennis Bacher vom 25.04.2025 in schwaebische.de


 („„Wenn es sein muss, bleiben wir einen Monat“: Demonstranten belagern israelisches Unternehmen“) mit Video und Fotos – siehe mehr zu den Protesten und deren Folgen:


Grundrechtekomitee beobachtet den Prozess gegen „Ulm 5“ wegen Sabotage gegen Elbit: Vorsitzende Richterin verweigert den Angeklagten grundlegendes


RAV zum Prozess gegen die »Ulm 5«: Unabhängige Beobachtung erheblich erschwert


„

Der Republikanische Anwältinnen- und Anwälteverein e.V. (RAV) kritisiert nach Prozessbeobachtung das Verbot handschriftlicher Notizen sowie Einschränkungen der Kommunikation zwischen Angeklagten und Verteidigung. Eine unabhängige Beobachtung der Verhandlungsführung werde erheblich erschwert.


Der RAV hat am 25.09.2026 die Hauptverhandlung gegen die sogenannten »Ulm 5« vor der 18. Großen Strafkammer des Landgerichts Stuttgart beobachtet. Nach Einschätzung des Prozessbeobachters Rechtsanwalt Yunus Ziyal erschweren die Bedingungen im Hochsicherheitssaal des OLG-Prozessgebäudes in Stuttgart-Stammheim sowohl eine unabhängige Dokumentation des Verfahrens als auch die effektive Wahrnehmung von Verteidigungsrechten. (…)


Kritisch bewertet der RAV zudem, dass eine von der Verteidigung auf eigene Kosten beschäftigte Protokollkraft nicht zugelassen wurde. Gerade in umfangreichen Strafverfahren könne eine solche Unterstützung wesentlich für eine effektive Verteidigungsarbeit sein. Ein pauschaler Ausschluss bedürfe daher einer konkreten und nachvollziehbaren Begründung.


Kommunikation mit der Verteidigung erheblich erschwert


Besonders problematisch ist aus Sicht des RAV die räumliche Situation der Angeklagten. Diese saßen während der Hauptverhandlung getrennt von ihren Verteidiger*innen in einem Glaskasten. Eine Kommunikation war lediglich über Telefonhörer möglich. Da Teile der Verhandlung verdolmetscht wurden, mussten sich die Angeklagten nach den Beobachtungen von Ziyal zeitweise entscheiden, ob sie über Kopfhörer der Übersetzung folgen oder über den Telefonhörer mit ihrer Verteidigung kommunizieren wollten. Beides gleichzeitig war technisch nicht möglich. (…)


»Was in Stammheim vor sich geht, ist zutiefst besorgniserregend. Es ist sehr fraglich, ob diese Prozesssituation noch mit rechtsstaatlichen Grundsätzen zu vereinbaren ist«, resümiert Rechtsanwalt Ziyal.


Der RAV fordert deshalb:


– eine verhältnismäßige Ausgestaltung sitzungspolizeilicher Maßnahmen


– die Zulassung handschriftlicher Notizen für Prozessbeobachter*innen


– eine konkrete Prüfung der Zulassung von Protokollkräften sowie


– technische und räumliche Bedingungen, die es den Angeklagten ermöglichen, der Verdolmetschung zu folgen und zugleich vertraulich mit ihrer Verteidigung zu kommunizieren

…“

Pressemitteilung vom 10.11.2026

author: Assembly in memory of Kyriakos Xymitiris and in solidarity with the persecuted of the Ambelokipi case
title: To the second anniversary of the death of our comrade Kyriakos Xymitiris
content:
[german below]
On 31 October 2024, two years ago, the anarchist Kyriakos Xymitiris lost his life. We want to keep remembering him and therefore publicly commemorated this anniversary together in front of NY/ Bethanien, here in Berlin, where he was active for many years.


Kyriakos died as an armed guerrilla fighter. During his years in Germany from 2015 to 2021 he was first and foremost a sociable and politically active Berliner. Soon after his arrival, he became part of the anarchist movement and initially contributed to grassroots struggles against the state and capital. Before long, he became fully involved in the local militant movement and was a familiar face at events, demonstrations and struggles on the streets.


In 2021, he returned to Athens, where he was born and raised. There, he continued what he had begun in Berlin, following his imaginative and cheerful path towards a struggle in which personal risk becomes secondary to the importance of the goal. In this context, it is understandable that his political analysis, the many street battles and the violent repression eventually led him to the decision to take up arms and familiarise himself with explosives. Looking at the history of the movement, particularly the more recent Greek movement, this decision was by no means purely individual, as many people before him had already chosen armed struggle, and many after him will do so as well.


On 31 October 2024, tragedy struck. An explosive charge that Kyriakos was handling detonated in his hands and killed him.


“Kyriakos Xymitiris, one of us!” is a slogan that has been shouted in many places around the world since that day. Today, Kyriakos‘ name stands for the continuity of struggles for freedom, even in places conceived as the peaceful hinterland of white imperialism. Kyriakos fell on the margins of Europe during a period of upheaval, in which war and genocide are openly and controversially discussed here. His decision not only to participate in the discourse but instead to sharpen the sword is remarkable. But it is also challenging. Challenging for those in power, who constantly declare resistance dead. But also, and much more importantly, challenging for the oppressed, who find themselves stumbling in the dark along the endless paths of their search for solidarity.


As the assembly in memory of Kyriakos Xymitiris, which organised the gathering on October 31, we find ourselves, two years after the difficult loss of a valued comrade for many of us, facing the question of how we want to remember Kyriakos in the future. What significance do his decisions and his death hold for the movement here in Berlin?


These are questions that must be answered by that part of society which wants to overthrow the system and build a free and solidaristic life in its place. We were not many here in the commemoration, but the protests and riots, conscientious objection to military service, strikes and sabotage spreading across the world show that the struggle continues. In the demonstrations which took place alongside our gathering, the flame of action and the warmth of solidarity, for which Kyriakos fought for many years here in Berlin, continue to live on. In every emerging revolt, in everyday acts of resistance and in every uprising that will hopefully soon take place in Berlin again, Kyriakos himself lives on.


Perhaps the memory of Kyriakos will help the new movement prepare itself for the system’s counterattacks. Perhaps his example will contribute to arming both thoughts and actions in such a way that temporary uprisings become a permanent condition, in which the armed force of the state is pushed back further and further, and the warmongers and exploiters can no longer live without fear.


On this second anniversary, we contributed to preserving Kyriakos‘ memory by gathering in a place that holds significance for grassroots struggles in Berlin. Kyriakos himself attended many meetings at NewYorck, and this place was also a regular starting point for him to head out into the streets of Kreuzberg.


Also, NewYorck is connected to our comrade Nicole, who lived and was active there until her death in 2023, as well as to our comrade Devran, who lived and was active on Adalbertstraße until her death in 2025. Both were militant figures whose stories intersected with Kyriakos’s for several years.

content:
İstanbul Kadıköy Kaymakamlığı, TOBB ETÜ yurdunda yaşamını yitiren 19 yaşındaki trans kadın Arya için adalet talebiyle yapılmak istenen eylemi yasakladı.


“Arya’ya Ne Oldu?” İnisiyatifi’nin bugün Kadıköy Süreyya Operası önünde düzenlemek istediği eylem öncesinde polis, LGBTİ+’ların etrafını sardı.


Gazeteci Yusuf Çelik'in aktardığı bilgilere göre, bir süre polisle görüşen LGBTİ+’lar, eylemi gerçekleştirmeden alandan ayrıldı.


Kaymakamlık açıklaması


Kadıköy Kaymakamlığı, TOBB ETÜ yurdunda yaşamını yitiren 19 yaşındaki trans kadın Arya için adalet arayan "Arya'ya Ne Oldu?" İnisiyatifi'nin bugün Kadıköy'de yapacağı eylemi yasakladı. Video: @21yusufcelk https://t.co/Of4HXkLOAP


— bianet (@bianetorg_)

November 8, 2026


Çelik'in aktardığı bilgiye göre, Kadıköy Kaymakamlığı, yasak kararını 2911 Sayılı Toplantı ve Gösteri Yürüyüşleri Kanunu ile 5442 Sayılı İl İdaresi Kanunu’na dayandırdı.


Kaymakamlığın açıklamasında, “İntihar değil cinayet! 19 yaşında TOBB ETÜ yurdunda intihara sürüklenerek katledilen Arya’nın hesabını sormak için sokaklardayız!” sloganıyla yapılması planlanan eylemin toplumda infial uyandırabileceği ve “toplumsal iç barışı tehdit edebileceği” öne sürüldü.


Açıklamada ayrıca eyleme katılacak gruplarla yurttaşlar arasında provokatif olaylar yaşanabileceği iddia edildi.


Kaymakamlık, 8 Kasım saat 00.00’dan itibaren bir gün süreyle ilçe genelindeki tüm açık alanlarda basın açıklaması, yürüyüş, oturma eylemi, miting ve benzeri etkinliklerin yanı sıra bu etkinliklere yönelik çağrı yapılmasını, bildiri dağıtılmasını ve stant açılmasını da yasakladı.


Yasak kararı, bugün saat 16.50’de kamuoyuna duyuruldu.


Ne olmuştu?


TOBB Ekonomi ve Teknoloji Üniversitesi (TOBB ETÜ) İngiliz Dili ve Edebiyatı Bölümü öğrencisi 19 yaşındaki trans kadın Arya, 13 Nisan’da üniversitenin yurdunda yaşamını yitirmişti.


Arya’nın ölümünün ardından arkadaşları ve üniversiteli LGBTİ+ toplulukları, olayın tüm yönleriyle aydınlatılması talebiyle “Arya’ya Ne Oldu İnisiyatifi”ni kurdu. İnisiyatif, Arya’nın eğitim ve yurt yaşamı boyunca sözlü, fiziksel ve dijital şiddete maruz bırakıldığını, yurt yönetimi ve bazı öğrenciler tarafından hedef gösterildiğini açıklamıştı.


Soruşturmada Arya’nın telefon ve bilgisayar gibi temel dijital materyallerinin henüz incelenmediğine dikkat çeken inisiyatif, ölümün yalnızca bireysel bir karar olarak değerlendirilmemesi gerektiğini vurgulamıştı. İnisiyatif, sistematik transfobinin ve kurumsal ihmallerin de soruşturulmasını talep etmişti.

author: Kate Sharpley
title: We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years : Travels of a Protest Poem
content:
As ‘We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years’ this poem is possibly the most widely reprinted item from Freedom.

In September 1893 the London anarchist newspaper Freedom : A Journal of Anarchist Communism published a poem called ‘A Humble Reminder : To the Propertied Classes’, credited to ‘N.’[1] It’s an anti-capitalist protest, lamenting the ‘workers’ dead’ whose deaths enriched those ‘propertied classes’. It rails at the rich ‘We have fed you all for a thousand years, / And you hail us still unfed’. I do not know who ‘N.’ was, though they seem to be connected to the Freedom milieu. Freedom had published another poem by them, ‘The Pet Voter’, in August 1892.[2] Max Nettlau used the same initial when writing in Freedom in June 1891; the Fabian socialist Edith Nesbit had a poem ‘A Word For The Children’ in Freedom in February 1891 (‘The right to give help is your own, / The right to claim it theirs.’) Neither seems a convincing candidate for the authorship of this poem. The Kipling connection

‘N.’ introduced their poem by saying it was ‘slightly altered from Rudyard Kipling’s Ode in praise of English Enterprise.’ That’s a reference to Kipling’s ‘Song of the Dead’ published four months earlier in The English Illustrated Magazine (May 1893). ‘N.’s address to the propertied classes ‘For if blood be the price of England’s wealth, / Good God, we ha’ paid in full’ rewrites Kipling’s address to the sea ‘If blood be the price of admiralty, / Lord God, we ha’ paid in full!’.[3] The ‘Humble Reminder’ changes Kipling’s poem – but leans heavily upon it. Mark Leier said ‘strictly speaking the poem is not a parody of Kipling’s poem but a re-working of the words based on the original verse and meter.’[4] It reminds me of Utah Philips’ comment on IWW songmaking: ‘The Wobblies liked to steal the hymn tunes ‘cos they were pretty and change the words so they made more sense.’[5]

The connection to Kipling persisted. He was credited in many of the reprints (inevitable, perhaps, given that the author remained unknown and their debt to Kipling was clear). There were even articles discussing what it would mean if the poem were by Kipling.[6] Reprinted and recited

Once printed, it was always possible for the poem to reappear, and this one spread beyond the anarchist press, becoming a standard of labour movement papers. The title often changed, varying from ‘The Cry of Toil’ to ‘The Capitalist’. Just as the connection to Kipling is sometimes there and sometimes not, the text varies between the poetic ‘ha’’ to the everyday ‘have’.

Apparently a version was published in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania in 1895.[7] The Portland anarchist newspaper The Firebrand reprinted the poem (anonymously) as ‘The Workers Outcry’ in 1897.[8] Changes had been made to Americanise the text: instead of pounds the third line talks of ‘there’s never a dollar of all your wealth’.

Sometimes you can read about the poem’s life off the printed page. In May 1897 Miss Olive Keep recited ‘We have fed you all for a thousand years’ at a gathering of the Socialist Labor Party. [9]. In August 1899, The Carpenter, a union journal for ‘Carpenters, Stair Builders, Machine Wood Workers, Planing Mill Men, and Kindred Interests’ reprinted the ‘Firebrand version’ (with credit).[10] In 1904 the poem reappeared as ‘The Price of England’s Wealth’ in Glasgow’s The Voice of Labour.[11] This version talks of ‘sovereigns’ rather than ‘pounds’ or ‘dollars’ but there are other changes: I can’t tell if it’s rewritten from the Freedom or Firebrand version.

The anarchist journal Mother Earth (‘published every 15th of the month’) reprinted ‘The Cry of Toil’ (credited to Kipling) in April 1908.[12] On April 18, 1908 it appeared in the IWW’s Industrial Union Bulletin (also credited to Kipling).[13] Once the poem was reprinted in the IWW songbook, and was later put to music (‘about 1916’ by Rudolf von Liebich), it was firmly established as a classic of working class protest.

In November 1913 strikers in Auckland used a line from the poem on their banner during the 1913 Waterfront Strike: ‘If blood be the price of your cursed wealth, good God we have bought it fair’.[14] It’s not often we get the names of people who helped circulate the text but ‘Gordon’ suggested it (as ‘The Workers’ Answer’) in the 1917 compilation New songs for Butte Mining Camp.[15]

As ‘We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years’ this poem is possibly the most widely reprinted item from Freedom. In March 1969 it was reprinted …

author: Anne Marxze Umil
title: Trump out! | Progressive groups launch 12 days of protest
content:
Photo by Emman Capones/Pinoy Weekly

We don’t want this lunatic to come to our country. He is a mass murderer who has initiated wars around the world, led by and benefiting the US.

Progressive groups launch 12 days of protest as the visit of US President Donald Trump to the Philippines approaches.

“Trump is not welcome here in the Philippines, he is not welcome anywhere in the world,” said International League of Peoples’ Struggles-Philippines Secretary General Arnold Padilla in a press conference on Wednesday, November 4.

Trump is scheduled to visit the Philippines on November 16 to sign the Pax Silica initiative also in time for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit.

“Under the banner of Trump Out, we shall hold daily actions ranging from rallies, indoor assemblies, public forums, pickets, concerts, teach-ins, camp-outs, and vigils aimed to express the Filipino people’s strong objection to Trump’s visit,” Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) Chairperson Teddy Casiño said.

Casiño added in Filipino, “Trump represents the largest imperialist power, which sows war, terror, oppression, and plunder across the world. This includes military aggression against Iran, support for genocide, the imposition of economic sanctions and intervention in Venezuela, Cuba, and other countries; military escalation in the Philippines and across the Asia-Pacific; and brutal repression of immigrants and critics within his own country.”

For Ana Marie Nemenzo of the Network Opposed to Pax Silica, Trump should be declared as persona non grata and barred from entering the country.

“We don’t want this lunatic to come to our country. He is a mass murderer who has initiated wars around the world, led by and benefiting the US. This shows that imperialism remains very much alive and must be opposed because it poses a major threat to the planet and endangers the lives of ordinary people around the world,” she added.

Nemenzo said the Philippines has not been truly free. She said since the so-called independence in 1946, the Americans have kept the Philippines tied to the U.S. economy. She also criticized the presence of soldiers and its equipment in the country and urged the public to join the movement to drive U.S. military forces out of the country.

Nemenzo also added that Pax Silica will only further tie the Philippines “to an economic framework that primarily benefits powerful countries seeking access to our critical resources.”

“We know that the Philippines is among the most vulnerable countries. The loss of people’s livelihoods must be a paramount concern,” she added, saying that her organization, Women’s Health is one in the campaign against Pax Silica.

For Pastor Allan Sarte, secretary general of Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association, Trump is the number one enabler of (then Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu that killed 70,000 citizens of Gaza, more than 20,000 of which are children. “We cannot in conscience welcome Trump in the Philippines,” he said.

Not only the Filipinos are rejecting Trump, Bayan said the glaring defeat of Trump’s party in the U.S. midterm elections is a powerful boost to the Trump Out campaign.

“The Democratic Party’s landslide victory, wresting control of both Houses of Congress and defeating Republicans even in traditional strongholds like Texas, Kansas, and South Carolina, is a resounding repudiation of Trump and his rule,” the group said in a statement.

The group said the results of the election is a reflection of the growing disgust and rejection by the American people of Trump’s corrupt, authoritarian, war mongering, racist, anti-immigrant and over all anti-people policies. “They show that even in his own country, Trump faces mounting opposition to his disastrous leadership,” Bayan said.

The group expressed their solidarity with the American people who are resisting Trump’s attacks on their democratic rights, livelihoods, and welfare.

“They see through his collusion with his big corporate backers to enrich himself. They oppose his war on Iran and belligerence towards other countries’ sovereignty,” Bayan said. (RVO)

author: Amy Goodman
title: Palestinian Journalist Speaks Out After Being Released From Israeli Detention
content:
Israel is “using intimidation tactics. They’re trying to get us scared and afraid and isolated,” says Abed Abu Shehadeh.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The prominent journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh, a Palestinian citizen of Israel, has been released from Israeli custody after five days in detention. He was arrested on Wednesday by armed police and Shin Bet agents who conducted a nighttime raid on his home in the Israeli city of Jaffa. Abu Shehadeh’s detention was related to his reporting on the October 27 Israeli election and the role of Palestinian political parties. Ahead of the election, he interviewed Azmi Bishara, a Palestinian intellectual and former member of the Israeli Knesset who has lived in exile in Qatar since fleeing Israel amid allegations that he aided Hezbollah during the 2006 Lebanon war. Israeli authorities detained Abu Shehadeh on suspicion of “contacting a foreign agent,” in connection to his interview with Bishara.

“Men with ski masks knock on your door at 11 at night. They tell you that they have an arrest warrant. They raid the house. They wake your wife, your children,” says Shehadeh. “It tells how messianic and dangerous the extreme right in Israel has become, willing to use this unprecedented power against journalists.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. I’m Amy Goodman, with Juan González.

The prominent Palestinian journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh has been released from Israeli custody after five days in detention. Azmi Bishara has lived in exile in Doha since being accused of aiding Hezbollah during the 2006 Lebanon war.

The legal rights organization Adalah, which represents Palestinian citizens of Israel, said, quote, “The message to Palestinian citizens is unmistakable: a public conversation with a political figure can land you in a cell. This is political persecution carried out through criminal law,” they said.

Abed Abu Shehadeh hosts the Arabic-language podcast Al-Midan and writes for several publications, including +972 Magazine. He recently came here to New York to speak at an event hosted by Jewish Currents.

We thank you so much for being with us as you join us from Yaffa, from Jaffa. If you can start off by saying what happened? Describe what happened to you. It was after also you got back from New York from this Jewish Currents conference.

title: Muratakan: Lack of concrete steps undermines public trust in the process
content:
Yunus Muratakan, Co-Chair of the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) in Diyarbakır (Amed), spoke about the resolution of the Kurdish question and the ongoing peace process, drawing attention to its historical background, legal guarantees, participation in democratic politics and the importance of social reckoning. Muratakan said that the Kurdish question could not be addressed solely through security-oriented policies, emphasizing that a lasting solution would only be possible through the recognition of democratic rights and the establishment of constitutional guarantees.


 


Muratakan discussed the historical development of the Kurdish question, saying that the centralized and uniform approach to governance that emerged with the founding of the Republic restricted the rights of different identities, languages and cultures. He stated that this approach, institutionalized through the 1924 Constitution, paved the way for policies of denial and repression targeting Kurdish identity and cultural rights. Muratakan added that restrictions on democratic expression, organization and political participation contributed to the emergence of the armed conflict.


'A process without a legal framework cannot become permanent'


Muratakan said that the period of armed conflict had imposed heavy human, economic and social costs on Turkey, recalling that tens of thousands of people had lost their lives, villages had been burned and evacuated, and forced displacement and serious human rights violations had occurred.


Muratakan also discussed peace and dialogue initiatives that emerged from the 1990s onwards, noting that the peace process launched in 2013 had received significant public support. He described the work of the Wise Persons Committee, the participation of political parties in discussions and public support as important achievements of the process. Muratakan said that Turkey had entered another period of intense conflict following the collapse of the process in 2015.


Muratakan stressed that past experiences offered important lessons, saying, "A process may begin through political will, but it cannot become permanent without legal guarantees. Any process that lacks a legal framework remains vulnerable to provocations and political interference."


'The process must move towards building positive peace'


Muratakan described the developments following the 27 February call as the beginning of a new era, saying that the declaration of a ceasefire, the decision to dissolve the organization and steps towards disarmament were significant. He also noted that the legal regulation introduced in Parliament represented an important beginning but contained shortcomings in its scope and content.


Muratakan said, "At this point, attention must be drawn to the DDR mechanism used in international conflict resolution experiences. Disarmament, demobilization and reintegration must be addressed as an integrated process. It is crucial to establish legal and institutional arrangements that enable people who have participated in armed struggle to reintegrate into social life and democratic politics. Negative peace means the end of armed conflict. Positive peace, however, requires addressing the structural problems that caused the conflict, guaranteeing rights and freedoms, and establishing a democratic social order. What we need today is a process that does not remain limited to negative peace but also builds positive peace."


Muratakan also criticized the scope of the legal regulation introduced in Parliament, saying that a step, albeit limited, had been taken towards seeking a solution through legal means with an organization that had waged an armed struggle against the government in Turkey's history.


Muratakan drew attention to shortcomings in the regulation's scope, saying, "For the first time in the history of the Republic of Turkey, a very small step has been taken towards recognizing through law an organization that has engaged in armed struggle, an insurgent organization, and resolving the rebellion through legal means. The fact that the law covers only a particular group involved in armed struggle, while excluding intentional homicide and related offenses, as well as people who were investigated before 2005, is a serious shortcoming. This process is also not entirely consistent with the conventional DDR processes implemented around the world."

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "We Have to Be Brave": Palestinian Journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh Speaks Out After Israeli Detention
content:
The prominent journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh, a Palestinian citizen of Israel, has been released from Israeli custody after five days in detention. He was arrested on Wednesday by armed police and Shin Bet agents who conducted a nighttime raid on his home in the Israeli city of Jaffa. Abu Shehadeh’s detention was related to his reporting on the October 27 Israeli election and the role of Palestinian political parties. Ahead of the election, he interviewed Azmi Bishara, a Palestinian intellectual and former member of the Israeli Knesset who has lived in exile in Qatar since fleeing Israel amid allegations that he aided Hezbollah during the 2006 Lebanon war. Israeli authorities detained Abu Shehadeh on suspicion of “contacting a foreign agent,” in connection to his interview with Bishara.


“Men with ski masks knock on your door at 11 at night. They tell you that they have an arrest warrant. They raid the house. They wake your wife, your children,” says Shehadeh. “It tells how messianic and dangerous the extreme right in Israel has become, willing to use this unprecedented power against journalists.”

title: Spagna: “Contro il rentismo finanziario, il capitale e i suoi governi”. Intervista a una lavoratrice verso lo sciopero generale dell’11 novembre
content:
In 

Spagna

 oggi, martedì 10 novembre, 24 ore di sciopero blocco dei macchinisti dei treni.


da

Radio Onda d’Urto


L’astensione dal lavoro, con un’adesione quasi totale, riguarda Renfe, l’ente ferroviario pubblico, ed è stato proclamato dal sindacato Semaf per chiedere il rispetto degli impegni sulla sicurezza ferroviaria, dopo le stragi 2026 di Adamuz (Cordoba) e di Urda (Toledo) sulla linea ad alta velocità Madrid-Siviglia, costate complessivamente 116 vittime.


A febbraio 2026, dopo il primo schianto vicino a Cordoba, i macchinisti avevano concordato con il ministero dei Trasporti, Renfe e Adif, l’ente di gestione delle infrastrutture ferroviarie, una serie di misure. Il sindacato denuncia però “il mancato avvio dei gruppi di lavoro incaricati di introdurre le nuove norme, protocolli di emergenza e procedure operative”. La mobilitazione proseguirà giovedì 12 novembre con tre fasce di sciopero, mentre per domani, 

mercoledì 11 novembre, sarà sciopero generale

 in tutta la Spagna con l’intero panorama sindacale, l’inquilinato resistente e i movimenti sociali e politici di base. “Contro il rentismo finanziario, il capitale e i suoi governi” la parola d’ordine delle realtà più combattive nella Penisola Iberica.


Radio Onda d’Urto si trova in Spagna con Felipe, nostro inviato, per seguire l’11N e la huelga general. Oggi, martedì 10 novembre, vi proponiamo la corrispondenza con Felipe dal quartiere La Latina – Puerta del Ángel, nel cuore popolare di Madrid, con l’intervista a una lavoratrice durante una delle iniziative in preparazione dello sciopero generale.

title: Cafer Mahiroğlu soruşturması: 7 gözaltı
content:
Halk TV'ye kayyım atanmasından önce kanalın Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı olan Cafer Mahiroğlu hakkında yürütülen soruşturmada ikinci dalga operasyon düzenlendi.


İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı'nın talimatıyla İstanbul, İzmir, Ankara ve Eskişehir'de yapılan eş zamanlı operasyonlarda 7 kişi gözaltına alındı, bir kişi hakkında yakalama çalışması başlatıldı.


Savcılığın açıklamasına göre soruşturma, 2021 yılında İzmir'de kurulan BUSTECH Araç Bakım Onarım Hizmetleri AŞ üzerinden yürütülen para transferlerine odaklanıyor. Şirketin Cafer Mahiroğlu'na ait olduğu ve paravan olarak kullanıldığı iddia edildi.


Savcılık, BUSTECH aracılığıyla Halk TV, Özdemir Üç Tekstil, Mahiroğlu'nun diğer şirketleri ve kişisel hesaplarına para aktarıldığını öne sürdü. Yurt içi ve yurt dışı SWIFT işlemleriyle gerçekleştirilen transferlerin ardından paranın farklı hesaplar arasında kısa süre içinde birden fazla kez dolaşıma sokularak aklanmaya çalışıldığı iddia edildi.


Açıklamada, Halk TV'nin de bu süreçte "topluma karşı kalkan olarak kullanıldığı" ileri sürüldü.


Soruşturma dosyasında gizli tanıkların ve etkin pişmanlık hükümlerinden yararlanan kişilerin beyanları da yer aldı.


Savcılığın iddiasına göre Cafer Mahiroğlu'nun Halk TV'yi satın almasının ardından kanalın ekonomik sıkıntı yaşamaması amacıyla İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesi'nden araç bakım ve onarım, temizlik işleri ve maske alımı ihaleleri alındı.


İhalelerin alınması ve hakediş ödemelerinin yapılması karşılığında ilgili kişilere elden döviz ve Türk lirası cinsinden rüşvet verildiği öne sürüldü. Savcılık, iddiaların gizli tanık ve etkin pişmanlık beyanlarına dayandığını belirtti.


Operasyonda gözaltına alınan 7 kişi ile firari olduğu bildirilen bir kişinin isimleri şöyle: Ramazan Tezcan (Eski İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesi Genel Sekreteri), Filiz Bulut (BUSTECH büro memuru), Emre Kaya (ESBAKIM adlı şirketin sahibi, firari), İbrahim Seyfittinoğlu (Maker ve Zafer İnşaat ortağı), Murat Topuz (BUSTECH proje yöneticisi), Haluk Harun Tuzsuzoğlu (Eski İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesi Makine İkmal Daire Başkanı), Mehmet Meral (İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesi Makine İkmal Daire Başkanlığı kontrolörü) ve İbrahim Tuncol (başka bir dosyadan tutuklu, eski İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesi Makine İkmal Daire Başkanı'nın elemanı).


Soruşturmanın ilk dalgasında 14 Ekim'de düzenlenen operasyonda 13 kişi gözaltına alınmış, bunlardan 5'i tutuklanmıştı.


İlk operasyonun ardından Halk TV'ye Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu (TMSF) kayyum olarak atanmış ve kanalın yayınları durdurulmuştu. İkinci dalga operasyon kapsamında 7 kişi gözaltına alınırken, firari şüphelinin yakalanması için çalışmaların sürdüğü bildirildi.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Court to police: Fabricated charges ‘severest, most unmerited punishment’
content:
A Metropolitan Trial Court branch in Manila dismissed a criminal case related to the September 21, 2025 violent police dispersal, affirmed the primacy of the rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly, and cautioned law enforcers against filing unfounded criminal complaints against innocent citizens.


In a decision promulgated on Monday, November 9, 2026, the Court dismissed a criminal case for violation of Article 153 of the Revised Penal Code (Tumults and Other Disturbances) against nine individuals arrested at Mendiola during the September 21, 2025 rally. It was dismissed on demurrer to evidence due to insufficient evidence.


In dismissing the charges, the court ruled:


The prosecution failed to establish the alleged complicity of the nine individuals in the acts constituting the offense. Although the Information alleges conspiracy, it failed to prove that a conspiracy existed.


The Court noted a discrepancy between the allegations in the Information and the supporting affidavits and witness testimonies. The Information charges Tumults and other Disturbance, while the affidavits and testimonies allege facts related to direct assault, which involves different elements.


This discrepancy is significant because, during the inquest proceedings, the nine arrested individuals were initially charged with Tumults, and Direct Assault. The Inquest Prosecutor dismissed the Direct Assault charge and recommended filing a case for Tumults. However, the affidavits submitted to the Court support the dismissed Direct Assault charge and do not support the Tumults case.


The Court also did not give weight to the witness testimonies identifying the nine individuals. The Court found that, given the tense situation and the fact that witnesses were hiding behind shields, they could not possibly make accurate identifications.


The allegations that the nine individuals kicked police officers’ shields and attempted to break the police formation are insufficient to conclude that they engaged in a tumultuous disturbance.


Instead, the Court ruled that the “[V]ery act of pushing and grabbing during a public assembly automatically rises to the level of a serious disturbance. The prosecution must establish, through specific and credible evidence, the nature, gravity, and circumstances of the alleged acts showing that they indeed resulted in the disturbance penalized by law.”


The Court also cited the ruling of the Supreme Court in People vs. Apurado portions of which partly states that:


“It is rather to be expected that more or less disorder will mark the public assembly of the people to protest against grievances whether real or imaginary, because on such occasions feeling is always wrought to a high pitch of excitement, and the greater the grievance and the more intense the feeling, the less perfect, as a rule, will be the disciplinary control of the leaders over their irresponsible followers. But if the prosecution be permitted to seize upon every instance of such disorderly conduct by individual members of a crowd as an excuse to characterize the assembly as a seditious and tumultuous rising against the authorities, then the right to assemble and to petition for redress of grievances would become a delusion and a snare and the attempt to exercise it on the most righteous occasion and in the most peaceable manner would expose all those who took part therein to the severest and most unmerited punishment, if the purposes which they sought to attain did not happen to be pleasing to the prosecuting authorities.”


The Court found no basis to charge the nine individuals with Tumults and other disturbances. It cautioned the police against filing fabricated cases and prosecuting innocent citizens. In its Decision, the Court stated:


“Police officers must bear in mind that the filing of criminal charges against the very citizens they have sworn to serve and protect is a serious matter inherent in every State. It must, however, always be, based on careful assessment; convenience and expediency have no place in requiring a person to answer for criminal liability. To accept otherwise, would be a disservice not only to the accused but also to the cause of justice itself.” #


The post

Court to police: Fabricated charges ‘severest, most unmerited punishment’

 appeared first on

Kodao Productions

author: dev
title: Nouvelle lettre ouverte de prisonniers du 17 octobre 2026
content:
Depuis plusieurs prisons de France, des détenus sont parvenus à rédiger cette seconde lettre ouverte et à nous la transmettre. Dans la continuité

de la première missive que nous avions publiée

, ils appellent à poursuivre la lutte et racontent la manière dont l'administration pénitentiaire les accueille.


Il y a deux semaines, nous vous adressions une première lettre ouverte. Nous prisonniers du 17 octobre 2026 reprenons la parole et sommes rejoint par de nouvelles voix qui s'échappent désormais de plusieurs prisons de France.


Depuis nos cellules et grâce aux échos qui nous arrivent, nous suivons le combat en cours à l'extérieur. La cohésion et la solidarité des différentes forces engagées nous fait chaud au cœur. Et si le pouvoir et ses médias tentent de nous séparer, il faut continuer à nous tenir ensemble.


Une révolution est impossible si ses premières lignes sont isolées. Mais les premières lignes doivent aussi comprendre l'importance des deuxièmes, troisièmes et de toutes les lignes qui suivent et qui garantissent la survie et l'extension du mouvement.


Si nous voulons voir la fin de l'ère Macron et de ce régime qu'il ose encore appeler République, nous devons réunir toutes nos forces pour y parvenir. Blocages, émeutes, manifestations, grèves, batailles médiatiques et institutionnelles sont autant de chemins sur lesquels nous devons marcher et faire front, massivement.


Nous devons mettre toutes nos forces pour faire pencher la balance de notre côté. Leurs prisons ne sont pas assez grandes pour accueillir tous les insurgé.es de ce pays. A Fleury-Merogis, un bâtiment entier a été vidé pour parquer là une cinquantaine d'entre nous. A la Santé, on nous isole pour éviter la contagion révolutionnaire. A Villepinte et à Fresnes, on nous fait subir les pires conditions carcérales pour briser notre élan et notre moral. Mais le pouvoir se trompe en pensant pouvoir nous faire plier.


Ici aussi la colère monte. Nous voyons bien les chiens de garde de CNEWS et BFM s'acharner pendant des semaines entières sur nous tout en taisant les motifs de notre révolte. Nous sommes lucides sur la différence de traitement opérée par ces médias entre nous et un fasciste tueur d'enfant à Trappes. Nous les voyons bégayer pour justifier leur haine de l'autre et pour nier leur culpabilité évidente dans cette atrocité qui a notamment emporté la vie d'un homme et envoyé une fillette de onze ans à l'hôpital. Ils ont tenté de justifier froidement les actes du tueur par des motifs psychiatriques tandis qu'ils pleuraient à chaude larme pour des vitrines brisées. Dans ce pays, il vaut mieux être une vitrine, une paire de Ray-Ban ou un sac Louis Vuitton qu'un enfant agressé, une femme violée ou un noir ou un arabe abattu. Dans ce pays, il vaut mieux être un fasciste qui sème la mort qu'un révolutionnaire qui combat pour la vie.


Alors face à la guerre répressive et idéologique que l'État nous mène, nous appelons à tenir bon. Ce que la macronie fait mine de nous concéder ne trompe personne. Les miettes ne nourriront pas ceux qui viennent pour reprendre la boulangerie. Nous, ici, depuis ces prisons pour pauvres et enragés, nous tenons bons. Notre détermination est intacte et si leur « justice » s'obstine à nous maintenir enfermés, alors nous serons prêts, comme notre camarade Ritchy, à étendre la révolte aux prisons.


Derrière les murs et les barreaux, dans les couloirs froids de ces bâtiments sombres, nous aussi nous entendons de plus en plus souvent ce murmure, celui qui dit que ça ne peut plus durer. Des alliances se sont tissées dans la rue le 17 octobre 2026. Elles ne demandant qu'à être approfondies. Gare à l'État qui pense maîtriser le feu de la colère, il finira par se brûler.


Des prisonniers du 17 octobre

author: Netzwerk Freiheit für alle politische Gefangenen
title: Hintergründe zu Holger Meins, der am 9.11.1974 im Kampf gegen Isolationsfolter gefallen ist
content:
Holger war Filmstudent und in der 67/68-Bewegung aktiv und er wäre am 26.10. 80 Jahre alt geworden. Er schloss sich 1970 der RAF an und und sie begann im Jahr 1972 mit ihrer Mai-Offensive.


In diesem Jahr verschärften die USA ihren ohnehin schon barbarischen Krieg in Vietnam mit der systematischen Bombardierung ziviler Ziele und der Verminung der nordvietnamesischen Häfen, um – wie es ein verantwortlicher General Westmoreland formuliert – dieses Land in die Steinzeit zurückzubomben. Diese Angriffe werden über einen Großrechner im europäischen US-Hauptquartier in Heidelberg koordiniert. Jahrelange erfolglose und mit polizeilichen Mitteln zerschlagene Proteste hatten nicht zum Ende der US-Aggression in Vietnam geführt.


Deshalb ergriff die RAF in diesem Krieg militärisch Partei: Sie griff am 11. Mai 1972 das Hauptquartier des 5. US-Korps in Frankfurt und am 24. Mai das Hauptquartier der US-Army in Heidelberg mit Autobomben an.


In der Erklärung des “Kommandos Petra Schelm” (1) heißt es zur Begründung der Frankfurter Aktion:


„Für die Ausrottungsstrategen von Vietnam sollen Westdeutschland und Westberlin kein sicheres Hinterland mehr sein. Sie müssen wissen, dass ihre Verbrechen am vietnamesischen Volk ihnen neue erbitterte Feinde geschaffen haben, dass es für sie keinen Platz mehr geben wird in der Welt, an dem sie vor den Angriffen revolutionärer Guerilla-Einheiten sicher sein können.“


Am 12. Mai führt die RAF Attacken auf die Polizeihauptquartiere in Augsburg und München durch. Am 16. Mai erfolgt ein Angriff auf den Bundesgerichtshof-Richter Buddenberg. Mit dieser Aktion richtet sich die RAF gegen die Isolationsfolterbedingungen, denen die politischen Gefangenen unterworfen werden:


„Wir verlangen von der Justiz, dass das Leben und die Gesundheit der Gefangenen nicht länger systematisch angegriffen und zerstört werden.“


Am 19. Mai explodieren zwei Bomben im Hamburger Springer-Hochhaus. Trotz rechtzeitiger und dreimaliger telefonischer Warnung vorher, lässt Springer das Gebäude nicht räumen. 17 Arbeiter*innen werden verletzt. Mit diesem Zynismus hatte die RAF nicht gerechnet und übt deshalb Selbstkritik:


„Wir haben Springer nicht als das Schwein eingeschätzt, das er tatsächlich ist.“


Im Juni und Juli desselben Jahres wurde ein Großteil der RAF verhaftet: Ulrike Meinhof, Gudrun Ensslin, Brigitte Mohnhaupt und Irmgard Möller,


Holger wurde am 1.Juni in Frankfurt zusammen mit Andreas Baader und Jan-Carl Raspe verhaftet.


Haft


Holger war bis zu seinem Tod am 9.11.74 vollkommen isoliert, alle Zelle um seine herum waren leergeräumt, jeder Kontakt zu anderen Gefangenen wurden ausgeschlossen. Alle Details zu den Haftbedingungen vom Bundeskriminalamt bestimmt und von der Klassenjustiz in „Beschlüsse“ gefasst.


Nach 2 kollektiven Hungerstreiks 1973 traten die politischen Gefangenen am 13.9.74 in einen neuen Hungerstreik gegen Isolation und Sonderbehandlung, die zum Ziel hat, die revolutionäre Identität zu zerstören.


Über 40 Inhaftierte kämpften gemeinsam gegen diese Folter bis zum 5.2.75.


In dem fast 5 Monate andauernden Hungerstreik Holger Meins starb an Folgen der Zwangsernährung. (9.11.74). Insgesamt 9 politische Gefangene wurden im Knast ermordet.


Die Hinrichtung von Holger Meins war damals der deutlichste Ausdruck dafür, dass die Kriegsführung des Staates gegen die RAF auch nicht am Knast Halt machte. Der Geiselstatus der Gefangenen ist offensichtlich, die Gefangenen sollen zerstört werden, um die Politik der RAF zu ersticken.


Der Kampf geht weiter


Am Tag nach Holger Meins‘ Tod wird der Berliner Kammergerichtspräsident Drenckmann durch ein Kommando der „Bewegung 2. Juni“ erschossen.


Am 24. April 1975 besetzt das RAF-„Kommando Holger Meins“ die deutsche Botschaft in Stockholm. Die Forderung nach Freilassung von 26 politischen Gefangenen unterstreicht das Kommando durch Ultimaten, die es mehrmals verlängert, ohne dass die Bundesregierung darauf eingeht. Nach Ablauf der Ultimaten erschießt das Kommando zunächst den Militärattaché von Mirbach, als ihre Forderungen auch danach nicht erfüllt werden, den Wirtschaftsattaché Hillegaart. Die Polizei stürmt das Gebäude, wobei die vom Kommando installierte Sprengladung durch ein Mobiles Einsatzkommando gezündet wurde. Dabei kommt ein Angehöriger des Kommandos, Ulrich Wessel, ums Leben. Siegfried Hausner erleidet schwere Brandverletzungen, wird aber, obwohl transportunfähig, nach Stammheim geflogen, wo er am 4. Mai an den Folgen der Verletzungen stirbt …

author: Andrew Crocker
title: We’re Asking an Appeals Court to Require a Warrant for ALPR Searches
content:
Today, along with the ACLU, EFF filed an amicus brief in the Sixth Circuit court of appeals in United States v. Sturdivant, a case where police warrantlessly tracked a suspect’s movements using Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) data. Our brief details the vast, interconnected network of ALPRs that constantly track drivers around the country and argues that this tracking is a “search” under the meaning of the Fourth Amendment.

Sturdivant involves a series of robberies in and around Cleveland, Ohio. Using surveillance camera footage, police identified the make, model, and color of the robber’s car, but they did not know its license plate number. After running an open-ended search of two ALPR databases, Flock and ELSAG, officers learned a car belonging to the defendant had been tracked near sites of the robberies, eventually leading to his arrest. Faced with a motion to suppress the ALPR evidence, the district court held that Mr. Sturdivant had no reasonable expectation of privacy in his license plate number because it could be observed by members of the public, and that therefore he had no Fourth Amendment interest in not having his car tracked in public places.

But ALPRs are simply not comparable to observing an individual license plate on a passing car. As we’ve explained in many amicus briefs and in our lawsuits directly challenging ALPR use in San Jose, California and Wisconsin, ALPRs give law enforcement “a virtual time machine to view suspects’, or anyone else’s, past movements (and much more) with just the click of a button.” Just last month, a federal district court agreed and held that ALPRs are a “form of indiscriminate mass surveillance” that can violate the Fourth Amendment.

We hope the Sixth Circuit will reverse the lower court in this case and hold that ALPR searches require a warrant.

author: dev
title: Habiter au corps d'un âne mort ou le chemin de Nietzsche
content:
Dans la continuité des très nombreux articles que nous avons publiés afin de déchiffrer l'Intelligence artificielle, le monde qu'elle avale, celui qu'elle charrie et celui qu'elle produit, nous partageons cette semaine l'épatante découverte d'Olivier Chiran et Pierre Muzin. La première occurrence de l'expression IA reviendrait au célèbre philosophe Friedrich Nietzsche dans le tout aussi célèbre

Ainsi parlait Zarathoustra

, un tiret séparait néanmoins les deux voyelles :

« Braire à tout propos I-A, c'est ce qu'apprennent les ânes et ceux qui en ont l'esprit. »


« Donnez-moi du travail, de la fatigue,


de la douleur et de l'enthousiasme. »


George Sand


1.


Pour savoir précisément où nous en sommes, mais aussi faire face à ce qui nous arrive, alors que l'intelligence artificielle étend son emprise sur le monde et les vies, nous avons besoin d'un sémaphore.


2.


On dit que l'expression « intelligence artificielle » a été lancée par John McCarthy, en 1956, lors de la conférence de Dartmouth, coup d'envoi du programme de recherche consacré à la reproduction algorithmique de la pensée humaine. Soixante-douze ans plus tôt, en 1884, Friedrich Nietzsche, le célèbre philosophe allemand, rédige son grand poème philosophique :

Ainsi parlait Zarathoustra

. Dans la troisième partie de cet ouvrage (trouvée « sous le ciel alcyonien de Nice », dira-t-il), il écrit : « Braire à tout propos I-A, c'est ce qu'apprennent les ânes et ceux qui en ont l'esprit

 [

1

]

. » Première apparition de ces deux lettres, longtemps avant Dartmouth. Évidence de leur rapprochement – en même temps que, d'un simple tiret, de leur mise à distance. On pourrait s'étonner que les traducteurs français (Henri Albert en 1903, Geneviève Bianquis en 1969) aient fait le choix, au lieu du « hi-han » conventionnel, de les conserver telles quelles. Mais le texte allemand dit bien : «

Immer I-A sagen – das lernte allein der Esel, und wer seines Geistes ist

 ! » – Nietzche ayant délibérément fait tomber le

h

 de «

iah

 », braiment de l'âne dans la langue de Goethe. Nous dirons donc, quant à nous, que l'histoire de l'I-A commence à la fin du xixe siècle, lorsqu'un philosophe visionnaire, cheminant à flanc de montagne, a compris qu'on pouvait arracher au cri de l'âne sa puissance d'exclamation intempestive – et qu'il y avait là, pour nous, un grand danger

 [

2

]

.


3.


C'est qu'il y a deux ânes. Gilles Deleuze, commentant les propos de Nietzsche : « On aurait pu croire que l'âne, l'animal qui dit I-A, était l'animal dionysiaque par excellence. En fait, il n'en est rien ; son apparence est dionysiaque, mais toute sa réalité est chrétienne

 [

3

]

. » Le braiment sans son ou ses

h

, c'est cette manière qu'a l'âne de dire toujours oui – mais un faux oui, une fausse affirmation qui ne sait pas dire non, qui ne sait qu'acquiescer face à ce qui est. Bêtise. Démission de la pensée. Obscurantisme. Post-vérité. Positivisme logique. (Margaret Thatcher : «

There is no alternative

 » → TINA : « I-A ! I-A ! ») Toutes choses contre lesquelles, justement, la philosophie s'évertue à lutter. « Le réel tel qu'il est, conclut Deleuze, c'est une idée d'âne. »


4.

author: EDRi
title: Data retention is mass surveillance of people’s phone and internet activity
content:
In 2014, the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) declared mass retention of internet traffic and location data as contrary to the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights. Any proposal for a new EU instrument harmonising data retention must respect the boundaries of CJEU jurisprudence and uphold the rights to privacy, data protection and freedom of expression. Read more in EDRi’s new publication.

It is the legal requirement for internet service providers to retain metadata about their users beyond what is necessary for the provision of the service (e.g. billing or network optimisation and security purposes) and to keep it solely so that it can later be accessed by law enforcement bodies and intelligence services.

Metadata is data generated for the purpose of transmitting content in electronic communications services and networks. This includes mobile numbers of the sender and recipient, the time and duration of a call or an internet session, websites accessed, and the location of mobile devices. On a technical level, metadata is no longer needed once the transmission ends.

Metadata is very revealing about people’s private lives.

Systematic recording of location data will reveal a person’s permanent and temporary places of residence, political and religious preferences (e.g. participation in public demonstrations and religious ceremonies), health status (e.g. visit to a specialised clinic), sexual orientation (e.g. LGBT+ venues), or other sensitive aspects (e.g. visit to a lawyer’s office).

Metadata contains information about social or professional relations with other people (“social graph”).

Usage patterns for website visits and other internet services reveal an enormous amount of information about a person’s interest and state of mind.

Metadata is more revealing than the content of communications, especially because metadata is highly structured, which makes it easy to analyse. Governments can easily profile and categorise entire populations solely based on metadata.

The Court of Justice of the EU rightly described metadata retention as creating a feeling of being under constant surveillance. This has a chilling effect on participation in public life, as individuals restrict their own civil liberties to avoid surveillance.

While data access requests may be specific and targeted, general and indiscriminate data retention treats everyone as a potential suspect. Surveillance without suspicion violates the presumption of innocence, which is an essential right in democratic societies.

Retention of vast amounts of personal data inevitably creates huge vulnerabilities to cyberattacks. Malicious actors can gain access to massive amounts of data and abuse it for identity theft or blackmail.

Data retention severely undermines the possibility of online anonymity. Anonymity is a question of safety for many, even a matter of life or death: investigative journalists, whistleblowers, crime survivors, political opponents, refugees, victims of transnational repression, artists, human rights defenders, and more. It supports the exercise of key fundamental rights such as freedom of expression and the freedom to receive and impart information.

US telecom company AT&T was hacked by an attacker who stole the logs of calls and texts to more than 100 million customers over a six-month period in 2022.

In 2024 the Garda Síochána Ombudsman Commission (Ireland’s police watchdog) accessed journalists’ phone records to identify their sources as part of its own investigation into the Irish police, even though the journalists were not accused of any criminal offence.

In 2013, the Polish Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (CBA) obtained access to billing data of a journalist who had reported on irregularities in the intelligence services. The CBA’s aim was to uncover their source’s identity. The journalist won the case in court, and the CBA published an official apology.

The Berlin Data Protection Authority reported that most cell tower dumps (law enforcement requesting information on all the devices that connected to a particular cell site during a specific time period) by German authorities between 2009 and 2011, when data retention was in place in the country, were unlawful. The German police used this surveillance technique as an everyday investigative tool despite its very intrusive nature, and systematically failed to meet several legal requirements. Data retention enabled this abuse.
