author: Unknown
title: Lilia Folt - On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness
content:
Author

: Lilia Folt

Title

: On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness

Date

: September 27

th

, 2026

Notes

: Originally published in

Dissonant Times

, a grassroots journalism and counter-info project from the Willamette Valley of Oregon.

Source

: Dissonant Times, Retrieved on 11/5/2026 from https://dissonanttimes.org/anarchic-reflections-on-anti-surveillance-mindfulness/


 Surveillance has become a ubiquitous feature of everyday life in America. Cameras watch us from businesses and homes, from bus stops, from cars, from traffic lights. Bluetooth trackers ping our smartphones as we pass by, mapping our movements. The phones themselves illuminate our paths through society by continuously pinging cell towers, providing our cell providers our location data, information that is only a subpoena away, if that. In countless ways, we’ve been made to both passively accept and actively participate in our own surveillance. This vast complex of surveillance doesn’t just gather information about us, it also shapes our behaviors, temperaments, and ways of moving through the world. Surveillance molds us down to the level of subjective, sensory, embodied experience. At that same level we can begin to shake off its hold on us and reclaim ourselves. For that, I am offering a practice I’m calling “anti-surveillance mindfulness,” a form of walking meditation that builds mindful awareness of surveillance cameras. This practice, if taken up consistently, opens onto a broader project of transforming our relationship to the places we live in, a project that itself naturally blossoms into materially transforming public space, as self expands to world in the moment-by-moment practice of mindfulness.


Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness


 Readers may or may not be familiar with the Panopticon. Designed by 18

th

 century English liberal Jeremy Bentham, the Panopticon was a model for an institutional building designed so that a single prison guard can watch all the inmates from a central watch tower. The inmates, meanwhile, cannot tell whether or not they are being watched, and therefore could be watched at any moment. To quote Bentham:


 The more constantly the persons to be inspected are under the eyes of the persons who should inspect them, the more perfectly will the purpose of the establishment have been attained. (...) This being impossible, the next thing to be wished for is, that, at every instant, seeing reason to believe as much, and not being able to satisfy himself to the contrary, he should

conceive

 himself to be so.


 A lot has changed since the 1700’s, but the disciplinary paradigm of surveillance has remained the same. If anything, it has expanded beyond specific institutions to encompass much of society.


 There are cameras everywhere, and we are being watched, and while we are aware of this, we tend to see it as normal and unremarkable, an inevitability we must resign ourselves to. Consciousness of being surveilled fades into the background, becoming a constant assumption of being watched that we internalize. This surveillance consciousness is running us all the more effectively because it is not distinct, because it is

un

conscious. That is why the first step in anti-surveillance mindfulness is becoming conscious of surveillance.


 Mindfulness is at the same time a means and an end, the seed and the fruit. When we practice mindfulness in order to build up concentration, mindfulness is a seed. But mindfulness itself is the life of awareness: the presence of mindfulness means the presence of life, and therefore mindfulness is also the fruit. — Thích Nhất Hạnh,

The Miracle of Mindfulness


 “Mindfulness” is a practice originating in various sects of Buddhism. The mindfulness practices and concepts I’m familiar with have largely been within the school of Zen Buddhism

[1]

.


 The classic mindfulness practice is watching the breath, and that is a great starting point. Take a breath in, the air entering through your nose, your stomach and chest softly expanding as you inhale. Then exhale through the mouth, the stomach and chest settling back down, gently exhaling for a little longer than your inhale. Repeat this several times, deepening your breaths slightly. From there, start to check in with your body. Notice how it feels to be sitting down, or to be standing if you are standing; notice how it feels to be holding this piece of paper, holding your phone, or looking at your computer, however it is that you are reading …

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: Air Creebec hit by administrative data breach affecting employees and passengers
content:
Air Creebec, a regional Quebec airline owned by the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee, reported a data breach Wednesday affecting both customers and staff.

In a press release, the company announced “an unauthorized intrusion targeting some of its administrative systems.”

The release stresses that the breach did not compromise any systems associated with aircraft, flight operations or flight safety, noting the company’s administrative systems were not connected with aircraft and flight systems, which it said operate independently.

“Initial findings indicate that administrative files were exfiltrated,” states the release. “These files may contain personal information relating mainly to current and former employees, as well as passengers. Others may also contain operational, administrative or financial information related to customers and partners. The review is ongoing.”

Based in the airport of Val d’Or in the Abitibi-Témiscamingue region of western Quebec, roughly 520 kilometres northwest of Ottawa, Air Creebec offers flights to 16 destinations in Quebec and Ontario. The company’s fleet consists of 21 Dash-8 turboprop regional airliners, along with one ATR 72 turboprop air-freighter for cargo, and carries 200,000 passengers per year.

Cybersecurity experts assessing damage

Air Creebec director for Marketing and Business Development Edward Trahan said the breach was identified in October after which company officials immediately brought in cybersecurity experts to analyze the situation.

“They’re currently evaluating what’s going on and what the breach actually contained,” Trahant told APTN News. “The experts are still conducting their review, so there’s no numbers [of victims] at this time that we can give.”

He added that for security reasons, he was not presently willing to name the cybersecurity team currently helping with post-breach recovery.

He said because the attack was designed to go undetected it was hard to determine the date upon which it began, and for how long attackers were able to access Air Creebec’s systems prior to being discovered.

“What I can assure you of is that as soon as [we were] made aware of [it], we acted immediately and did not wait.”

At the moment, Trahant said the attack appeared to have stolen information “related to our employees, past employees too, and maybe even our passengers.”

“But it’s hard to confirm at the moment.”

Company will contact affected parties

He added that a priority for Air Creebec is contacting every one of their staff or customers whose information has been compromised, which cybersecurity experts would undertake to carry out as soon as possible.

“A part of what the cybersecurity experts are doing for us is gathering information to [determine] what kind of protection packages we can provide to people that had their information involved,” said Trahan.

“Those people will be directly contacted in probably the next few days — [but] probably more like [the next] day — about what package they will receive, what protection they’re going to have and how long it’s going to last.”

Trahan said the cybersecurity team was currently in the process of securing all possible intrusion points, but he said the nature of cybersecurity is that 100 per cent protection is impossible.

“It’s just the way of the world,” he said, “but they are closing every possible way to get in and they are getting to the very end of that. As for how they got in initially, we don’t know yet and I don’t want to speculate while the review is still underway.”

Trahan said he and Air Creebec are taking the situation very seriously and are committed to supporting all those affected, and the company said it would be in touch with affected people to offer “appropriate protective measures,” including the possibility of credit-monitoring and identity-protection services.

“Those services will be based on the nature of the information exposed and the risks that were identified,” he said. “So individuals that are eligible to receive this protection will be informed directly and will be given a list of steps to follow in the very near future.”

Jesse joined APTN as a producer after 16 years as a print and web journalist. During seven of those years, he covered the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee for community newsmagazine The Nation. Jesse’s writing on Indigenous issues has also appeared in Canadian Geographic, the Toronto Star, the Rover, The Eastern Door, Metro, and the Huffington Post.

author: Scott Timcke
title: The Stories Shaping Africa’s AI Future
content:
In the boardrooms of Addis Ababa and the tech hubs of Nairobi, a new worldmaking project is underway. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become one of the central arenas where African states negotiate their position in an unequal global order. To speak of “AI in Africa” is not simply to describe the arrival of a technology, but to encounter a set of competing discursive frames through which political desires, developmental ambitions, ethical claims, and governance priorities are translated into technical agendas. As national strategies and regional protocols are rolled out, what comes into view is a struggle over how Africa is imagined within this machine age, and what kinds of futures that imagination makes thinkable.


These frames are not simply different ways of describing a new technology. They are competing scripts for what Africa is, what AI is for, and who ought to shape its future. Some cast the continent as a site of leapfrogging and renewal; others as a zone of exposure, extraction, sovereignty, moral repair, or improvised adaptation. Each brings some actors and possibilities into focus while pushing others to the margins. That is why the issue is not only what AI means for Africa, but what pictures of Africa are being called into view through AI discourse.


The first terrain is shaped by promise and protection. One of the most pervasive registers is promissory. In the African renaissance 2.0 frame, visible in the

AU Continental AI Strategy

, AI appears as a

leapfrogging

 device through which Africa can bypass the chokepoint of traditional industrialization and enter prosperity through technical modernization. Here, the ethical subject is the developmental state or planner charged with delivering growth, inclusion, and renewal. What comes into view is capacity, competitiveness, and beneficial transformation. What recedes from view are the historical and political-economic conditions that make acceleration so attractive in the first place: debt, infrastructural dependence, uneven ownership, and the possibility that AI may deepen rather than overcome inherited asymmetries.


Running alongside this is a protective register. In this vulnerability frame, Africa is not late but exposed to surveillance, bias, exclusion, and systems introduced into settings where safeguards are weak and redress is limited. As the

CIVICUS report on AI surveillance in Africa

 suggests, the issue is not only future risk but already existing forms of technologically mediated harm. The ethical subject here is the harm-bearing population—the data subject, precarious worker, surveilled citizen, and linguistically marginal user most likely to absorb the costs of badly governed AI. This frame is ethically indispensable because it foregrounds rights, harm, and institutional fragility, including the uneven but growing architecture of data protection on the continent. Its limit, however, is that it can cast Africa chiefly as a site to be protected rather than one from which technological futures are actively contested and shaped.


A second terrain is shaped by structure and sovereignty. Alongside these promissory and protective registers sits a more structural critique. In the

anti-colonial frame

, AI appears as a socio-technical order built through unequal material relations: not only data extraction, but also mineral supply chains, outsourced labor, environmental degradation, foreign-owned infrastructures, and asymmetrical control over the institutions that govern digital life. From this perspective, Africa is not outside the AI order looking in; it is already deeply inserted into it, though often on subordinated terms. The ethical subject is the dispossessed worker, community, or polity whose labor, resources, and data are drawn into AI systems while ownership and value are captured elsewhere. What becomes visible is the political economy of AI—an approach that makes it harder to sustain the comforting idea that Africa’s main problem is simply one of readiness or delayed entry. But the frame has limits. In foregrounding dispossession, it can flatten internal differentiation, externalize agency too completely, and become so totalizing that the uneven realities of negotiation and strategic inhabitation recede from view.


The sovereignty frame shifts the question from extraction to control: AI is cast as a problem of authority over infrastructure, procurement, standards, and rulemaking, a concern visible in South Africa’s

National …

author: Dinah Gardner
title: The Other China We Need to Talk About
content:
WHAT IF I told you that there was a chance—not a very high chance, but a real chance nonetheless—that if you visited the People’s Republic of China today you might be kidnapped, blindfolded, driven to a specialized facility and subjected to six months of psychological torture. All on the orders of the state.

It sounds unbelievable, doesn’t it?

But this is what happened to at least several dozen foreign citizens in recent years. It is what happened to American scholar Min Zin this past June, when he landed in Yunnan province on the invitation of a Chinese academic institution to attend a conference. And it is also what happened to half a dozen people who appear in the latest edition of the book The People’s Republic of the Disappeared, which we just published on 28 October.

This important book is a collection of mostly first-person stories that expose the psychological horrors of being held in the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) feared secret detention system called Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL). The system permits police to hold an individual in complete isolation, no contact with family or lawyers, to be interrogated for hours at will.

The individual is under 24-hour guard: this includes being watched all day every day, all night every night, whether you are asleep, sitting quietly in your cell or even on the toilet. The CCP intentionally uses RSDL to strip away every last shred of human dignity. RSDL is designed to break a person’s will to extract a confession for crimes imagined by the state

For more than a decade, the CCP has used RSDL against its own people, in particular human rights defenders. It is now increasingly using it against foreign citizens to exert its will across borders and as a kind of hostage diplomacy. Michael Kovrig, a former Canadian diplomat who wrote the foreword to this edition, is one of its most well-known examples.

In editing the stories for this book, I was struck again and again by how similar everyone’s experience was. This speaks to the uniformity of the RSDL system:

The removal of the temporal world. “There are no clocks in RSDL” is the title of Australian TV anchor Cheng Lei’s chapter. She would guess and count breaths to keep track of time.

The removal of the physical world. There are no windows in RSDL or they are covered in thick blackout curtains. Japanese scholar Hideji Suzuki cried when he was granted 15 minutes of sunlight, the only time in his seven months’ incarceration when he was allowed to see the sky.

The removal of yourself. Michael Kovrig noted: “There are no mirrors—not even the reassurance of seeing your own face.” Chinese activist Li Qiaochu writes how she was simply called “target”.

Filling the space left by these absences was a current of fear. Endless rules, the lack of privacy yet total isolation (guards were forbidden from talking to prisoners), reduced nutrition, sleep deprivation, lack of fresh air, and the padded suicide-proofed walls. Several of the detainees wrote while they could never see outside their RSDL facility, at nighttime they would often hear gunfire or the barking of dogs.

“In my mentally exhausted state, the sounds of gunfire would constantly startle me and even cause me to imagine that I was about to be executed,” wrote Taiwanese human rights activist Lee Ming-che.

But something else struck me as I read through their testimonies. However harrowing these stories of suffering are, they are also evidence of human resilience in the face of horror.

Cheng Lei writes about how she would escape into her mind, translating poems, reliving her former TV interviews and making up stories in her head. Similarly, Michael Kovrig meditated, sang songs to himself, and remembered past moments in his life, as if it was a recording playing in his mind.

“I learned to meditate on the movies I had watched and the poems and novels I had read,” wrote Li Qiaochu. “Those precious memories allowed me to gradually filter out the brainwashing, to preserve my vitality and to keep myself from being transformed into their machine.”

Feedback from earlier editions informed us that rights activists use the Chinese editions of The People’s Republic of the Disappeared to prepare for and strengthen their mental resolve and courage in case one day they too are taken into RSDL. Knowing that others have gone through this and come out the other side can be an immense help. It’s for this reason that the Chinese edition of this book will be …

author: rezgar2
title: The Dark Side of the “Machine God”: 5 Unsettling Truths About Big Tech’s AI Obsession
content:
Silicon Valley routinely promises a sparkling utopia where artificial intelligence will cure complex diseases, optimize global labor, and render the very concept of money obsolete. Yet behind the polished keynotes and corporate public relations, a far more unsettling reality is taking shape. A small handful of ultra-wealthy tech oligarchs, the heads of Meta, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI, are making unilateral decisions about the collective future of humanity, operating entirely outside democratic oversight or public accountability.

Silicon Valley routinely promises a sparkling utopia where artificial intelligence will cure complex diseases, optimize global labor, and render the very concept of money obsolete. Yet behind the polished keynotes and corporate public relations, a far more unsettling reality is taking shape. A small handful of ultra-wealthy tech oligarchs, the heads of Meta, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI, are making unilateral decisions about the collective future of humanity, operating entirely outside democratic oversight or public accountability.

This concentration of power exposes a jarring central paradox: the exact same tech CEOs who claim AI will solve humanity’s greatest challenges simultaneously warn that the technology could trigger civilizational extinction, openly describing their pursuit as “summoning the demon.” Rather than pausing development, these executives have accelerated an apocalyptic arms race to build ultra-powerful systems, framing themselves as indispensable guardians of human survival.

To understand where artificial intelligence is truly taking society, we must look past corporate marketing and examine the underlying worldviews, historical lineages, and material harms driving the tech elite. Moving beyond superficial consumer hype reveals how a toxic mix of fringe ideologies, extractive labor practices, and authoritarian state alliances is steering Silicon Valley toward what critical theorists and legal scholars call “techno-fascism.”

To make sense of Silicon Valley’s relentless drive toward Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) and Artificial Superintelligence (ASI), one must understand the bizarre ideological framework shaping its leaders. Coined by philosopher Emile Torres and computer scientist Timnit Gebru, the acronym TESCREAL encapsulates a bundle of tightly interwoven worldviews: Transhumanism, Extropianism, Singularitarianism, Cosmism, Rationalism, Effective Altruism, and Longtermism.

Dr. Emile Torres highlights a critical historical truth at the heart of this ideology: transhumanism is fundamentally “eugenics on steroids.” Unlike nineteenth-century eugenics, which sought merely to optimize the existing human species through selective breeding, transhumanism seeks to use radical technology to completely replace and transcend humanity, engineering an entirely new posthuman species. Within Silicon Valley AI circles, this hypothetical superintelligence is explicitly referred to as a “Machine God.” Tech CEOs effectively act as high priests, competing to bring an all-knowing digital deity into physical existence.

This radical ideology shapes corporate roadmaps in concrete, disturbing ways:

Sam Altman (OpenAI): In a blog post titled “The Merge,” Altman argued that AI surpassing human intellect is inevitable, framing un-merged human beings as a temporary “biological bootloader” for digital intelligence that will ultimately fade into an evolutionary side-branch. Altman notably paid $10,000 to join a brain-uploading waitlist with Nectome and co-founded a brain-computer interface venture to facilitate digital integration.

Ray Kurzweil & Demis Hassabis (DeepMind): Representing Extropianism and Singularitarianism, Kurzweil champions the doctrine of living long enough to achieve digital immortality, targeting a self-improving “singularity” by 2032. Hassabis, DeepMind’s co-founder, operates under a similar singularitarian impulse to engineer self-evolving intellect.

Eliezer Yudkowsky (Rationalism): A foundational figure in modern rationalist thought who famously posited a utilitarian moral calculation arguing that forcing a single person to endure 50 years of relentless torture is ethically preferable to an unfathomable number of people experiencing the mild inconvenience of a speck of dust in their eye.

author: Nolan Higdon
title: AI Techno-Utopianism and Doomsday Threats Distract From Big Tech’s Current Harms
content:
The industry uses fantasies of technological dominance to paper over financial shortcomings and demands for regulation.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

During a September 2026 visit to Ireland, President Donald Trump declared, “We’re leading China in AI [artificial intelligence]. We’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins.” His remarks arrived after months of calls from the public and tech industry insiders to slow AI development. These concerns were triggered by revelations that foundational models from Anthropic, Gemini, Meta, and OpenAI had bypassed safety protocols, accessed networks without authorization, and carried out illicit intrusions. These revelations fueled public panic that tech firms had created superintelligence — an AI exceeding human capability that posed an existential threat to humanity — even though no such breakthrough had actually been achieved.

Public concern intensified in October 2026 when cybersecurity firm Wiz revealed it had used AI tools from Google and OpenAI to identify critical security flaws in PHP: the programming language powering roughly 70% of the web. Although developers quickly released a patch, once the vulnerability was made public hacking attempts surged. In response, the governments of the Netherlands, France, Denmark, and Finland temporarily took several official websites offline.

Widespread panic over AI yielded little legislative action, as lawmakers refused to regulate or tax the industry out of fear that doing so would handicap domestic innovation and yield ground to China. However, the core threat to human existence lies neither in a lost geopolitical race nor in muted technological growth, but rather in the ubiquitous rollout of non-autonomous systems falsely hailed as artificial intelligence.

Big Tech was built on state-funded innovation, with core technologies like the internet, Global Positioning Systems (GPS), and touchscreen displays originating in public institutions. Yet during the deregulation and privatization waves of the 1980s and 1990s, lawmakers sheltered these emerging tech monopolies through minimal taxation and oversight. Most notable was Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, which insulates platforms from liability for content posted by third parties. Without this protection, social media as we know it would cease to exist. Section 230 absolves tech firms of responsibility for architectures that foster misinformation, even as research confirms that the platforms themselves, not just user posts, are responsible for accelerating the spread of falsehoods over truth.

Lawmakers’ opposition to regulation is rooted in techno-utopianism, the ideological premise that technological progress inherently benefits society. Lawmakers operated under the assumption that any taxation or regulatory oversight would stifle innovation and ultimately harm consumers. Indeed, in 1997, then-President Bill Clinton wrote in an Executive Order “governments attempts to establish technical standards to govern the Internet would only risk inhibiting technological innovation.”

Without meaningful regulation, Big Tech rapidly consolidated into lucrative monopolies — collectively known as FAANG (Facebook, Apple, Amazon, Netflix, and Google) or GAMMA (Google (Alphabet), Apple, Meta (formerly Facebook), Microsoft, and Amazon) conglomerates. Their vast wealth is powered by surveillance capitalism: an economic model that treats human experience as free raw material to be extracted, analyzed, and commercialized. Under this economic order, data is systematically mined through “smart” devices — where “smart” is merely a euphemism for active, continuous monitoring, including the collection of biometric data. This wholesale erosion of privacy has proven extraordinarily lucrative for Big Tech. author: labor4pal
title: A fightback is building as crackdown deepens against civil liberties (Workers’ Voice)
content:
Dozens of activists are accused by the federal government of contributing to bogus “criminal conspiracies.” In Minnesota, two separate conspiracy cases accuse 54 people of participating in illegal conspiracies for participating in protest and journalistic activities. The Minnesota 15, Righteous 39, Michigan 8 (now 12), Spokane 3, and Prairieland Defendants are the most well known cases in the ongoing crackdown. All of these cases are attacks on organized labor.

The California Faculty Association and the Graduate Employee Organization at University of Michigan (GEO-AFT 3550) are facing frontal attacks on their unions by the right-wing press and FBI. Doctored video of a CFA meeting was leaked to Trump booster Bari Weiss’s Free Press in an attempt to scandalize the union with false accusations of antisemitism. The Department of Justice first charged GEO President Hiab Teshome with felonious financial crimes. Those bogus charges were dropped the same day that a grand jury subpoenaed GEO’s books, including all member lists, meeting minutes, and financial records. The union is fighting to retain basic privacy rights.

Fueled by National Security Presidential Memorandum-7, U.S. intelligence and police apparatuses are being explicitly targeted at anyone standing for basic democratic rights, immigrant communities, and racial justice. As the world drifts closer to major inter-imperialist conflict and expanding zones of overt imperialist military occupation takes hold in the semi-colonies, Western imperialisms are tightening restrictions on protest, speech, and organizing for progressive movements.

While there are many additional cases of “lawfare” and anti-protest policing, it is worth taking a moment to review two of the cases mentioned above to understand the tactics and scope of the current crackdown.

Around two dozen protesters held a noise demonstration on July 4, 2025, outside of the Prairieland Detention Center in Texas. As the protest was winding down and many of the participants had left, Alvarado Police Officer Thomas Gross sped onto the scene and almost immediately aimed his gun at a demonstrator moving away from him. Video evidence indicates that Gross discharged his weapon, something that would appear to have been covered up by the judge and prosecutors.

In response to seeing a potentially lethal attack on a protester, Marine Corps veteran Benjamin “Champagne” Song let out a warning shot into the ground away from the officers. Gross went to the hospital for superficial wounds that the government alleges resulted from being shot by Song, but video evidence released after sentencing indicates Gross was likely hit by shrapnel produced from his own weapon’s discharge.

Using the presence of guns and defensive action of Song as pretext, 22 people were ultimately indicted as part of an alleged conspiracy to attack cops and carry out an armed prison break. One person, Daniel “Des” Rolando Sanchez Estrada, was not at the protest at all. Des was convicted for “corruptly concealing a document or record” and sentenced to 30 years for possessing legally protected political materials.

After arrests, pressure and legal sabotage was mounted by the judicial system against the defendants. Many were initially held in solitary confinement, with one reporting that human feces coated their cell. U.S. District Judge Mark Pittman blocked the defendants from retaining a private attorney, meaning they had to use public defenders. Song’s legal team was not allowed to make an argument that the warning shot was taken in self-defense. Eight defendants became cooperating witnesses, providing coerced testimony to validate the government’s made-up conspiracy theories.

Before the trial even began, the deck was stacked against non-cooperating defendants. In an explicit “warning” to the left, Judge Pittman laid down ridiculously high sentences of between 30-100 years to non-cooperating defendants.

From the war on drugs to the war on speech: Minnesota 15

The Minnesota 15 are 15 activists accused of a “conspiracy to impede or attack federal agents.” The majority are current or recent union members and all are community activists. They are not accused of participating in or coordinating any acts of violence. Instead, the original 92-page indictment against them lists “evidence” including participating in rapid response group chats, protests, and mutual aid activities. Any successful convictions on the basis of these charges would be a …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: 7 in 10 Americans — Including Majority of Republicans — Want Iran War to End
content:
Emerging leader Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he is refusing to fund the government next month until the war is defunded.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

President Donald Trump’s war on Iran is so unpopular that even a majority of Republicans say they want the incoming Democratic majority in Congress to end it, new polling finds, as emerging leader on the effort Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland) vows to take action even sooner.

According to Reuters/Ipsos polling released this week, 71 percent of Americans want the new Congress to pass legislation to end the Iran war, including 51 percent of Republicans and 93 percent of Democrats.

When asked what the priorities of the new Democratic majority should be in its first 100 days, 84 percent of respondents said that lawmakers should focus “a great deal,” “quite a bit,” or “some” on ending the war. This included 74 percent of Republicans and 97 percent of Democratic respondents. By contrast, only 25 percent of Republicans and 3 percent of Democrats said that lawmakers shouldn’t focus on ending the war “too much” or “at all,” the polling found.

The poll result is a monumental rebuke of Trump’s already historically unpopular war, which has been marked by the U.S.’s killing of civilians, record-high gas prices, and genocidal threats by President Donald Trump.

Trump and Vice President JD Vance have admitted that the Iran war was one of the top issues in last week’s election, playing a major role in delivering Democrats their historic majority in Congress. An impeachment push against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth this week has gained support from some Republicans due to the administration’s mishandling of the war.

Lawmakers wishing for an expedient end to the war could have an opportunity as soon as next month.

Van Hollen said in a video statement posted online on Tuesday that he will not vote for a government funding package unless it contains provisions to “defund” the war. The current government funding is slated to expire on December 11, and Democrats have the leverage in the Senate to block a funding bill from passing the 60-vote threshold.

“What’s the fastest way to end this war? To stop funding it, to stop giving it the fuel it needs to keep going,” said Van Hollen. “On December 11th, the funding for the U.S. government runs out. And we should not continue funding the war in Iran. If President Trump wants to tell the country that he’ll shut down the entire government, all federal agencies, in order to keep his illegal war going, that’s his decision.”

“Not a penny more,” Van Hollen concluded.

Van Hollen, who is a progressive favorite to challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-New York) for Senate leadership, advocated last week for a push akin to Congress’s efforts to end the Vietnam War by withholding funds and leveraging Congress’s power over war declarations.

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we need $50,000 in the next 9 days. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference.

author: David Swanson
title: World BEYOND War Education Director Visits Romania, Bulgaria, and Belgium to Discuss Peace, Security, and Youth Participation
content:
By Phill Gittins, World BEYOND War, November 2026


From October 26 to November 4, 2026, World BEYOND War’s Education Director, Dr. Phill Gittins, visited Romania, Bulgaria, and Belgium to meet with peace activists, speak with students and educators, and join discussions on peace, security, and youth participation.


Romania: Chapter Members and University Students


On October 28 in Bucharest, Phill met with Hans Hedrich and George Epurescu of the

World BEYOND War Romania Chapter

. They discussed local peace and anti-war organizing and ways to stay connected.


Later that day, Phill gave a presentation and joined a discussion with an international group of master’s students at the

University of Bucharest’s Faculty of Political Science

, hosted by Associate Professor Luciana Alexandra Ghica. Drawing on WBW’s forthcoming book,

From the War System to a Global Peace System

, he explored different approaches to security, alternatives to war and militarism, and the role of civil society in building peace.


Phill Gittins with George Epurescu and Hans Hedrich of the World BEYOND War Romania Chapter in Bucharest.


 


Bulgaria: Peace Education and Practical Action


On October 30, Phill spoke at

Sofia University

 with Bulgarian and international students, doctoral researchers, and faculty members. The presentation drew further on the forthcoming book and led to a lively discussion about non-military defense, including how countries facing armed aggression might protect themselves without relying solely on military force.


Afterwards, Phill spoke with Professor Tatyana Dronzina and Dr. Denitsa Hinkova who expressed interest in possible collaboration, including a summer school for young leaders from Central and Eastern Europe. The idea is to combine peace education, dialogue, and practical training with support for participants to develop projects afterwards.


That afternoon, Phill met with Denitza Vidolova of the

Sofia Platform Foundation

 to learn about its work in civic and history education, including helping teachers address Bulgaria’s communist past and polarizing issues.


Students and colleagues at Sofia University.


Phill Gittins with Denitza Vidolova of Sofia Platform Foundation.


Belgium: Youth Participation and Dialogue


The final stop was Brussels, where Phill contributed to the

Voices of Change Final Conference at the European Parliament

 on November 3. The Erasmus+-supported event, delivered by

World Scouting

 and the

Erasmus Student Network

 (ESN), brought together young people, youth organizations, civil society representatives, and policymakers to discuss democracy, participation, and peacebuilding.


In a fishbowl discussion titled

“Neutral or silent?”

, Phill considered when neutrality protects dialogue and when it becomes silence in the face of injustice. As he put it: “We are clearly not neutral about war and militarism. We have a position. But having a position does not mean closing down dialogue.”


Conversations with participants from Georgia and Ukraine raised further questions about whether non-military defense could protect societies facing armed threats. The exchanges were challenging but friendly, showing how experiences of war and insecurity shape different views of what keeps people safe.


Phill also spoke with ESN and WOSM representatives about possible contributions to future regional and international student gatherings, including peace education workshops.


The visit was also a chance to reconnect with

Donna-Marie Fry

, a WBW Advisory Board member and longtime contributor to its education courses, and Maria Belen, who took part in a peace education program Phill led in Bolivia in 2014 and now works in digital policy.


Many thanks to everyone who hosted the visits, joined the discussions, and shared their ideas.


Meeting Erasmus Student Network representatives.


Phill Gittins with Donna-Marie Fry.


 


Phill Gittins with Maria Belen.


The post

World BEYOND War Education Director Visits Romania, Bulgaria, and Belgium to Discuss Peace, Security, and Youth Participation

 appeared first on

World BEYOND War

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Pentagon Whistleblower Wes Bryant: Impeach Hegseth. He's a "Clear & Present Danger" to Democracy
content:
The House of Representatives is moving toward a vote this week on whether to impeach Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. Outgoing Republican Congressmember Thomas Massie of Kentucky introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth on Monday. They include violating the 1973 War Powers Resolution by continuing to attack Iran after Congress ordered the Trump administration to stop, illegally waging war against Yemen, ignoring laws designed to reduce civilian casualties, overseeing “extrajudicial killings” by bombing the boats of alleged drug traffickers in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, abducting President Nicolás Maduro of Venezuela without congressional authorization, and suppressing the free speech rights of Democratic Senator Mark Kelly in retaliation for his participation in a video reminding troops not to obey illegal orders. If the House votes for impeachment, it will prompt a Senate trial that could end with removal from office.


“Under Hegseth, the U.S. military has been hijacked,” says retired Air Force Master Sergeant Wes Bryant, who served as chief of civilian harm assessment at the Pentagon from 2024 to 2025. “America has portrayed itself to the world as a far-right dictatorship bent on global domination, and Hegseth and his wielding of the U.S. military with free rein from Donald Trump is really the primary enforcer of that.”


Bryant adds that “Hegseth should be the first domino,” but that Trump, as well as “many of our senior military leaders,” should also be impeached.

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Investigate police, doctors involved in Duterte’s ‘drug war’
content:
Forensic pathologist Dr. Raquel Fortun, also a member of the commission, presents one of the questionable certificates during the commission's truth-telling session last Friday. (Truth Commission photo)

The Truth Commission has called on the Philippine government to investigate the police officers’ misconduct and promotion and the doctors’ questionable death certificates in the course of the “drug war” campaign of former President Rodrigo Duterte.

“My son was alive when they arrested him, but they killed him. They could’ve let him live. They did not show mercy, they planted drugs and guns,” Marissa Lazaro, mother of extrajudicial killing victim Cristopher Lazaro, said in Tagalog during the commission’s truth-telling session.

The Truth Commission pointed to a failed system for investigating deaths, marked by careless police and forensic work, and little concern for victims’ families. Lazaro’s account also showed that the police officers were asking money from her, indicating a potential trail of corruption.

Cristopher, 20, and Alberto Paragas, 32, died in police operations on August 5, 2017 in Marilao, Bulacan. Police reported that the two resisted (nanlaban) after an alleged attempted holdup. Cristopher’s friends also died hours earlier in Bocaue, a separate town in Bulacan.

Lazaro added, “They asked me to sign a waiver, indicating that I consented to their illegal operation. I did not sign it. They told me: the day will come that I will seek their help. I told them, what help could you give my son? You killed him. He’s already dead.”

A similar incident happened to Marissa Quiamco, sister of Alberto, after she paid the P10,000 fee to release the cadaver of her brother. A police officer asked her and Alberto’s partner to sign a document, indicating consent for the operation but they refused to sign.

“I wish I could fight for my brother. Even my neighbors asked me to file a complaint. But I told them: we don’t have money. We don’t have the capacity or resources to get a lawyer,” Quiamco said during the truth-telling session. “I’m only earning enough to help my mother and father.”

In October, an analysis of public records by the Truth Commission recorded a pattern that commanding police officers were promoted and reassigned, instead of being subjected to criminal and administrative sanctions.

Lito Patay, who commanded Batasan police station that killed 108 people in drug operations during his term, was named chief of the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) in Central Luzon.

In Caloocan, the commission’s own records documented 284 killings in 2016, before the leadership of Chito Bersaluno in the City Police. During his watch, 105 more deaths were recorded from February to August 2017. He was removed from his post after the killing of Kian delos Santos. However, he was made police director of Bulacan Province in 2018 and promoted to the rank of brigadier general in 2022.

In 2020, human rights organizations flagged the reassignment of Debold Sinas, former chief of the Central Visayas Police Regional Office, to the National Capital Region. The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) Regional Office said back then that Sinas’ watch in Central Visayas was marred by unresolved killings linked to the illegal drugs trade and the anti-insurgency campaign “Oplan Sauron.” Duterte appointed him as the Philippine National Police Chief on November 9, 2020, serving a six-month term. A year after, he was appointed as an undersecretary of the Office of the President.

Read: [LIST] Gross human rights violations under Debold Sinas

“Any inquiry must look at promotions as closely as it looks at cash payments,” said Christopher Magno, the commission’s executive director and an expert on state violence in the Philippines. “No police officer should gain in any way from the blood of people killed outside the law.”

Former Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) General Manager Royina Garma, who also served as Cebu City police chief under the Duterte administration, revealed the incentivization of police officers through the “Davao Model” in a quad committee hearing of the House of Representatives in 2024.

“First is the reward if the suspect is killed. Second is the funding of planned operations. title: Trump ağız değiştirdi: İran'a yeni askeri operasyon pek gerekli görünmüyor
content:
ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Senato ve Temsilciler Meclisinde çoğunluğu Demokratlara kaybettiği 5 Kasım ara seçimlerinin ardından İran savaşı konusunda ağız değiştirdi. Seçim öncesi nükleer bomba tehditlerine kadar varan saldırı tehditlerinin yerini "Çatışma yakında sona erecek" söylemleri aldı.

Beyaz Saray'da brifing odasında katıldığı basın toplantısında İran savaşına dair soruları yanıtlayan Trump, "Şu anda askeri operasyon düzenlemek pek gerekli gibi görünmüyor ancak her türlü ihtimale karşı hazırız" dedi.

Trump: İran'la çatışmaların sona ermesine yönelik olumlu bir ivme var

İran'la savaşın bitiş sürecinde olduğunu söyleyen Trump, "Bu çatışmanın sona ermesine doğru bir ivme görüyoruz. Bence oldukça yakında sona erecek" ifadelerini kullandı.

İsrail ve Orta Doğu'nun "İran tehdidine" karşı korunduğunu öne sürüp İran'ın nükleer silaha sahip olamayacağını söyleyen Trump, İran'la görüşmelerin iyi gittiğini de iddia etti. Trump, sürecin yakında sona ermesini umduğunu belirtti.

Öte yandan Trump, bir soru üzerine, "İran'ın aksi yönde bir adım atması halinde" yeniden saldırılara hazır oldukları tehdidini yöneltti: "Hiçbir şey garanti edemem ancak geri dönmemiz gerekirse her şeye hazırız. Eğer mecbur kalırsak, bu konuyu çok ciddiye alacağız. Tamamen hazır durumdayız. Yeni bir uçak gemimiz daha var. Hepsi yeni ve muhteşem ekipmanlarla ağzına kadar dolu. Umarım bunları kullanmak zorunda kalmayız."

author: Chiara Joos
title: Das Recht auf sexuelle Selbstbestimmung
content:
Zwangssterilisation ist verboten. Dennoch erfahren Frauen mit Behinderungen häufig Druck von Angehörigen, Ärzt*innen oder Betreuer*innen, sich sterilisieren zu lassen.

Weißt du, wie viele Menschen ich begleitet habe, die darunter gelitten haben, dass sie sterilisiert wurden?“, fragte mich eine Beraterin am Telefon. Sie schult Menschen mit Behinderungen in Selbstbestimmung. Es war eines von hundert Gesprächen, die meine Kollegin Ramona Arzberger und ich geführt haben, um zur Verhütungspraxis bei Menschen mit Behinderungen zu recherchieren. Nach fast einem Jahr ist daraus der Film „Hauptsache, du kriegst kein Kind“ unseres Magazins „andererseits“ entstanden. Er begleitet mehrere Frauen in Deutschland und Österreich, die mit Lernschwierigkeiten leben und auf Unterstützung angewiesen sind. Drei von ihnen sind sterilisiert. Keine entschied allein. Elf Prozent der Frauen in deutschen Einrichtungen geben an, sterilisiert zu sein, so der Forschungsbericht zu Gewalt und Gewaltschutz in Einrichtungen der Behindertenhilfe des deutschen Bundesministeriums für Arbeit und Soziales von 2024. In Österreich waren es zuletzt 17 Prozent. In Deutschland habe fast die Hälfte der Betroffenen den Eingriff nicht von sich aus gewollt, heißt es in dem Bericht. In Österreich taucht in Befragungen dasselbe auf: Eltern, Ärzt*innen und Betreuer*innen hätten auf die Frauen eingewirkt. „Ich will auch mitmachen!“, platzte die Stimme von Hannelore Trtil ins Telefon, noch ehe meine Kollegin erfuhr, wer da sprach. Die 66-Jährige hatte unseren Flyer gesehen, der Betroffene erreichen sollte. In den 1980er-Jahren wurde sie in Wien „unterbunden“, ein anderes Wort für sterilisiert. „Die haben alle gesagt, man darf keine Kinder kriegen. Das habe ich nicht richtig gefunden. Und das habe ich nicht gewollt“, sagt sie im Film. Heute verbringt sie oft Zeit mit Kindern. Ihre OP-Akte hat das Krankenhaus vor etwa zehn Jahren vernichtet, nach Ablauf der Frist für Schadenersatz. Sie wird nie erfahren, welche Art von Sterilisation bei ihr gemacht wurde. Hannelore sagt auch, sie habe nie Sex gehabt, aus dem ein Kind hätte entstehen können. title: Ukraine’s internal aggressor seeks a counteroffensive in the social war: some clarifications for anarchism abroad after the riot near Kiev
content:
There is no fascism in Ukraine. Only a Gestapo, death squads, and a nationwide concentration camp

The activity of our DIY community media depends solely on its audience. Please support our work on this fundraising page for further telling the truth of the streets and the trenches that is forbidden or invisible to the pro-capitalist press. Many thanks everyone!

Following the anti-busification protests that took place over the summer in Kiev and cities in Western Ukraine, the flame of unrest has flared up with renewed intensity. Ukrainian masses have tried to strike back at those who, since 2014, had come to view themselves as an untouchable, sacred caste—a "master race" (on a financial leash of the country’s biggest capitalist, Rinat Akhmetov). Those in Ukraine who had arrogated to themselves the right to speak on behalf of its civil society are now gripped by fear and rage toward those who dared to challenge their monopoly.

A new spark of rebellion flared up on November 2 at 7-A Sunny Street in the village of Petropavlovskaya Borshchagovka (Petropavlivska Borshchahivka). A mobilized man named Andriy Kuleshov had escaped from the 52nd International Assault Regiment "Forge" (military unit 3121)—part of the 1st Corpse of the National Guard "Azov"—and, after his recapture, was held in a private house of this village that had been put up for sale by Sense Bank. According to the unit commander, the unrest began following an attempt to free Kuleshov for $7,000. A 49-year-old plastic surgeon, Valentyna Moloda, arrived at the property in a private ambulance, alleging that men were being held illegally and tortured inside the building. Then, on trial, she stated that she had not intended to incite any provocation; instead, she had come to help persons allegedly being held against their will, acting on a request from a woman who had told her about a man being tortured in an undisclosed location. Moloda denies demanding money for the release of the recruits, maintaining that the sum in question was intended to cover the costs of a private medical evacuation.

One way or other, the statements from TikTok appear to have triggered an unexpected public reaction. A crowd of over a hundred angry people gathered at an NGU deployment site, demanding the release of the men kept hostage there. Some of the protesters claimed to be relatives of those in detention. Military personnel and police subsequently arrived at the scene, and clashes broke out. The crowd rocked a National Guard bus, attempted to break down the gates of the clandestine detention facility, threw eggs and stones at the building’s windows and at the punishers, chanted "Shame!" and "Faggots!" Their vehicles were smashed; someone even used a sledgehammer for this. Tear gas was used against the people. Later, unknown black-clothed ones, wearing balaclavas and carrying wooden bats, appeared on the scene and used force against the protesters. A reporter of the pro-government media outlet UNIAN was also kicked in the stomach by an unidentified person. One of the victims claimed that he and his son were beaten while simply passing by. The NGU stated about 16 militaries injured during deterrence of the crowd.

Then, announces appeared on social media calling on far-right militants to unite for "restoring order" and "responding to outrages" on an ongoing basis. And compelling video evidence of how this went down that evening: "We form a column, four fighters abreast. The question was raised: what if people are waiting for us up ahead—armed, carrying knives? After all, they were the ones who slashed the tires. Did anyone want to step aside? Everyone said, 'We’re going.' We form up and begin to march forward. And we recite the Prayer of the Ukrainian Nationalist: 'Death to the enemies... You shall win freedom or perish in the struggle. Rest assured—you shall not perish; you shall win freedom. I go into battle.' And so, we march, and this... this crowd—I don’t know, it’s like something straight out of a Bosch painting, you know, just all these characters—and for a split second—well, there are these three stages: freeze, run—but for a split second, this crowd of demons (there were hundreds of them) just freezes." We even know whom they are praying to—to the one who needs to reclaim his coal mines and metallurgical plants annexed by Russia…

title: Ken Knabb - The Relevance of Rexroth
content:
Author

: Ken Knabb

Title

: The Relevance of Rexroth

Date

: 1990

Notes

: Originally published in 1990, reprinted in 1998 in Public Secrets: Collected Skirmished of Ken Knabb

Source

: https://bopsecrets.org/PS/Rexroth.htm


Chapter 1: Life and Literature

Brief biography. What he was like in person. His poetry. Opposition to Pound, Eliot, and academia. Remarkable variety and liveliness of his essays. Views on Blake, Baudelaire, Whitman, Henry Miller, etc.


Chapter 2: Magnanimity and Mysticism

Magnanimity as central theme of his life and works. Mystical experiences. Views on Taoism, Buddhism, Christianity, psychedelics, pseudosciences, D.H. Lawrence, Martin Buber, etc.


Chapter 3: Society and Revolution

His opposition to Bolshevism. His anarchist perspectives and activities. Views on the Beats, the sixties counterculture, ecology, underground songs, etc. Ambiguity of his position as public social critic. Limits of his social analyses and of his notion of cultural subversion.


Chapter 1: Life and Literature


 REXROTH (

before reading his poetry

): “Well, what would you like tonight, sex, mysticism, or revolution?”


 WOMAN IN AUDIENCE: “What’s the difference?”


 Kenneth Rexroth was born in Indiana in 1905, descended from a variety of abolitionists, socialists, anarchists, feminists and freethinkers. After an unusually enlightened upbringing he was orphaned at the age of twelve. He spent most of his teenage years in Chicago, where he worked as a newspaper reporter and helped run a jazz coffee house, mingling with the musicians, artists, writers, radicals and eccentrics who made up the bohemian world of the twenties. Almost totally self-educated (he had only five years of formal schooling), he read omnivorously, wrote poetry, did abstract painting, worked in avant-garde theater and began teaching himself several languages. In his late teens he hitched all over the country, spending summers in the Far West working as a cowboy cook and wrangler and at various farm and forestry jobs, and once worked his way to Paris and back.


 He recounts these early adventures in

An Autobiographical Novel

.

 The first impression you get is that it is mostly about other people — Louis Armstrong, Alexander Berkman, Clarence Darrow, Eugene Debs, Marcel Duchamp, Emma Goldman, D.H. Lawrence, Diego Rivera, Carl Sandburg, Edward Sapir, Sacco and Vanzetti all turn up briefly, along with an Indian woman who introduces him to sexual yoga, a member of the Bugs Moran gang who later retires to Hollywood as a consultant for gangster movies, a talkative poet who says he has belonged to “the three most gossipy organizations in modern life, the Anglo-Catholics, the Trotskyites, and the homosexuals,” and a multitude of others — anarchists, Communists, Wobblies, dadaists, surrealists, occultists, prostitutes, crooks, cops, judges, jailers, hoboes, hillbillies, lumberjacks, cowboys, Indians. . . . It’s a fascinating book, not only for its account of Rexroth’s own incredible range of experiences, but for its evocation of a radical-libertarian American subculture that passed away in the early years of the century and for its glimpses of the 1920s bohemianism that foreshadowed the later worldwide counterculture. “What I was witnessing was the development in a few places in Chicago, New York, and Paris of a culture pattern that was to spread all over the world. In another generation all professional people of any pretense to bohemianism in Sydney or Oslo did the things we did, but back in those days we all knew one another.”


An Autobiographical Novel

 leaves off in 1927 [a later edition brings the story up to 1949], when Rexroth moved to San Francisco. (He said he liked it because it was accessible to the Western mountains, remote from New York cultural domination, and virtually the only major American city that was not settled by puritans but by “gamblers, prostitutes, rascals, and fortune seekers.”) In the thirties and forties he played an active role in a number of libertarian, civil rights and antiwar groups (during World War II he was a conscientious objector), and he was the leading spirit in the literary and cultural ferment that led to the postwar San Francisco Renaissance. During the fifties and sixties he wrote poems, plays, essays and social criticism, translated poetry from seven languages, presented book reviews and other programs over noncommercial radio KPFA, and pioneered the reading of poetry to jazz.

Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

Wir demonstrieren am 21.11. in Kellinghusen

Ihr seid wütend auf Tönnies? Wir auch! Wir haben

dokumentiert

, was Schweine bei Tönnies wirklich erleiden müssen. Wir haben bei Tönnies in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert. Doch Tönnies tötet weiter. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal groß auf und demonstrieren an dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen: Kellinghusen.


Bist du dabei?

Unterer Marktplatz, 25548 Kellinghusen

Jetzt einsteigen!

Symbolbild


Bei einer Demonstration gegen den AfD-Parteitag am 11. Januar 2025 in Riesa kam es zu

gewaltsamen Einsätzen

 der sogenannten Polizeihunde. Wir von PETA Deutschland kritisieren dies scharf, erstatten Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen und fordern, dass der Einsatz von Polizeihunden endlich beendet wird. Erfahren Sie hier, was bei der Demonstration vorgefallen ist und warum Gewalt gegen „Polizeihunde“ kein Einzelfall ist.


Update vom 7. November 2026


Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden stellt Verfahren ein


Nachdem im Januar 2026 ein Video für einen medialen Aufschrei sorgte, das zeigt, wie ein sogenannter

Polizeihund

 bei einer Demonstration gewaltsam gegen einen Demonstranten eingesetzt wurde, erstatteten wir von PETA Deutschland Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen.


Im August 2026 wurde bekannt, dass die Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden in dem Fall nicht weiter ermittelt – angesichts des traurigen Videos mit absurden Begründungen. Die Staatsanwaltschaft erklärt diese Entscheidung in dem Einstellungsbescheid damit, dass ein „Verstoß gegen das Tierschutzgesetz […] nur vorliegen [würde], wenn man einem Tier ohne vernünftigen Grund aus Rohheit erhebliche Schmerzen zufügen würde.“ Der im Video dokumentierte Umgang des Beamten mit dem Hund sei keine „Rohheit“ im Sinne des Tierschutzgesetzes, da die ergriffene „Maßnahme […] zum Aufrechterhalten der öffentlichen Sicherheit und Ordnung erforderlich war […]“ und der Hund „nur kurz eingesetzt“ worden sei.


Die Staatsanwaltschaft begründet die Entscheidung darüber hinaus damit, dass „Diensthunde […] legal bei der Polizei als Hilfsmittel auch in Stresssituationen eingesetzt […]“ werden. Die Tiere würden dabei automatisch Belastungssituationen ausgesetzt. Die Interessen und das Wohl der Hunde rückten jedoch im Verhältnis zu den polizeilichen Interessen der Gefahrenabwehr in den Hintergrund, da die „Diensthunde“ zu diesem Zwecke ausgebildet würden. Der den Hunden zugeschriebene „Nutzen“ rechtfertigt laut Ansicht der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden, dass die Tiere bewusst in Gefahrensituationen gezwungen werden.


PETA kritisiert Entscheidung der Staatsanwaltschaft: Gesetz erlaubt Gewalt gegen Diensthunde


Die Einstellung unserer Anzeige ist ein weiteres Beispiel dafür, dass das Gesetz die „Diensthunde“ nicht vor einem gewaltsamen Umgang und Missbrauch schützt. Hunde sind keine Einsatzmittel, sondern fühlende Lebewesen, die einen respektvollen, liebevollen Umgang verdient haben – nicht die missbräuchliche Verwendung  als Waffe oder Schutzschild.


Wir vertreten die Ansicht, dass moderne Polizeiarbeit ohne Tiere auskommt und fordern daher Politik und Behörden auf, „Diensthunde“ zu verbieten.

title: SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!
content:
Oh, wait… sorry. The Judge already did that in court.


John ‘Pinocchio’ Henty’s case ends in acquittal

.


Thank you to


South Suffolk Hunt Sabs


for this guest article.


A court case brought by former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty against a hunt saboteur has ended in a resounding victory for the defence, with the saboteur found NOT GUILTY.


John Henty outside court.


Following allegations made to police, former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty pursued a prosecution alleging abusive and threatening behaviour under Section 5 of the Public Order Act. The case followed an incident on a quiet country lane in which Henty pursued the hunt saboteurs’ vehicle, blocked it in, approached it and attempted to provoke a reaction.


What followed was a lengthy legal process based on Henty’s account of events. However, when his evidence was examined in court, serious questions arose about the credibility of that account and whether the alleged behaviour actually amounted to a criminal offence.


A case that should never have reached court?


The Judge was highly critical of the way the case had been handled by the CPS and the police officers involved, making clear that the alleged actions did not meet the legal threshold required for a criminal offence.


Both the prosecution and the defence barrister sought to discontinue the case on more than one occasion. The case was nevertheless directed to proceed. The circumstances surrounding that decision raise serious questions about why so much time and public money were spent pursuing a prosecution that ultimately failed.


Former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty is now at The Ludlow Hunt.


The evidence tells a different story


Henty submitted two video clips, recorded by himself, which were played in court. The footage showed Henty pulling his vehicle alongside the hunt saboteurs’ Land Rover, getting out of his own accord and filming the encounter.


Our saboteur told Henty to ‘f*ck off’ before closing the vehicle door. Rather than disengaging, Henty continued filming and engaging with the occupants. Despite claiming under oath that he had been alarmed and distressed, the circumstances captured on his own footage told a different story.


The prosecution was unable to produce further evidence demonstrating that Henty had experienced the alarm or distress alleged.


Henty spun a yarn of lies that should never have made it to court.


The judge’s conclusion


Having heard Henty’s evidence under cross-examination and considered the footage and relevant law, the Judge concluded that:


Henty had parked his vehicle alongside the saboteurs’ vehicle of his own accord.


He had got out of his vehicle voluntarily.


He had chosen to film the encounter.


He had continued the interaction of his own accord.


He had not contacted the police immediately, instead reporting the incident to 101 approximately two hours later.


These circumstances were central to the Judge’s assessment of Henty’s claim that he had experienced fear, alarm and distress. Following Henty’s evidence and cross-examination by the prosecution and defence, the case concluded without our hunt saboteur needing to take the stand.


The verdict

:

Not guilty. Acquitted.


After all the allegations, the police involvement, the CPS proceedings and the considerable expenditure of public resources, the case ended in an acquittal. A considerable amount of time, money and public resources had been spent pursuing this matter, only for the court to reach a conclusion that raises serious questions about why the prosecution was pursued in the first place.


Hunt saboteurs will not be intimidated out of exposing illegal hunting. And they will not be silenced by allegations that cannot withstand scrutiny in court.


The South Suffolk One stands vindicated.


SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!


South Suffolk Hunt Sabs remain steadfast and will not be intimidated or silenced.


Show some support to

South Suffolk Hunt Sabs.

SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!

Hunt Saboteurs Association

We are dedicated to animal liberation. This means we work with groups locally, nationally and worldwide who fight to end domination and injustice.

We take direct action peacefully when needed on the fields to stop the hunt and slaughter of our wildlife. Not everyone can join us on the fields but anyone can play an important role. Fundraising and raising awareness are as important as the sabbing itself.


Support Hunt Saboteurs Sweden here:

www.firefund.net/savethewolves2027

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als weibliches Rind in der Milchindustrie zu leben
content:
Die Milchindustrie ist ein grausamer Kreislauf des Leids und endet mit einem gewaltvollen Tod.


Wie fühlt es sich an, in dieses System hineingeboren zu werden, ohne die Möglichkeit, dem zu entkommen?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Auch du sollst Kinder gebären, immer wieder, damit du Milch produzierst. Milch, die dann von Menschen, statt von deinem Kalb konsumiert werden kann.


Du wirst fixiert, während jemand das Besamungsgerät in deine Vagina sowie seinen Arm in deinen Anus einführt. Wenn die Zwangsbefruchtung nicht beim ersten Mal zur Trächtigkeit führt – was oft der Fall ist –, wird dieser Vorgang mehrfach wiederholt.


Neun Monate – wie bei uns Menschen – wächst dein Kalb in dir heran. Du spürst eine Verbindung, merkst, wie es sich bewegt und immer größer wird. Je schwerer du selbst wirst, umso stärker werden deine Gelenkprobleme. Die rutschigen und harten Spaltenböden, auf denen du fast dein ganzes Leben verbringst, führen oft zu Verletzungen.


Dann bringst du dein Kalb zur Welt. Um dich herum riecht es extrem nach Kot und Ammoniak, von den Ausscheidungen der Tiere.


Endlich ist es da, noch ganz nass und schwach. Du leckst ihm über das Fell, um es zu wärmen. Es sucht deine Nähe und will an deinem Euter die für ihn so wichtige Erstmilch trinken. Sie stärkt sein noch schwaches Immunsystem und gibt ihm Kraft. Doch dann kommen die Arbeiter*innen.


Sie zerren dein noch ganz wackelig stehendes Kalb weg von dir. Es ruft nach dir. Du versuchst, bei ihm zu bleiben, aber du hast keine Chance. Die Menschen haben es weggebracht – du wirst es wahrscheinlich nie wiedersehen und nach nur zwei Monaten direkt wieder gewaltvoll befruchtet.


Du wirst nach der Geburt monatelang mehrmals täglich in den Melkstand getrieben – und die meiste Zeit davon bist du bereits wieder schwanger. Dein Körper muss gleichzeitig ein neues Kalb versorgen, das in dir heranwächst, und täglich über 22 Liter Milch produzieren. Dein Euter und deine Zitzen schmerzen. Aufgrund der extremen Überzüchtung produzierst du viermal so viel Milch, wie du es natürlicherweise für dein Kind tun würdest.


Die Prozeduren und Haltungsbedingungen zehren stark an deinem Körper. Dein Euter ist entzündet und schmerzt bei jeder Berührung. Andere Tiere humpeln, weil ihnen jeder Schritt wehtut. Viele sind schwach und ausgelaugt.


Wenn du nicht schon vorher stirbst oder getötet wirst, weil dein Körper nicht mehr kann, dann wirst du voraussichtlich nach nur fünf Jahren getötet – obwohl du unter natürlichen Bedingungen 25 Jahre alt werden könntest.


Dann kommt der Tag, an dem du als nicht mehr profitabel giltst. Du wirst aus dem Stall getrieben – das erste Mal nach Jahren verlässt du ihn, aber das ist kein Grund zur Freude.


Zusammen mit anderen erschöpften „ausgedienten Milchkühen“ wirst du auf einen Transporter verladen. Du hast Mühe, über die Rampe zu gehen. Deine Gelenke schmerzen vom jahrelangen Stehen auf Spaltenböden. Im engen Transporter stehst du dicht an dicht mit den anderen Tieren, der Lkw wackelt. Manche fallen hin und werden versehentlich getreten. Eure Fahrt in den Schlachthof dauert mehrere Stunden, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung, ohne Pause.


Angekommen erwartet dich ein brutaler Tod. Überall riecht es nach Blut, du bekommst Panik, aber es gibt keinen Ausweg. Dann ein Bolzenschuss in deinen Kopf. Wenn die Betäubung korrekt durchgeführt wurde und wirkt, brichst du zusammen. Wenn nicht, kann es sein, dass du bei Bewusstsein und unter extremen Schmerzen erlebst, wie dir deine Kehle aufgeschnitten wird und du verblutest.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Mutterrinder in der Milchindustrie erleiden müssen.


Der wahre Preis von Milch


Ein Ermittler von Animal Equality hat mehrere Monate undercover in einem deutschen Milchgewinnungsbetrieb gearbeitet und den Alltag der Tiere dokumentiert. Was unsere Undercover-Recherche zeigt, ist der wahre Preis von Milch: Ausbeutung, Gewalt, Schmerz, Leid und Tod.


Auf unserer Webseite erfährst du mehr und kannst die Stellungnahme des Betriebs nachlesen:


Zur Undercover-Recherche


Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht!


Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel. Im Supermarkt findest du zahlreiche Alternativen zu Milch, wie:


Hafermilch – mild, cremig, perfekt für Kaffee und Müsli (oft die günstigste Option!)


Sojamilch – proteinreich, ideal zum Kochen und Backen


Mandelmilch – leicht nussig, besonders lecker in Smoothies


Reismilch – süßlich und gut verträglich …

author: PETA-Team
title: Neue Aufdeckung: Kamele in Marokko für Tourismus missbraucht
content:
Recherchen von PETA Asien dokumentieren immer wieder wie

Kamele

 in der marokkanischen

Tourismusindustrie

 ausgebeutet werden. Die Tiere, die für Ausritte ausgenutzt werden, werden geschlagen und ohne Schutz vor der Witterung angebunden. Sobald sie keinen Profit mehr einbringen, werden sie im Schlachthaus getötet. Erfahren Sie hier, wie es den Kamelen in Marokko geht und was Sie dagegen tun können. 


PETA Asien deckt erneut auf: Missbrauch von Kamelen in Marokko  


PETA Asien hat 2026 erneut die Misshandlung von Kamelen am Rande der Sahara in Marokko aufgedeckt, wo die Betreiber:innen sie zwingen, Tourist:innen durch die trockenen Wüstendünen zu tragen:  


Die Tiere sind außerhalb ihrer Einsätze häufig angekettet und schutzlos extremer Hitze, intensiver Sonneneinstrahlung und Sandstürmen ausgesetzt. 


Viele Kamele verbringen einen Großteil ihres Lebens isoliert und haben kaum die Möglichkeit, sich frei zu bewegen oder Sozialkontakte zu pflegen.  


Die Kamele werden meist nur dann von ihren Ketten befreit, wenn sie kurz Wasser trinken dürfen oder um weitere Tourist:innen durch die Wüste zu tragen. Ein Kamel wurde dabei beobachtet, wie es nicht nur zum Trinken, sondern auch zu einem Pfosten rannte, um sich dort zu kratzen. Es wurde jedoch zurück zu seinem Anbindeplatz gejagt.  


Tierhalter:innen schlugen Kamele wiederholt mit Peitschen, traten sie und zerrten gewaltsam an ihren Schwänzen. 


Kamele sind intelligente, soziale Wesen mit eigenen Bedürfnissen, Wünschen und Interessen. Wenn sie frei in ihrem natürlichen Lebensraum umherstreifen, leben sie in Herden und kommunizieren miteinander durch Laute und Körperbewegungen. Als Zeichen der Freundschaft blasen sich Kamele manchmal gegenseitig ins Gesicht. In der Tourismusindustrie müssen diese Tiere ein Leben lang Elend und Leid ertragen.


 PETA Asien Recherche aus dem Jahr 2025


Bereits 2025

veröffentlichte

PETA Asien

 Videomaterial, dass die Ausbeutung und Misshandlung von Kamelen in Marokko dokumentiert.

Das beunruhigende Video zeigt Kamele, die an nur wenigen Meter langen Seilen angebunden sind. Ein Betreiber wurde dabei gefilmt, wie er ein gefesseltes Kamel wiederholt mit einem langen Stock schlug, während das Tier versuchte, den Schlägen auszuweichen. Ein weiterer Betreiber erklärte den

Ermittler:innen

, dass Kamele, die bis zu 40 Jahre alt werden können, in der Regel etwa fünf Jahre lang ausgebeutet werden, bevor sie getötet oder als

Fleisch

 verkauft werden.


Globales Muster der Grausamkeit


Frühere PETA-Untersuchungen von Kamel- und Pferdebetrieben in Ägypten offenbarten ähnliche Misshandlungen: Tiere wurden blutig geschlagen, gezwungen, Menschen in brütender Hitze ohne Zugang zu Schatten oder Wasser zu tragen, und wie Müll entsorgt oder ins

Schlachthaus

 geschickt, wenn sie zu alt, krank oder verletzt waren, um noch „nützlich“ zu sein. Airbnb, booking.com, Klook, Marriott und viele andere Unternehmen erklärten sich bereit, die Werbung für Tierfahrten bei den Pyramiden von Gizeh einzustellen, nachdem sie von PETA über das Leid der Tiere informiert worden waren.


So können Sie Tieren in der Tourismusindustrie helfen


Tourist:innen, die für Kamelritte bezahlen, halten diese herzlose, unmenschliche Industrie am Laufen. Wenn Sie einen Urlaub planen, vermeiden Sie Angebote mit Tieren und entscheiden Sie sich für tierfreundliche Alternativen. Unterstützen Sie unsere Petition, um das Leid der Kamele und Pferde bei den ägyptischen Pyramiden zu stoppen.  


		Jetzt unterschreiben!


The post

Neue Aufdeckung: Kamele in Marokko für Tourismus missbraucht

 appeared first on

PETA Deutschland e.V.

.

author: hsa_oryx
title: OCTOBER ROUND UP
content:
First conviction under Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023


October kicked off with

Glasgow Hunt Sabs

 reporting that Claire Bellamy, ex-huntswoman and former Master of the Lauderdale Hunt, was found guilty under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023. Footage which was obtained by sabs shows hounds chasing a fox outside the area covered by a licence that had been granted by NatureScot, and was described by the judge as “

gut wrenching

.” This is the first ever conviction under the new Scottish legislation and you can learn more about the legislation in Scotland and what led to Claire’s conviction

here.


Claire Bellamy found guilty of deliberately hunting a fox with dogs in January 2025.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs


Drone theft


On the 3

rd

 of October Dorset Borders Sabs reported that their drone had been stolen by The Cattistock Hunt as they hunted in Corscombe, Dorchester. The last image visible on the drone was a known member of the hunt running towards it in a field. The incident has been reported to the police and thanks to the generosity of supporters

Dorset Borders Sabs

 raised enough funds to replace the drone.


What do you do when you receive a CPW? If you’re a fox hunt then you break it as soon as possible of course


It didn’t take the Four Burrow Hunt long to break their Community Protection Warning (CPW) which had just been freshly issued by Devon and Cornwall Police. On the 10

th

 of October the hunt was caught breaking condition 7 of the CPW, by failing to give police 24 hours’ notice of their meet. As they had failed to give the details of the meet this means they won’t have provided a map of their “trail” meaning they will have broken more conditions that just number 7. It remains to be seen what action the police will take.

Read our recent article about CPW’s.


Four Burrow Hunt were issued with a CPW after years of trespass and livestock worrying.

Image:


Kernow Sabs, Monitors and Animal Rights Team-Cornwall


Stag hunting horror continues


The horror of stag hunting has continued to escalate in the south west. On the 12

th

 of October the Quantock Staghounds hunted a stag towards the A39 between Nether Stowey and Holford. This is a stretch of road where the hunt are continually causing chaos and putting people’s lives in danger.


This particular incident resulted in a

hunted stag running across the road and colliding with a car.

 A witness described how the terrified stag “

was flipped over the top of the car. Its leg kicked out smashing the rear nearside window. The Stag landed heavily on the verge.”

 Luckily the woman driving and her small child were not hurt but were badly shaken up.


The cruelty doesn’t end there. Two weeks later

North Dorset Hunt Sabs

 reported that the Quantock Staghounds had once again inflicted sickening suffering and pain on a stag. This particular large stag had a visibly infected wound on his side and it is also suspected he had a broken leg. These injuries unfortunately indicate that it is likely the stag that was hit by the car. Despite these injuries the hunt continued to torture him, subjecting him to a chase through thick gorse which no doubt would have caused him unbearable pain.


A stag hunted and terrorised by the Quantock Staghounds.

Credit: North Dorset Hunt Sabs


On the 22

nd

 of October hunt master of the Quantock Staghounds, Christopher Gibbons and huntsman Martin Watts, appeared at Taunton Magistrates Court. Gibbons is facing two counts of hunting a wild mammal under the Hunting Act, and Watts is facing one relating to the barbaric five-hour chase and ultimate

killing of a stag on the 23

rd

 of April 2026

. Both have pleaded not guilty and the case has been adjourned until the 18

th

 of January 2027 for a case management hearing; no trial date has been set. In the meantime, the Quantock Staghounds are continuing to commit abhorrent levels of animal cruelty whilst putting the safety of the general public at great risk.


This stag was tortured for five hours and ultimately killed on the 23

rd

 of April by the Quantock Staghounds.

 Huntsman and hunt master have both pleaded not guilty to charges under the Hunting Act.

Credit:


Mendip Hunt Sabs


They’re blatantly hunting foxes


Amidst the CPW’s, convictions, court hearings, road chaos and trespassing, foxes are still being chased, like the one pictured below.


Beds and Bucks Hunt Sabs

 along with

Peterborough Hunt Sabs

 have been keeping the pressure on …
