author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Administration Seeks to Strip 6.3 Million More People of SNAP Food Aid
content:
The proposed rule change comes as 34 percent of Americans report that they are suffering from food insecurity.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A proposed rule change by the Department of Agriculture (USDA) seeks to limit eligibility standards for some households with low incomes when it comes to automatic enrollment into the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), sometimes referred to as the food stamps program.

Currently, any household that receives cash or in-kind assistance from the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program is automatically enrolled into SNAP. The USDA proposal would change that, requiring individuals who receive TANF assistance to apply for SNAP separately.

The administration claims that cuts would occur “because their income or resources exceed the Federal statutory limits.” USDA’s draft proposal states that more than $44 billion would be saved by the changes, but admits that the cuts would kick 6.3 million people off of the program in its first year.

The formal notice was published on Monday. It requires a 30-day comment period before it can be fully implemented.

The changes to SNAP would follow similar cuts that were made last year, when Republicans and President Donald Trump passed the “One Big Beautiful Bill” Act into law. In the year after that act was passed, 5.1 million people lost SNAP eligibility, amounting to a 13 percent decrease in total participation and dropping enrollment numbers for the program to the lowest levels seen in almost two decades.

The new rule would be even more drastic, dropping participation by 17.6 percent from its current numbers.

Major cuts to SNAP have long been a goal of conservatives — indeed, changes to the program, like those being proposed this week by the Trump administration, were part of Project 2025, the Heritage Foundation-backed blueprint for how Trump should govern that was published during the 2024 presidential campaign.

Trump has claimed that he had nothing to do with Project 2025, but his administration has implemented over 55 percent of its published objectives so far, and two-thirds of his first round of executive orders were taken directly from the document.

The SNAP changes, if the administration does indeed move forward with them, come at a time when more Americans are becoming food insecure. According to one survey, more than a third of consumers (34 percent) reported that they have skipped meals or cut meal sizes for financial reasons over the past year — an 11 percent increase from the previous year’s rates.

Relief doesn’t appear to be coming anytime soon, as the latest federal inflation report, published Tuesday morning, indicates that costs on most goods continue to increase, despite Trump’s claims last week that “inflation is solved.”

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Democrats Demand Admin Stop Shredding Records Related to Trump’s DC Projects
content:
Reports find that the Interior Department has been routinely shredding official documents.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

House Democrats are demanding that key federal agencies and corporations retain their records after receiving a whistleblower report that the Trump administration is shredding records related to the president’s expensive, scandal-ridden construction projects around Washington, D.C.

CNN reports that administration officials are rushing to shred key paperwork before Democrats take charge of Congress in January. Democrats have pledged to conduct a wide variety of hearings and investigations into Trump administration actions, and are planning a “high-profile hearing on one or several projects early in the new Congress,” CNN reported.

President Donald Trump’s plans to build a massive arch and revamp the East Potomac golf course are two major areas of focus because Democrats believe they may be able to stop construction before it starts. The Trump administration, on the other hand, is trying to move as fast as possible on the president’s arch, golf course, Lafayette Square, and Tidal Basin projects before the new Congress is sworn in on January 3.

Huffman said the Democrats “have standing to go to court if we have to” over the projects, per CNN. “We’ll have tools to be able to stop a lot of it.”

The Interior Department has denied reports that it is violating federal records preservation requirements.

The Democratic push against the records deletions is more wide-ranging than just Trump’s D.C. projects, however.

On Monday, the House Natural Resources Committee’s top Democrat, Rep. Jared Huffman (California), sent letters to 36 federal agencies and corporate donors ordering them to preserve records and communications related to the committee’s investigation of the Trump administration and corporations that have donated to Trump’s projects. The records requests require a certification from recipients, and include requirements to recover lost records that may have been deleted.

“For two years, this administration has stonewalled us and kept the American people in the dark while Democrats have fought tirelessly to daylight and stop their corruption,” said Huffman in a statement. “I am sending a message to President Trump and his allies: our investigations will continue full steam ahead. And to every agency official and corporate executive receiving these letters: save everything.”

The committee, which oversees federal lands, is slated to take the lead on the investigations into the projects. It’s also working with the powerful House Oversight and House Judiciary committees on other as-yet unspecified investigations into the Trump administration.

Agencies that received letters from the Democrats include the Department of Agriculture, Department of Interior, and Department of Commerce. Non-governmental recipients include military contractors like Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Oracle, and Palantir, as well as other entities like ExxonMobil, Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), and UnitedHealth Group.

Huffman’s office cited a report from August by Politico that found that the Interior Department has “devolved into secrecy” and hemorrhaged staff under Doug Burgum. The agency, which oversees federal lands and agencies like the National Parks Service, has blocked over 100 projects being undertaken at national parks while working to help fast-track Trump’s D.C. projects, even sometimes against court orders.

That report found that Interior Department officials have “routinely shredded official documents and use disappearing Signal messages — even for mundane scheduling matters — to avoid communications being preserved, as is required by the Federal Records Act.”

Burgum has created an environment of paranoia, apparently asking for the installation of a second sensitive compartmented information facility (SCIF) in the building. A SCIF is a unit used to house and access classified government information, typically used by the Department of Defense.

“They’re terrified of written records,” one former Interior Department official told Politico.

author: David Venn
title: Preparations for Nunavut devolution entering ‘final phase,’ premier’s office says
content:
Preparations for devolution are entering “their final phase,” Nunavut Premier John Main’s office said Tuesday in a news release.


The release provides an update on the Government of Nunavut’s devolution process, which will see control over a vast majority of Crown land in the territory

transferred

 to the GN.


To enable devolution, Nunavut must

mirror

 six pieces of federal legislation: The Waters Act, Public Lands Act, Archaeological and Palaeontological Sites Act, Surface Rights Tribunal Act, Nunavut Planning and Project Assessment Act, and the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act.


MLAs passed four of those acts through second reading during the fall sitting of the legislative assembly. They include the Waters Act, the Surface Rights Tribunal Act, Public Lands Act and Archaeological and Palaeontological Sites Act.


The final two bills will be tabled during the winter sitting, said the release.


Work is also ongoing to create a new Department of Mines, Natural Resources and Land. The department has a new organizational structure and Inuktitut name: Nunalirijikkut.


“Many Nunavummiut who will work in the new department are currently employed by the [federal government],” the release said, adding that the deadline for such employees to respond to the GN’s job offer is Nov. 22.


“Their knowledge and technical expertise are highly valued.”


The GN is also offering training through the Namminiqsurniq Professional Project Administrator Program to boost Inuit employment, according to the release.


The federal and territorial governments are finalizing the transfer of properties, staff housing, vehicles and records, the release said.


Devolution is

set to take place

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Israeli Apartheid-Linked Firms Win UK Contracts Despite Sanctions Pledge
content:
Companies with links to illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank have won £10.7m worth of UK government contracts since Ed Miliband’s

pledge to sanction businesses

 facilitating the settlements.


The foreign secretary said on 8 September that Andy Burnham’s government would “take action” against companies and individuals involved in settlement activities.


“To those who finance or facilitate illegal settlements, let me say this: you will face the full force of UK sanctions,” he said, adding: “Settlements are illegal.”


But businesses

named and shamed by the UN

 for their involvement in Israeli settlements have since been awarded new public sector contracts,

analysis by Tussell for Al Jazeera shows

. 


The vast majority were signed with Heidelberg Materials, a German-headquartered firm. It has been granted 14 UK contracts worth £10.4m since Miliband announced sanctions. 


“Britain cannot credibly claim that it is imposing sanctions on Israeli settlements while letting contracts continue through the back door,” said former Labour leader and Your Party MP Jeremy Corbyn. 


“The fact that public money is still going to firms that could be targeted under the government’s own sanctions regime… is outrageous and frankly insulting to the public.”


Heidelberg operates an Israeli subsidiary, Hanson Israel, which runs a quarry on land belonging to the Palestinian villages of

Al-Zawiya and Rafat

. In the UK, materials from Heidelberg will be used to resurface roads in Nottingham and Lincolnshire.  


Two contracts worth about £87,900 were granted to Motorola Systems to provide communications for the police service. The US company is the sole provider of the Israeli military’s 4G cellular network,

according to the Who Profits

 research centre. 


Companies Fosun and Egis were also flagged in the Al Jazeera report for taking home contracts worth more than £100,000 each. Heidelberg, Motorola and Fosun did not respond to Al Jazeera’s requests for comment whilst Egis said it “formally expressed its disagreement” with being included in the UN database.


Novara Media contacted the UK foreign office for comment.

author: Unknown
title: YPG internationalist Konstantin Gedig remembered in Kiel
content:
This Saturday, the seventh annual commemoration of Konstantin Gedig – Şehîd Andok Cotkar was held in Kiel. Andok was martyred on October 16, 2019, in an attack by the Turkish Air Force on the western Kurdish border city of Serêkaniyê (Ras al-Ain), in violation of international law. Since 2016, he had fought against the Islamic State (ISIS) as a member of the People’s Protection Units (YPG). To this day, Andok’s killing has had no political consequences for Turkey, a NATO member, and there is still no information about the whereabouts of Konstantin’s body.


Shortly after 3 p.m., the Kurdish Community Center in Kiel was filled to capacity. More than 100 friends, comrades and family members gathered in the hall, lovingly decorated with flowers, flags and photographs, to commemorate Konstantin Gedig – Şehîd Andok Cotkar and remember his struggle. They came to remember Konstantin, the humorous and lively person, the son, the friend, the brother, the farmer, the student of Kurdish, the medic and the fighter for justice. They also came to remember the struggle for freedom waged against ISIS and Turkey’s war of aggression. In this struggle, Andok and 11,000 other fighters lost their lives, while 19,000 were wounded, in an effort to protect the lives of countless others.


“When you lose your child, every memory is sacred”


In a moving speech, Konstantin’s mother, Ute Ruß, once again described how the family had experienced his journey to Rojava. On September 1, 2019, Konstantin contacted his family to say that he was on his way to Sulaymaniyah to join the fight against ISIS. From that moment on, time took on a different meaning for the family: researching the political situation in North and East Syria, searching for photographs of Andok and hoping for signs that he was alive.


Since his killing seven years ago, their daily lives have been shaped by efforts to reconstruct Andok’s final moments, the search for his body and the struggle for justice. Even today, new information about Andok, a fighter and frontline medic, continues to emerge: small mementos handed over to the family, stories shared by fellow fighters and photographs brought to them. This year’s invitation to the commemoration, for example, features a photograph of Andok taken in the summer of 2017, which filmmaker Pedro Brito da Fonseca gave to the family.


The struggle for justice is directed against what the family describes as deliberate attempts by the Turkish and German governments to erase the memory of Andok. Ute Ruß spoke in harrowing terms: “Nothing terrible is impossible. The Turkish state’s treatment of fallen enemies is profoundly degrading. Graves and bodies are desecrated on an unimaginable scale. Families have to beg for the return of their loved ones’ remains. A dead person is no longer treated as a human being; they are degraded, regarded as dirt in the eyes of the Turkish state.”


The search for Andok’s body has been made more difficult, according to the family, by the German government’s lack of interest and its unwillingness to confront Erdoğan. As a result, even seven years after Andok’s death, there is still no grave where his family can mourn him with dignity.


A special form of remembrance is the Konstantin Andok Literature Prize. Awarded since 2023, the prize is supported by Konstantin’s parents and was initiated by the Soli-Netz solidarity network, with contributors including Dario Azzellini, Yossi Bartal, Christian Baron, Jörn Boewe and Kerem Schamberger. Nearly 500 entries were submitted for the third edition of the competition, held under the motto “Speak. Write. Break the silence.”


During the commemoration, an excerpt was also shown from a laudatory speech delivered by Christian Baron at the most recent award ceremony. Baron emphasized that, under capitalism, literature and art must always take a stand against the existing order, exploitation, oppression and NATO wars waged in the name of Germany’s

raison d’état

.


The flower of Heval Andok


Musical performances accompanied the commemoration. As has almost become a tradition at these gatherings, 

Zana û Andok

 was sung, a tragic song about comrades Zana and Andok, who symbolize the pain and resistance of the Kurdish resistance movement. Following performances of 

Ez Nisêbin Tu Qamişlo

 and 

Çû

, everyone joined together to sing 

Bella Ciao

, including a verse rewritten in honor of Heval Andok.


Thus ended a deeply emotional, yet beautiful and defiant Saturday …

author: Unknown
title: Turkey steel factory explosion kills at least 16 people
content:
A fire broke out following an explosion at the HABAŞ Iron and Steel Factory in the Bozköy neighbourhood of Aliağa, Izmir. The death toll among workers has risen to 16, while 15 injured workers, four of whom are in critical condition, continue to receive treatment in hospital.


It was announced that search and rescue operations are continuing to reach four workers trapped beneath the rubble. According to initial assessments, the explosion is believed to have occurred when an overhead crane broke loose during the pouring of molten steel and fell into an electric arc furnace.


As part of the investigation launched into the incident, four public prosecutors have been assigned to the case, and five people have been taken into custody.

title: Call for truth and justice on the 21st anniversary of attack on Umut Bookshop
content:
The Şemzînan district organisations of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) and the Democratic Regions Party (DBP) held a press statement in front of the DEM Party’s district office to mark the anniversary of the bombing of Umut Bookshop on 9 November 2005. Civil society organisations from the district also took part in the event.


Reading the press statement, DBP District Co-Chair Senar Duyan said that the attack was not an isolated incident, but a significant turning point that once again brought to the fore the shadowy relationships within the state and illegal structures in Turkey’s recent political history.


Senar Duyan stated that an approach which regarded the Kurdish people’s identity, language, culture and demands for democratic freedoms as security threats had, for years, laid the groundwork for policies of denial, assimilation, repression and violence. He said these practices had inflicted deep wounds on society’s collective memory.


Emphasising that the dark events of the past must be confronted if the Peace and Democratic Society Process is to have any genuine impact, Senar Duyan called for the truth to be brought to light and for policies of impunity to come to an end.


Duyan said: “ For the ongoing discussions on peace and a democratic society to have any genuine meaning, the dark pages of the past must be confronted, the truth must be brought to light, and policies of impunity must come to an end. We know that peace is built not by forgetting the past, but by confronting its pain, uncovering the truth and establishing justice. Shemdinli events of 9 November must be fully investigated and brought to light. This is a shared responsibility not only of the people of Şemdinli, but of everyone who stands for a democratic and just future.”

title: IOM: 3,834 displaced people return home in Iraq
content:
Pascal Reyntjens, Chief of Mission of the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Iraq, issued a statement on the return of displaced people to their homes in Iraq.


Reyntjens said that the organization continues to coordinate with the Iraqi government on closing displacement camps and facilitating the integration of displaced people, with the participation of government institutions, United Nations (UN) agencies and relevant organizations.


Reyntjens stated that the Iraqi government remains determined to consolidate the Behirkê and Dîbegê camps in Erbil (Hewlêr), along with three camps east of Mosul, into a single camp.


He added that the IOM, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and the Iraqi government continue to engage with camp residents to discuss possible solutions.


The IOM Chief of Mission in Iraq reported that 639 families, comprising 3,834 people, have returned to their homes or been relocated to other areas as part of integration efforts under the facilitated voluntary return program since the beginning of 2026. He added that financial assistance for camp residents is continuing.


The statement also noted that Iraq's Ministry of Migration and Displacement is overseeing the closure of camps in Sulaymaniyah (Silêmanî), with approximately 1,100 families having returned as part of the process. Most of these residents, primarily from Ashti Camp, have been resettled in the Dujail district of Saladin Governorate. Families meeting the eligibility requirements for return have received financial assistance of 4 million Iraqi dinars.

title: Duygu Özbay: Centralized exams deepen educational inequalities
content:
The Common Written Examination System introduced by the Ministry of National Education has drawn criticism from education workers. Teachers warn that centralizing examination procedures will diminish their decisive role in teaching and assessment, while disregarding differences in the physical, economic and social conditions of schools.


Teachers emphasize that the system is far from ensuring equal educational opportunities. They warn that a standardized approach to assessment, which fails to consider students' different learning conditions and needs, will further deepen existing inequalities in education.


Duygu Özbay, co-chair of Branch No. 2 of the Education and Science Workers' Union (Eğitim Sen) in Diyarbakır (Amed), spoke to ANF about the Common Written Examination System.


'Centralized exams make teachers passive'


Duygu Özbay said that the common examination system increases centralization in education and weakens teachers' decisive role in teaching and assessment.


Özbay said: "We have previously stated that the common examination system is highly centralized. The education system has become even more centralized with the introduction of the Turkey Century Education Model (Maarif Model), the Ministry of National Education's new national curriculum framework. We regard the common examination system as one of the methods used to implement this model. In a sense, the Ministry is trying to make the model appear more comprehensive and successful. However, making assessment and evaluation so centralized places teachers in a very passive position in the classroom.


When preparing examination questions, we take into account our students' readiness to learn, their living conditions, their specific needs, the physical conditions of the school and how prepared each child is to absorb particular knowledge. Every student's learning process is different. Educational policies must therefore take these differences into account. However, the centralized examination system operates without considering children's individual circumstances. It also removes teachers' decisive role in the classroom and establishes an even more centralized structure."


'

Children do not start from equal positions'


Duygu Özbay said that students do not begin their education under equal conditions. She emphasized that poverty, the denial of mother-tongue education, overcrowded classrooms and difficulties accessing education directly affect learning processes.


Özbay also said: "It is particularly important to recognize that children have different starting points. The learning conditions of a child studying in an overcrowded classroom are very different from those of a child studying in what we consider an ideal classroom of twenty students. There are also children who cannot receive education in their mother tongue. There are children living in poverty and others who cannot access educational opportunities. The education system must therefore recognize these different starting points and, above all, address the inequalities between them.


The right to education in one's mother tongue is one of the most important dimensions of these inequalities. Poverty is another. We are still confronted with the reality of children who have not been able to enter the education system. Our assessments in Diyarbakır show that there are still children who cannot attend school. Months have passed, yet many children remain excluded from education because school transportation services have not started and tenders for these services have not been completed. Subjecting these children to a common examination system before they have even gained access to education is itself a form of inequality.


We therefore believe that the problems within the education system must be resolved before children are subjected to this examination system. Children must enter the education system with equal opportunities. However, simply attending a classroom does not mean that a child benefits from equal educational opportunities. If schools and the education system continue to reproduce existing inequalities, that structure must first be changed. Children must be able to receive education in their mother tongue, develop their reading and comprehension skills, and participate in education according to their individual needs."

Students' learning conditions are being ignored'

title: Following in Şaristan's footsteps...
content:
Some people come into this world merely to breathe; others are born as the embodiment of an ideal. Martyr Şaristan represented a determined will that refused to surrender to the comfort of an ordinary life, even from her first breath, and carried storms within her soul. Her story is not simply the account of one person's life, but an epic tale of a land's suffering, a people's resistance and a woman's unwavering rebellion against the system.


Her childhood unfolded in a land where there was nothing ordinary about life. There was no room for being "ordinary" in the environment in which she grew up; one either stood tall or bowed down. Şaristan felt this reality deep within herself from a very young age. Even as a child, she was driven by a burning desire to stand on her own feet.


She was a child who possessed the courage to forge her own path rather than follow those laid out by others. The dignity she displayed when she took on her family's burdens and supported them despite financial hardship was the first sign of her iron will. The injustices she encountered at an early age and her confrontation with the true face of the enemy planted a seed of rebellion within her. Over time, that seed would grow into a mighty tree of resistance.


Her struggle did not begin in the present. It had started years earlier as a great battle for existence, through which a woman sought to prove that she would not be crushed by the machinery of the system. Standing against the system with such courage and determination required more than physical strength; it demanded extraordinary character and unwavering conviction. Şaristan had developed that strength of character.


She rejected the role of the "silent woman" imposed on her by the system and chose instead to become the architect of her own freedom.


The years she spent in prison were not a breaking point for her. Rather, they became a fortress in which her spirit matured. She paid the price for her honorable resistance against the enemy's oppression behind the cold walls of prison, where she developed herself, remained faithful to her ideals and forged her spirit into steel armor.


By 2012, the hunger strikes had left deep marks on her body, but they had also strengthened her unwavering determination. That hunger strike was not merely a protest; it was a battle for existence against the darkness that had descended upon her people and their struggle. She continued her resistance without regard for the damage to her body, the pain or the exhaustion, demonstrating the unshakable strength of her character. Time did not simply pass behind those walls. Şaristan emerged from prison as a pioneer.


Then the mountains of freedom called to her. By the time she was released from prison at the end of 2012, Şaristan was no longer the person she had once been. She was a fighter who had come to understand the impossibility of living within the system and knew the price of freedom. She entered the mountains not as a new student, but as an experienced pioneer who could guide others and whose every step was deliberate. Her character was so strong that she earned a special place in the hearts and minds of her comrades as someone sincere, pure-hearted and inspiring.


She knew not only how to fight, but also how to complement her comrades, clear the way for them and fill every gap through self-sacrifice. She understood that helping a comrade meant fulfilling one's own struggle. Overcoming an obstacle in a comrade's path was, for her, one of the greatest steps she could take along her own.


Today, when we remember her, we recall not only her smiling face but also her upright stance, unwavering courage and the heart with which she filled every void with a spirit of comradeship. When I watched the last footage of her recorded in the war tunnels, I saw more than an "end." In her eyes, I saw the radiance of victory, the light of freedom and an unmistakable message: "Either we will live through resistance, or, if death is inevitable, it must be an honorable death."


Those words are not a cry that calms the storm within me, but one that transforms it into an even greater ideal. Our martyrs have only one wish: to live freely or die with honor. The history of our struggle is built upon this unshakable truth.


We are not the true owners of this path. We are merely those entrusted with the path they left behind. The martyrs are the true owners of this struggle, and by walking this path, they transformed …

title: Dilan Kunt Ayan: Abdullah Öcalan is the coordinator of the process
content:
Budget discussions began amid protests as Justice Minister Akın Gürlek arrived at the parliamentary commission. MPs from the New Party protested by refusing to shake hands with Gürlek, while MPs from the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) held placards featuring photographs of Figen Yüksekdağ, Selahattin Demirtaş, politicians imprisoned in the Kobanê trial and Can Atalay.


DEM Party MPs also displayed photographs of Rojin Kabaiş and seriously ill prisoner Tuncer Sağlam, alongside placards reading "Rojin Kabaiş did not commit suicide" and "You have a budget, but no justice."


DEM Party MP Ömer Faruk Gergerlioğlu interrupted Minister Gürlek's presentation, protesting, "We did not come here to listen to stories."


'Lawlessness is everywhere'


DEM Party MP Dilan Kunt Ayan said that Turkey was experiencing a crisis of justice alongside its economic crisis. She recalled that Gürlek had declared upon taking office that he was the justice minister of all 86 million people. Ayan said that this declaration had not been reflected in practice, stressing that people from every section of society were seeking justice and facing unlawful practices.


Ayan referred to the Law on National Solidarity and Strengthening Social Integration, adopted by Parliament on 20 August 2026, and criticized the work of the commission established under the law. She said that holding only two meetings was insufficient and emphasized that responsibility for peace could not be postponed.


'Why are imprisoned politicians still behind bars?'


Dilan Kunt Ayan criticized the continued imprisonment of Selahattin Demirtaş, Figen Yüksekdağ, politicians imprisoned in connection with the Kobane trial, Can Atalay, Tayfun Kahraman and Osman Kavala. Ayan condemned the failure to implement rulings by the Constitutional Court and the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR), calling on the justice minister to provide an explanation.


She argued that there were no legal obstacles to the release of the imprisoned politicians and told the minister, "As justice minister, you are obliged to answer this."


'Peace carries responsibilities'


Dilan Kunt Ayan emphasized the need to advance the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that thousands of families had suffered because the necessary courage had not been shown in the past. She argued that the process should not be shaped by militaristic approaches or statements from small groups.


Ayan referred to Abdullah Öcalan's Call for Peace and Democratic Society on 27 February, saying that he had effectively been directing and coordinating the process. Ayan said, "Mr. Öcalan made the Call for Peace and Democratic Society on 27 February. Since that day, he has effectively been directing and coordinating this process. Mr. Öcalan is now the Coordinator of Peace and Political Participation in this process, and it is time to call this role by its proper name. We need to move beyond these debates and take the process further."


New Party Deputy Parliamentary Group Chair Gökhan Günaydın also demanded an explanation regarding an investigation into a list allegedly containing the names of 60 MPs and 30 ministers. Günaydın asked why the list had not been made public and why the investigation had not progressed.

title: PUK and New Generation file a lawsuit challenging parliamentary session in Hewlêr
content:
The dispute over the political leadership of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI) has now reached Iraq’s Federal Supreme Court. The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) and the New Generation Movement (Tevgera Nifşê Nû) have jointly filed a lawsuit challenging the parliamentary session held on November 4 in Hewlêr (Erbil). They are seeking to have the session and all decisions adopted during it declared invalid. At the center of the dispute is the election of the parliamentary leadership, which the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) pushed through without reaching an agreement with the other major political forces.


According to Hemdad Şahin, spokesperson for the New Generation Movement, who spoke to Shafaq News on Tuesday, the lawsuit has been officially registered with the Federal Supreme Court. The two parties argue that the session was held in violation of the prescribed procedures for convening parliament and therefore lacked a lawful basis. A court ruling is still pending.


Disputed majority in the election of the parliamentary leadership


The legal dispute stems from the November 4 session, through which the KDP sought to resume parliamentary proceedings that had remained largely paralyzed since the 2024 regional elections. A total of 52 out of 100 MPs attended the session. This meant that the quorum required for parliamentary business was narrowly met, although several major parliamentary groups did not participate.


The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan, the New Generation Movement and other opposition parties had boycotted the session because no agreement had been reached beforehand on how parliamentary proceedings should move forward. Nevertheless, the KDP succeeded in holding the election of the parliamentary leadership. Vala Farid was elected Speaker of Parliament, Rami Nouri Deputy Speaker and Muna Qahveci Secretary. Several MPs affiliated with the boycotting parties attended the session in defiance of their parties’ decisions, helping to secure the narrow majority.


These circumstances lie at the heart of the dispute. While the KDP defends the election by pointing to the quorum achieved and the parliamentary rules of procedure, the parties filing the lawsuit dispute whether the session was lawfully convened in the first place. Iraq’s Federal Supreme Court will now be tasked with determining whether a numerically sufficient majority also met the legal requirements for a valid election of the parliamentary leadership.


Parliamentary deadlock since the 2024 elections


The fact that the dispute has now reached the courts reflects a political crisis extending far beyond the appointment of the parliamentary leadership. Since the regional elections on October 20, 2024, the major parties have failed to reach an agreement on forming a new government. The KDP won 39 seats in the elections, the PUK secured 23 and the New Generation Movement obtained 15. Consequently, no single party holds a parliamentary majority.


In particular, disagreements over the allocation of key government positions and the future balance of power between the KDP and PUK have repeatedly stalled negotiations. Although the new parliament held its inaugural session in December 2024, no government has been formed. The KDP’s decision to proceed with the election of the parliamentary leadership in early November without a broader political agreement further intensified the conflict.


The PUK responded by announcing that it would not recognize the session or its outcomes. On November 6, party leader Bafel Talabanî announced his party’s withdrawal from the existing regional government. The dispute over parliamentary procedures thus escalated into an open confrontation over the future cooperation of the two parties that had previously governed together.


Court ruling could force new negotiations


While political divisions remain entrenched, efforts are also underway to resume dialogue. KDP leader Masoud Barzani called on the PUK on Monday to engage in fresh talks. However, no agreement is yet in sight. By filing a joint lawsuit, the PUK and the New Generation Movement have made clear that they are unwilling to accept the parliamentary decisions imposed by the KDP as the basis for further negotiations.


The consequences of the legal proceedings will now depend on the Federal Supreme Court’s ruling. If the court declares the November 4 session and the election of the parliamentary leadership invalid, the parliamentary leadership will have to be …

title: Iraqi Martyrs Foundation: 85 mass graves have been opened in Shengal
content:
More than twelve years after the genocide committed by the so-called Islamic State (ISIS) against the Yazidi population of Shengal, efforts to exhume and identify the victims continue. According to Iraq’s Martyrs Foundation, 90 mass graves have been discovered so far. Of these, 85 have been fully excavated, with the recovery of human remains and documentation completed. In total, the remains of around 700 people have been recovered.


Abdulilah Naili, head of the foundation, told the Iraqi daily newspaper Al-Sabah that 300 victims had been identified and their remains returned to their families. Identification was carried out through forensic DNA analysis. Genetic samples obtained from the mass graves were compared with blood samples collected from relatives during regular search and identification campaigns.


More mass graves may be discovered


According to Naili, work on the five remaining burial sites is expected to be completed within the coming months. This will mark the conclusion of investigations into the mass graves currently documented by the foundation. However, he said, it would not mean that the crimes had been fully investigated. Previously unknown burial sites could still be discovered during construction and reconstruction work in Shengal.


These figures differ from those published in late October by the Ministry of Martyrs and Anfal Affairs of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI). According to the ministry, 78 mass graves had been opened at that time, and the remains of 857 people had been recovered. Preparations for further exhumations were also announced. The respective statements do not explain the discrepancies between the figures reported by the two authorities.


Psychosocial support for families


The Iraqi Martyrs Foundation also stated that it had established a specialized unit to assist victims’ relatives. Psychologists and social workers are expected to support families receiving the remains of their murdered loved ones after years of uncertainty.


On August 3, 2014, ISIS launched an assault on Shengal and committed genocide against the Yazidi population. Thousands of people were murdered, while women and children were abducted and enslaved. Many families are still waiting to learn the fate of their loved ones.

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish organizations in Switzerland deny any links to criminal groups
content:
The Democratic Kurdish Council of Switzerland (CDK-S) and the Association of Kurdish Women in Switzerland (YJK-S) have firmly denied any links to criminal groups that publicly portray themselves as part of the Kurdish freedom movement. Their statement follows an investigation published on November 4 by Swiss public broadcaster SRF into alleged mafia-style networks with links to Basel and international operations. Subsequent media coverage repeatedly associated the groups in question with the Kurdish freedom movement and organizations affiliated with it.


In a joint statement on Tuesday, the two Kurdish umbrella organizations criticized the media for sometimes accepting the self-portrayals of criminal groups without sufficiently verifying their actual organizational ties. CDK-S and YJK-S specifically rejected allegations of cooperation with the group known as “Tolhildan” and other similar structures.


“No institutional ties whatsoever”


“We state unequivocally: We have no institutional ties whatsoever to Tolhildan or any other gang structures. These groups’ claims of affiliation with the Kurdish freedom movement cannot be regarded as evidence of any relationship with our organizations. We reject the misuse of our institutions’ names and symbols, or the values of our people’s struggle for freedom, to lend legitimacy to such groups.”


The organizations emphasized that the use of Kurdish symbols or references to political causes did not constitute evidence of actual organizational affiliation.


Warning against the recruitment of young people


The umbrella organizations expressed particular concern over attempts to recruit young people into criminal activities by appealing to their Kurdish identity and patriotic convictions. They called on Kurdish youth in particular to stay away from such groups and neither support nor participate in their activities.


“We must remain vigilant and resolute in the face of attempts to exploit Kurdish identity, patriotic sentiments and the shared values of our people to recruit young people. Our youth belong in spaces where free thought, solidarity, culture and democratic social struggle flourish.”


The organizations announced that they would use democratic and legal means to counter the spread of intimidation, violence and criminal networks of dependency. They stressed that the social achievements of the Kurdish community must not be exploited to advance private or criminal interests.


Criticism of unverified claims in the media


At the same time, CDK-S and YJK-S appealed to the media’s journalistic responsibility. They emphasized the need to distinguish claims through which criminal groups seek to portray themselves as politically legitimate from independently verified facts.


“We call on the media to distinguish between these groups’ self-proclaimed affiliations and verified information, to take into account the statements of our organizations, and to avoid sweeping associations of our people or democratic institutions with criminal organizations.”


In conclusion, the umbrella organizations called on families, young people and civil society organizations to work together to strengthen safe spaces for cultural activities, solidarity and democratic participation. The aim is to enable young people in particular to organize independently of criminal networks and participate actively in society.

author: Unknown
title: Hatimoğulları: This is not the first workplace killing at HABAŞ
content:
Tülay Hatimoğulları, Co-Chair of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), leveled serious accusations against the company and the relevant state authorities following the devastating explosion at the HABAŞ steel plant in Aliağa. The explosion at the iron and steel plant, located approximately 60 kilometers north of Izmir, killed 18 workers and injured another 18. Hatimoğulları described the disaster as a “workplace killing” and blamed years of failures in occupational safety measures.


After visiting the injured workers in hospital, Hatimoğulları traveled to the plant on Tuesday with a delegation. Speaking outside the factory, she stated that this was by no means the first fatal incident at HABAŞ. She recalled that eleven workers had lost their lives at the plant over the past ten years alone. She said there were serious indications that essential safety measures had not been implemented for a long time.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/0a66ee8f_20261110152022_2026-11-10-izmir-tulay-hatimogullari-dem-parti-es-genel-baskani-habas-is-cinayeti-aciklama-1.mp4


Two fatal incidents within just a few weeks


The explosion occurred on Monday morning while the plant was in operation. According to initial information from the Izmir Governor’s Office, an overhead crane broke loose during a casting operation and fell into an industrial furnace. The resulting explosion triggered a fire, sending thick clouds of smoke rising above the plant.


It was the third fatal incident within just a few weeks. In October, temporary worker Hakan Doğan fell from a height of approximately eight meters and lost his life. On November 5, 20-year-old temporary worker Eyüp Eğinli died when an explosion occurred while a tire on a piece of industrial machinery was being inflated. Including the victims of the latest disaster, a total of 20 workers have lost their lives at HABAŞ within a short period.


Hatimoğulları stressed that these deaths demonstrated the need for a comprehensive investigation into working conditions and the responsibility of the company’s management. She recalled previous court proceedings in which HABAŞ had been found to bear 70 percent of the responsibility for fatal workplace accidents. Those responsible had been sentenced to two years and six months in prison but had nevertheless been able to continue working at the company.


Call for the resignation of ministers and regulatory officials


The DEM Party Co-Chair therefore directed her criticism not only at the company’s management but also at the state authorities responsible for overseeing occupational health and safety. Despite repeated fatalities, she said, sufficient action was apparently not taken.


“The Minister of Labor and Social Security, the Director General of Occupational Health and Safety, the Minister of Industry and Technology, and the head of the supervisory and inspection authority, all of whom bear responsibility, must resign immediately. They must not remain in office for a single day longer,” Hatimoğulları declared.


The public prosecutor’s office has since launched an investigation into the explosion. According to Turkish Deputy Justice Minister Can Tuncay, arrest warrants have been issued for eleven individuals, including HABAŞ Chairman Mehmet Rüştü Başaran. Investigators are examining whether technical defects, inadequate maintenance or violations of safety regulations contributed to the disaster.


Criticism of continued production after the explosion


Meral Danış Beştaş, Co-Spokesperson of the Peoples’ Democratic Congress (HDK), also criticized the treatment of workers. She noted that while the search for victims was still underway at the plant, workers in another section of the factory were required to continue working. Beştaş described this as reflecting an attitude in which economic interests took precedence over the protection of human life, even in the face of numerous fatalities.


Beştaş called for a nationwide period of mourning to draw attention to the scale of the disaster and the continuing loss of life in workplace accidents. Hatimoğulları and Beştaş extended their condolences to the families of the workers who lost their lives and wished the injured a speedy recovery.


HABAŞ exports steel to Israel


The HABAŞ Group has also faced criticism over its trade relations with Israel. According to available information, the company has continued exporting high-quality steel to Israel since 2024. These business …

author: Unknown
title: DEM Party calls for climate justice instead of new profit opportunities as COP31 opens in Antalya
content:
At the start of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, the Ecology Commission of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) called for a fundamental transformation of international climate and energy policies. The commission argued that the climate crisis could not be overcome through market-based mechanisms but instead required a democratic and socially just restructuring of society’s systems of production and ways of life.


In a statement on Tuesday, the commission blamed the capitalist model of production and consumption for the ongoing destruction of the environment.


“Policies focused on unlimited economic growth, the exploitation of natural resources, deforestation and dependence on fossil fuels are exacerbating the crisis. Existing international climate agreements have failed to bring about binding changes. Instead, official climate negotiations have been reduced to market mechanisms and emissions trading.”


Criticism of Turkey’s energy policies


The DEM Party sees a fundamental contradiction between Turkey’s role as host of COP31 and its actual energy policies. Although Ankara is hosting the international climate conference, it still lacks a concrete and binding roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels, the party said, adding that the country continues to rely on coal and natural gas.


“The consequences of the climate crisis are distributed highly unequally across society. People living in poverty, workers, women, children, Indigenous peoples and local communities are particularly affected.”


The statement further noted that droughts, floods, forest fires, and water and food crises were exacerbating existing inequalities and forcing increasing numbers of people to flee their homes.


Energy transition under democratic control


As an alternative, the Ecology Commission called for a just and carefully planned phase-out of fossil fuels, democratic control over energy supplies and the protection of food sovereignty. According to the party, environmentally destructive projects must be halted.


“At the same time, those states and economic actors that have historically contributed the most to the climate crisis must fulfill their obligation to repay their climate debt,” the party demanded.


The commission stressed that climate justice could only be achieved if the social groups directly affected were able to participate in decisions concerning the necessary changes. These groups, it said, include local communities, farmers, workers, women, young people and environmental movements.


“The solution to the climate crisis does not lie in market mechanisms that create new profit opportunities for capital, but in building a democratic, egalitarian and ecological way of life that exists in harmony with nature and places society’s needs at its center,” the statement underlined.


Participation in the Peoples’ Climate Summit


The DEM Party announced that it would closely scrutinize the COP31 negotiations and actively participate in the preparations and events of the “Peoples’ Climate Summit.” The summit aims to provide a platform for social movements and communities affected by the climate crisis to develop their own demands and alternatives to the official negotiations.


“We will intensify our struggle for a future that places people rather than capital, life rather than markets, and ecological and social justice rather than profit at its center,” the Ecology Commission declared.

author: Unknown
title: PEN conference in Amed calls for recognition of the Kurdish identity, language and culture
content:
The international “Language and Peace” conference, held on November 6 and 7 in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır), has published its final declaration. Participants called for constitutional and legal guarantees of linguistic and cultural rights, recognition of Kurdish identity and the release of political prisoners. They also emphasized the responsibility of writers and intellectuals to stand up for truth, justice and lasting democratic peace.


Organized by PEN International, the Kurdish PEN Center and the municipal administrations of Amed, Sur, Yenişehir, Bağlar and Kayapınar, the conference was held under the theme “The Role of Literature, Language and Intellectuals in Processes of Dialogue, Peace and Equality.” The two days of discussions focused on the conditions necessary for social coexistence based on equal rights and recognition of different identities.


'Peace must not be reduced to disarmament'


In their final declaration, participants welcomed the ongoing efforts to achieve a peaceful resolution of the Kurdish question. They described calls for peace and corresponding political steps as necessary and positive developments. However, they emphasized that such efforts could only lead to lasting results if accompanied by legal guarantees and social change.


“For peace to be built on strong and lasting foundations, cultural and linguistic rights must be recognized, and conditions that enable freedom must be established,” the declaration stated.


The final declaration stressed that peace must not be defined solely in terms of laying down arms. Rather, it must encompass social equality and recognition of the political, social, economic, cultural and human rights of all people. According to the participants, coexistence within a common state and constitutional framework must also be based on equal rights, equal opportunities and free dialogue within society.


Call for recognition of Kurdish as a language of education and official use


One of the conference’s central demands concerns the legal status of the Kurdish language. Participants called for recognition of Kurdish identity, language and culture, as well as the establishment of the necessary conditions for their free development. This includes legal provisions guaranteeing the right to education in one’s mother tongue and ensuring the official use of Kurdish.


Linguistic equality must not be limited to symbolic recognition but must be reflected in the education system and public life, said the final declaration, which also rejected all forms of forced assimilation. In a society based on equality, it said, no one should be compelled to abandon their cultural identity or conform to another identity.


'Freedom for writers and political prisoners'


Alongside linguistic rights, the conference emphasized freedom of opinion and expression as a fundamental prerequisite for democratic peace. Particular significance was attached to the symbol of the “empty chair,” which PEN uses to draw attention to writers who are imprisoned, persecuted or prevented from freely expressing their views.


The empty chair serves as a painful reminder of the ongoing attacks on freedom of thought and human freedom, the declaration stated. PEN International and the Kurdish PEN Center therefore called for the immediate and unconditional release of all imprisoned writers, journalists and political prisoners.


“As long as critical thinkers and writers remain behind bars, no peace initiative can attain moral or democratic legitimacy,” the organizations declared.


'Literature becomes the voice of those who have been silenced'


The final declaration also emphasized the particular social responsibility of literature and culture. “Where political institutions reach their limits, literature can connect directly with people, bring experiences to light and foster mutual understanding. Literature becomes the voice of those who remain silent or whose voices have been forcibly silenced,” the declaration stated.


Participants reaffirmed their conviction that literature and culture are not merely secondary elements of political peace efforts but among their fundamental prerequisites.


“As writers and PEN representatives, we wholeheartedly believe that literature and culture are essential components of peacebuilding. We pledge never to place our pens in the service of conflict, hatred or chauvinism. Instead, we will use them with unwavering determination in the service of truth, justice and the …

author: Carlos Pérez
title: ‘This Isn’t Stopping’: A Rank-And-File Perspective on the Indefinite Strike for Public Education in Madrid
content:
Since October 14, teachers in Madrid, Spain, have been on an indefinite strike in defense of public education. After years of deteriorating conditions and systematic rank-and-file organizing, teachers have flooded the streets of Spain’s capital in a mass mobilization that has linked the fight for public education with the recent revolt around housing.


The shared struggle for housing and public education in Spain is now heading toward a general strike on November 11 in the midst of a broader uprising spreading throughout Europe.


Carlos Pérez, a North Carolina high school social studies teacher and Labor Notes board member, spoke with María, a secondary school teacher of history and geography in Madrid and a member of

Menos Lectivas

 (a group whose name means “Fewer Teaching Hours”), one of the leading rank-and-file forces behind the strike.


Pérez: Public school teachers in Madrid have been on an indefinite strike since October 14. What are the main issues that drove you and other teachers to call for a strike and what are your demands?


María:

 In the Community of Madrid, we have been dealing with cuts to public education since 2011. These have led to the deterioration of classroom conditions and the quality of education for students in the region.


A lack of resources and staff, high student-to-teacher ratios, an increase in direct teaching hours, and a failure to maintain or build necessary infrastructure have created a situation where teaching has become extremely difficult. We, as educators, are unable to adequately attend to all our students, and we have decided to take a stand against the institutional mistreatment that both we and our students are subjected to.


In my case, I’ve taught high school classes with 33 students; I had to find a classroom to accommodate my students every day for a month of heavy rain because the classrooms had leaks that kept them constantly wet; my students with special educational needs (autism or hearing and speech difficulties) were not supported by the necessary professionals because there was neither a social integration specialist nor a teacher specifically assigned to them; and of course, I work an enormous amount of unpaid and unrecognized overtime.


This is why we are demanding that the Community of Madrid reduce the number of instructional hours; lower the teacher-to-student ratios; end segregation, given that the Community of Madrid is the most segregated region in Spain in terms of education; increase salaries to bring them in line with current economic needs; and reduce bureaucracy, among other things.


Menos Lectivas

, a rank-and-file formation that includes several unions, has been a driving force behind the strike. What is Menos Lectivas and what role has it played in the strike?


Menos Lectivas

 was founded in 2023, inspired by groups like Labor Notes in the United States, with the goal of organizing education workers from within their workplaces and returning union power to the workers themselves. Since then, we have built our movement through assemblies held at individual workplaces.


In the years leading up to the indefinite strike, we organized strikes, demonstrations, and rallies. These actions helped the movement grow and, crucially, provided us with the institutional legitimacy—both with the workers, who view us as a legitimate force for struggle because they feel part of it through our assemblies, and with other unions, the media, and ultimately the government—to decide how, when, and where we would fight for the right to education and for our own labor rights.


From the outset, we knew that an indefinite strike would be our ultimate tool for union struggle if our demands went unheeded by the Community of Madrid. Last June, it was decided in an assembly that we, the teachers, would launch an indefinite strike.


Given that these assemblies held clear legitimacy, the other unions that were not part of

Menos Lectivas

 had no choice but to sit down with us on the Strike Committee to negotiate the establishment of a formal negotiating table and the terms of the strike.. This milestone is already a success; it has shifted power back into the hands of the workers, taking it out of the administrative offices.


How has the strike been received by students and their families?


Both families and students support our demands. Ultimately, they are the primary beneficiaries of the improvements we achieve. We feel very well supported by them, and …

author: Randi Beers
title: Expect office, road closures Wednesday for Remembrance Day
content:
Parts of downtown Iqaluit will be closed to traffic Wednesday morning to allow for a Remembrance Day ceremony and march to take place.


The closures will affect parts of Sivumugiaq Street and Mivvik Street starting at 9:30 a.m. until approximately 12 p.m., the City of Iqaluit announced Monday in a public service announcement.


“The closure is necessary to ensure the safety of participants and the public while the march is underway,” said the announcement.


The march, which starts at the RCMP detachment and ends at the cadet hall, is scheduled to start at 10:30 a.m.


Remembrance Day ceremonies are also planned in Rankin Inlet at the Singiituq Complex, from 10:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. and Cambridge Bay’s community hall at 10:30.


Government offices across the territory will also be closed to mark the day.


Remembrance Day is observed every year on Nov. 11 to honour armed forces members who have died in the line of duty.

author: Administrador
title: DI COSA SI TRATTA. COSA SÌ E COSA NO
content:
Attenzione a chi accompagna le Familias Buscadoras:

A.- Abbiamo rilevato una serie di confusioni, affermazioni infondate e tentativi di manipolazione riguardo agli obiettivi, alle date, ai luoghi e alle attività della delegazione della Commissione Sexta Zapatista per questi mesi di dicembre e per la prima settimana di gennaio del 2027.

Si parla e si diffondono notizie errate su un presunto incontro nazionale tra le famiglie delle persone scomparse, Familias Buscadoras, e la delegazione zapatista presso la cosiddetta “Glorieta de los Desaparecidos” il 6 dicembre, nonché su altre attività pubbliche della Commissione Sexta Zapatista in altri luoghi e in altre date.

Questo non è vero, compagne e sorelle buscadoras. Forse chi si riunisce in quel luogo o in altri, considerandoli punti di riferimento per la propria giusta lotta, terrà davvero un incontro, ma noi non vi parteciperemo.

Non solo perché “l’invito” che abbiamo ricevuto da loro denota ignoranza, malafede e maleducazione. Non si invita nessuno insultandolo. A tempo debito ne parleremo più approfonditamente. Ma anche perché non partecipiamo a raduni di massa con le familias buscadoras.

I gruppi, i collettivi e le familias buscadoras che si riuniscono nelle piazze o in qualsiasi altro luogo, possono incontrarci IN PRIVATO, gruppo per gruppo, presso la sede della delegazione a Città del Messico e nelle sedi che saranno rese note, registrandosi tramite il Frayba, nella data e nell’ora che preferiscono, se lo desiderano.

B.- Sentite, sia voi che noi, i popoli zapatisti, sappiamo che esistono non solo differenze, ma anche vere e proprie rivalità e controversie, persino tra i collettivi delle buscadoras, tra le reti e i movimenti. Si arriva persino a cercare di porre il veto su certi collettivi e a decidere chi può e chi non può incontrare la delegazione zapatista. Forse è per questo che cresce il numero delle familias buscadoras che non fanno parte di nessun gruppo o collettivo e che ci contattano direttamente.

Non vogliamo giudicare nessuno. Non vogliamo dire quale strategia sia giusta o sbagliata, quale sia legittima e quale no, quale sia buona e quale cattiva.

Riteniamo che chiunque cerchi la verità e la giustizia e abbia l’obiettivo di ritrovare la persona cara scomparsa a causa di una sparizione forzata possa e debba percorrere tutte le strade e bussare a tutte le porte per alleviare il proprio dolore.

Sia che conducano ricerche sul campo con piccone e pala; sia che si rivolgano alle autorità giudiziarie locali, statali e federali; sia che vogliano incontrare il capo dell’esecutivo federale o la sua piramide di funzionari; sia che organizzino campagne internazionali e nazionali; sia che riescano solo ad affiggere le foto dei loro cari scomparsi nelle strade e nei quartieri; sia che si rivolgano alle organizzazioni non governative per i diritti umani; sia che richiedano il sostegno di specialisti nella ricerca delle persone scomparse e nell’analisi dei resti umani; sia che ricorrano a marce, comizi, sit-in, occupazioni di edifici e blocchi di strade e autostrade; sia che preghino; sia che si lancino maledizioni; sia che si faccia tutto quanto sopra.

E sempre con la memoria come motore.

Qualunque cosa decidiate e facciate, è una decisione che spetta a voi, a coloro che portano quel dolore e provano quell’angoscia, e a nessun altro.

Quindi non vi diremo cosa fare né lo faremo al posto vostro. Vogliamo conoscervi, ascoltarvi, abbracciarvi.

Né intendiamo dire quale rete o gruppo sia migliore dell’altro.

C.- Per questo motivo il nostro percorso non privilegia né manifestazioni di massa, né eventi mediatici, né assemblee generali, né la creazione di alleanze, fronti o iniziative simili, né una nuova organizzazione che riunisca o includa tutti i collettivi e le familias buscadoras, o parte di essi.

Non discuteremo né dibatteremo nemmeno sul numero delle persone scomparse, che siano 135 mila o di più o di meno, perché quelle cifre hanno un nome, una storia, una tragedia, un dolore e un dovere: quello di cercare chi si ama, chi manca e, non di rado, chi è sangue del proprio sangue.

D.- L’obiettivo principale di questa iniziativa è quello di ascoltare ogni famiglia o gruppo di familias buscadoras che desideri raccontarci la propria storia e, soprattutto, la storia della persona scomparsa.

Perché noi abbiamo visto e ascoltato il loro cammino, i loro sforzi, i loro sacrifici, il loro non arrendersi nella ricerca, il loro non svendere il loro caro assente, il …

author: groundxero
title: দুনিয়া কাঁপানো শরৎকাল
content:
এরকম এক শরৎকাল প্রত্যক্ষ করার পর এক রকমের আশা জাগে – বসন্ত আসতে হয়তো বেশি দেরী হবে না।


 


দেবারতি


গুপ্ত

  


 


এ এক অন্য শরৎকাল এসে হাজির হয়েছে দুনিয়া জুড়ে। লেট ক্যাপিটালিজমের নখ দাঁত যেভাবে প্রকট হয়ে উঠেছে গত দুই দশকে তাতে সাধারণ মানুষের নাভিশ্বাস উঠতে শুরু করেছে। মিলেনিয়াল প্রজন্ম এই পরিস্থিতি একভাবে মোকাবিলা করেছে। তাদের যৌবনে তবু কিছু চাকরি ছিল মন ভোলানোর উপাদান ছিল। কোভিড পরবর্তী কালে যে প্রজন্ম যৌবনে পা দিয়েছে তারা পেয়েছে এক অবাক পৃথিবী। একদিকে সমাজ মাধ্যমের বিভ্রান্তিকর দুনিয়া আরেকদিকে নতুন হাজির হওয়া কৃত্রিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা। এইসবের মধ্যে দুনিয়াজোরা সরকারি শিক্ষা ব্যবস্থা, স্বাস্থ্য পরিষেবা আর কর্মসংস্থানের চূড়ান্ত বেহাল অবস্থা।


 


বছর দুই আগে থেকেই সার্বিয়ার ছাত্ররা বিক্ষোভ শুরু করেছিল। নোভি সাদ রেইল স্টেশনের ছাত ভেঙে ১৬ জনের মৃত্যু হওয়ায় ছাত্রদের বিরোধিতা শুরু হয়। ওই কান্ড নিছক দুর্ঘটনা বলে চাপা দেবার চক্রান্ত সহজে মেনে নেয় নি সার্বিয়ার ছাত্ররা। তারা আন্দোলন শুরু করে। সেই আন্দোলন দীর্ঘ ১৪ বছর ধরে ক্ষমতায় থাকা আলেক্সান্ডার ভুচিচকে সম্প্রতি গদিচ্যুত করেছে।


 


২৬ অক্টোবর, অর্থাৎ সার্বিয়ার ওই ঐতিহাসিক দিনে বেলগ্রেড থেকে এক সফটওয়্যার ইঞ্জিনিয়ার লাজার পেত্রোভিচ ‘কফি হাউস এক্সপেরিয়েন্স’ এর লাইভ পডকাস্টে এসেছিলেন। এই মুহূর্তে কলকাতা শহরে যেখানে প্রতিদিন ফ্যাসিজমের উপস্থিতি হাড়ে হাড়ে টের পাচ্ছি সেইখানে বসে সার্বিয়ার পার্লামেন্টের সামনে দাঁড়িয়ে উচ্ছ্বসিত লাজারকে দেখতে পাওয়া, নিঃসন্দেহে খুব আশাব্যঞ্জক ঘটনা। মজার কথা হল দক্ষিণপন্থী ভুচিচের এস এন এস (সার্বিয়ান প্রগ্রেসিভ পার্টি) দলের বিরোধী যে রাজনৈতিক দলগুলো – গ্রিন লেফট পার্টি বা ডেমক্রেটিক পার্টি এরাও ছাত্রদের দলের কাছে পাত্তা পায় নি। ক্ষমতাসীন বা তথাকথিত বিরোধী দুই পক্ষের প্রতিই গভীর অনাস্থা থেকে Student List বা Students Are Winning দলটি তৈরি হয়েছিল। লাজারকে জিগ্যেস করেছিলাম যে ছাত্র আর সার্বিয়ার সুশীল সমাজের যে প্রতিনিধিদের নিয়ে ওরা ক্ষমতায় এল তাদের রাজনৈতিক আদর্শ কি? লাজার জানালো ওদের গত দু বছরের লড়াই কোন নির্দিষ্ট রাজনৈতিক আদর্শের ভিত্তিতে গড়ে ওঠে নি। তাদের দেশের সংকট যেখানে পৌঁছেছিল তাতে শিক্ষা, স্বাস্থ্য আর নিরাপত্তার মতো মৌলিক অধিকার নিয়ে তাদের লড়াই করতে হয়েছে। লাজারের দেশের শাসনব্যবস্থা তথা রাজনীতি কোনদিকে এগোয় তা বোঝার জন্য আমরা নিশ্চই অধীর আগ্রহে তাকিয়ে থাকবো সার্বিয়ার দিকে।


 


এবার মুখ ফেরানো যাক বিপ্লবের পীঠস্থান ফ্রান্সের দিকে। সেখানেও ছাত্রদের নেতৃত্বে বিরোধিতা শুরু হয়েছে।


 


প্রায় দু’মাস হতে চলল ফ্রান্সে ছাত্র আন্দোলন চলছে। প্রাথমিক ভাবে যেটা শুরু হয়েছিল প্যারিসের এক শহরতলি এলাকার উচ্চ বিদ্যালয় বা Lycée-র ছাত্র-ছাত্রীদের মাধ্যমে, তা পরে আরও ব্যাপক ভূমিকা গ্রহণ করেছিল। শিক্ষক-শিক্ষিকারা, অধ্যাপক-অধ্যাপিকারা, স্কুল ছাড়াও কলেজ-বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের ছাত্র-ছাত্রীরা, তাদের অভিভাবকেরাও মিছিলে নিয়মিত সক্রিয় অংশ নিচ্ছিলেন। হাই স্কুল ছাত্র-ছাত্রীদের মূল দাবী ছিল সরকারি স্কুল গুলোর পরিকাঠামোর উন্নতি,  কারণ সরকারি স্কুলগুলোয় যথেষ্ট শিক্ষক নেই, ফলে একেকটা ক্লাসে একজন শিক্ষকের দায়িত্বে অনেক বেশি ছাত্র। স্কুল বিল্ডিং এর অবস্থা ক্রমশ খারাপ হয়ে পড়ছে। অতিরিক্ত গরমে বা অতিরিক্ত ঠান্ডায় সেই সব ঘরে ক্লাস করা খুব মুশকিল হয়ে পড়ছে। গত বাজেট সেশনে শিক্ষা ক্ষেত্রে বাজেট অনেক কমানো হয়েছে। ফলে এই সবকিছু নিয়েই ছাত্ররা বিক্ষুব্ধ। সম্প্রতি সরকার এদের কিছু কিছু দাবি মেনে নিয়েছে কিন্তু তবুও আন্দোলন থামেনি। কারণ ছাত্ররা বলছে এটা যথেষ্ট নয়। যা সমস্যা রয়েছে আরও গভীরে গিয়ে তার সমাধান করতে হবে। ফলে স্কুল কলেজ ব্লক করা অব্যাহত রয়েছেl এই ব্লক করার একটা নাম তারা দিয়েছে – ব্লকাস (Blocus)


 


কথা হচ্ছিল ফ্রান্সে বসবাসকারী অধ্যাপক সোমঋতা ভট্টাচার্যর সঙ্গে। সোমঋতা কঁ-নর্ম্যান্ডি ইউনিভার্সিটিতে (Université de Caen-Normandie) ইংরিজি পড়ান। অকে জিগ্যেস করেছিলাম, ম‍্যাক্রোঁর সেন্ট্রিস্ট সরকারের বিরুদ্ধে যদি আন্দোলন জারি থাকে তাহলে কি তা লা পেনের দক্ষিণপন্থী দলকে জোরদার করবে? না কি বামপন্থী জাঁ লুক মেলেশঁদলেরও সম্ভাবনা তৈরি করতে পারে?


 


সোমঋতা আন্দোলনের বিস্তারের কথা জানালো। প্রতিবাদী ছাত্র-ছাত্রীদের সঙ্গে শ্রমিকশ্রেণী যাঁরা ইয়েলো ভেস্ট (gillet jaune) মুভমেন্টে অংশ নিয়েছিলেন, অবসর প্রাপ্ত মানুষ যাঁরা কিছু দিন আগে অবস্র গ্রহণের বয়স বৃদ্ধির বিরুদ্ধে প্রতিবাদে অংশ নিয়েছিলেন, তাঁরা সকলে একে একে জড়ো হচ্ছেন। কারণ দ্রব্যমূল্য বৃদ্ধি, মানুষের ক্রয়ক্ষমতা কমে যাওয়ার সঙ্কট একটা ভয়াবহ আকার নিয়েছে। তবে আশার কথা এই যে, ছাত্র আন্দোলনে কিন্তু মেলেশঁর সমর্থক বেশি দেখা যাচ্ছে। নিয়মিত ছাত্রদের পাশে থেকেছেন মেলেশঁ, তাদের প্রতিবাদে অংশ নিয়েছেন। অন্যদিকে ছাত্রেরা স্পষ্ট ভাবে মারিন লো পেন এবং তাঁর অতি-দক্ষিণপন্থী দলের সমালোচনা করছে এবং প্রতিবাদী ছাত্ররা তাদের বিরোধী মিছিলে এমন কিছু পোস্টার নিয়েও এসেছে যেখানে পরিষ্কার লেখা রয়েছে, দক্ষিণপন্থী দলদের তারা কোনও ভাবেই সমর্থন করছে না এবং অতি-দক্ষিণপন্থীদের বিভেদ, বৈষম্যমূলক কার্যকলাপের সম্পূর্ণ বিরোধিতা করছে এবং ভবিষ্যতেও করে যাবে। অর্থাৎ সার্বিয়ার মতো ছাত্র বিক্ষোভ থেকে বিদ্রোহ ছড়িয়ে পড়েছে নানান ক্ষেত্রে। তবে ফ্রান্সে রাজনৈতিক আদর্শ …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Meet Will Lawrence: Sunrise Movement Co-Founder Elected to Congress on Anti-Data Center Platform
content:
Progressive candidate Will Lawrence of Michigan has defeated Republican incumbent Tom Barrett, flipping the state’s 7th Congressional District, a closely watched swing district that includes Lansing. Lawrence, the co-founder of the youth-led climate organization Sunrise Movement, refused corporate

PAC

 money, instead building a people-powered grassroots mobilization campaign. He focused on lowering the costs of housing and healthcare, opposing the war on Iran, and challenging the power of Big Tech.


“I’m fighting for a federal moratorium on new data center development, along with a pause on advanced AI development,” says Lawrence. “These developers come into small towns, and they say, ’We’re going to suck up a bunch of water. We’re going to use more energy than the current capacity of the grid. We don’t know what’s going to happen to your property values, but if everything goes well, we’re going to put 10 or 20 million people out of work, and if it goes poorly, we may kill everybody by accident.’”


Lawrence also says he will back Hakeem Jeffries for House speaker, but that he will demand Democratic leadership listen to progressive concerns.

author: Daron Letts
title: Iqaluit Northern store’s security guards get tactical makeover
content:
Iqaluit’s Northern store unveiled a

new look

 in October, following three years of in-store renovations. Its security guards also got a makeover.


Some of their new all-black tactical uniforms come with accessories, including body-worn cameras and what appear to be retractable batons.


“Two guards per shift have cameras and they are only turned on during an event,” Brigitte Burgoyne, spokesperson for the North West Co., the Winnipeg-based parent corporation of Northern, said in an email.


“The North West Company does not collect body camera footage.”


Canadian Arctic Protective Services does, the company’s regional manager said.


That’s who North West Co. contracts for its security.


With a head office in Iqaluit, Canadian Arctic Protective Services provides security services across Nunavut, and in Ottawa and Yellowknife, “and soon in Miami, Florida,” its website says.


“Footage access is limited to select management personnel and is used to review incidents and, where required, for law enforcement or legal proceedings,” said Paul Hunter, the security company’s regional director, in an email. 


“The cameras are turned on during an event and do not record continuously. They are not used for general customer surveillance.”


Hunter declined to say if the tool on the guard’s belt is a baton.


“We do not publicly share our internal security procedures or comment on site-specific security arrangements,” Hunter said.


Loblaws Inc., Canada’s largest food retailer, launched a pilot project using body cameras across B.C., Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, and Ontario in early 2025.

Shoppers Drug Mart followed.


“I take this as a completely misguided approach to the issue of food insecurity,” said sociologist Alissa Overend, interim director of the Research Institute of Urban Wellness at

Edmonton’s MacEwan University, in a phone interview.


“Even in cities, I don’t think policing is the right approach, but especially in northern and remote communities,” Overend said. “There have been criticisms of racial profiling.”


Shopper Marion Kusugak learned about some of the store’s on-site security arrangements first-hand on Thursday evening when a guard grabbed her backpack from her and then searched it, as she’d just begun shopping.

(The guard who interacted with Kusugak is not the guard in the main photo of this story.)


Nunatsiaq watched as a

guard dumped all her possessions on the checkout counter. 


“Be careful, please,” Kusugak said.


Some of her belongings fell to the floor as he rooted through them.


Northern store shopper Marion Kusugak shows the red ticket a cashier gave her after her backpack was taken and searched by a security guard on Thursday evening. She was not wearing sunglasses and a hood when the guard stopped her. She wore them only for the photo. (Photo by Daron Letts)


When the search was over, the guard stuffed her things back in her backpack. Then the cashier took the bag and put it out of sight behind the counter and handed Kusugak a red ticket.


“It’s a new policy,” the cashier told her.


After a pause, Kusugak asked the guard his first name, then put her hand out to shake his. He didn’t shake her hand.


Asked how she felt about the search as she pushed her cart down the frozen food aisle, she said, “I didn’t like it.”


“This was a town first and then it became a city,” she said.


Burgoyne at North West Co., and Hunter at Canadian Arctic Protective Services declined requests to answer questions about whether the way the guard searched Kusugak’s backpack was standard practice or whether it was appropriate.


Down the street at Arctic Ventures, elder Seemeega Kootoo staffs the entrance six days a week. He is one of three local security guards at the store.


Iqaluit elder Seemeega Kootoo staffs the door at Arctic Ventures in Iqaluit on Wednesday evening. He is one of three local security guards at the store. (Photo by Daron Letts)


“When people who are barred from here come, I don’t let them in,” he said during an interview on Wednesday. “That’s what I do.”

When he is not busy, he returns shopping carts to their stall, he added.


Arctic Co-op stores use fixed in-store surveillance systems to address theft concerns “in the least invasive manner,” said company vice-president Duane Wilson. The company has also not adopted body-worn cameras for security staff because they require detailed policies around when to record, as well as accessing, storing and retaining footage.
