title: Rize ve Artvin'de kar nedeniyle 22 köy yolu ulaşıma kapandı
content:
Karadeniz’de etkili olan kar yağışı günlük yaşamı etkilemeye devam ediyor. Rize ve Artvin’de yoğun kar yağışı nedeniyle Rize ve Artvin'de 22 köy yolu ulaşıma kapandı.

Rize'de dünden itibaren aralıklarla etkisini sürdüren yağış dolayısıyla merkezde 1, Ardeşen, Çamlıhemşin, Çayeli ve İkizdere ilçelerinde ise 3'er köy yolu ulaşıma kapandı.

İl Özel İdaresi ekipleri, kapalı yolları ulaşıma açmak için iş makineleriyle çalışmalarını sürdürüyor.

Karayolları ekipleri de Ovit Dağı'nın Sivrikaya mevkisindeki tünel bölgesinde ve Ayder Yaylası'nda yolları açık tutmak ve buzlanmayı önlemek için çalışma gerçekleştiriyor.

Artvin'in yüksek kesimlerinde de kar etkili oldu.

Yağış dolayısıyla Borçka ilçesinde 6, Şavşat'ta da 3 köye ulaşım sağlanamıyor.

İl Özel İdaresi ekiplerince kapalı yolların ulaşıma açılması için karla mücadele çalışması yürütülüyor.

Artvin-Ardahan kara yolu güzergahındaki Sahara geçidinde ise kar ve buzlanma nedeniyle zaman zaman trafikte aksama yaşanıyor.

Kentin en önemli turizm merkezlerinden Atabarı Kayak Merkezinde ise kar kalınlığı 50 santimetreyi aştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Kaliforniya'da milyarder vergisi önerisi reddedildi
content:
Fotoğraf: Yuri Keegstra from Milwaukee, USA/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 2.0

ABD'nin Kaliforniya eyaletinde, net serveti 1 milyar doların üzerinde olan kişilerin varlıklarına yüzde 5 oranında tek seferlik vergi uygulanmasını öngören yasal düzenleme geri çevrildi.

The New York Times'ın (NYT) haberine göre, 3 Kasım'da düzenlenen ara seçimlerde eyalette oyların yaklaşık yüzde 83'ü sayılırken, "Proposition 40" adı verilen düzenlemeye verilen destek yüzde 47'de kaldı. Teklif kapsamında, milyarderlerin kişisel varlıklarından bir defaya mahsus yüzde 5 vergi alınması ve elde edilecek gelirin büyük bölümünün sağlık hizmetlerine aktarılması öngörülüyordu.

Demokrat seçmenlerin ağırlıkta olduğu Kaliforniya'da varlıklı kesimden daha yüksek vergi alınması fikri genel olarak destek görse de, teklif Demokratlar ile işçi sendikaları arasındaki görüş ayrılıkları nedeniyle onay alamadı. Uzmanlar, teklifin reddedilmesinde milyarderlerin finanse ettiği devasa karşı kampanyanın etkili olduğunu değerlendiriyor.

Kampanya finansmanı kayıtlarına göre, Google'ın kurucu ortağı Sergey Brin'in vergi teklifinin reddedilmesi için 100 milyon dolardan fazla bağış yaptığı belirtildi. Brin'in öncülük ettiği grubun bu yıl 300 milyon dolardan fazla kaynak topladığı aktarıldı.

Demokratların güçlü olduğu bir eyalette milyarder vergisi teklifinin reddedilmesinin, ABD'de benzer servet vergilerine yönelik kamuoyu desteği tartışmalarını uzun süre gündemde tutması bekleniyor. Öte yandan, servet vergisi önerisinin 2028 başkanlık seçimleri kampanyasında da yoğun bir şekilde tartışılması öngörülüyor.

Kaliforniya Valisi Gavin Newsom daha önce yaptığı açıklamalarda, ülke genelinde uygulanacak bir servet vergisine sıcak baktığını ancak yalnızca tek bir eyalette geçerli olacak bir düzenlemeyi desteklemediğini ifade etmişti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Agência Mural
title: Construção: filhos de pedreiros que migraram para São Paulo buscam novas profissões
content:
Antônio Pedro de Lima, 54, e Naldo José Leite Lima, 50, têm algumas coisas em comum. Moradores de

Paraisópolis

, na zona sul de São Paulo, os dois chegaram à capital vindos do Nordeste em busca de trabalho e de uma vida melhor.


Começaram na construção civil como ajudantes de pedreiro, não concluíram o ensino fundamental e passaram boa parte da vida em uma profissão marcada pelo esforço físico. Ambos também são pais: Naldo tem três filhos e Antônio, quatro. Nenhum dos filhos, porém, quis seguir o mesmo caminho profissional.


A diferença está nas oportunidades. Quando chegaram a São Paulo, Antônio e Naldo encontraram na construção civil uma das poucas possibilidades de trabalho. Os filhos cresceram com acesso à educação, cursos e projetos sociais que ampliaram as opções de profissão.


Breno ao lado do pai, Antônio, que trabalhou na construção civil para sustentar a família


O tema virou polêmica este ano, quando um empresário da construção civil reclamou da

falta de mão de obra

.


Antônio veio de Murici, em Alagoas, em 1994, aos 22 anos. Chegou à cidade com uma promessa de trabalho que o irmão havia conseguido para ele. Na República, região central, começou fazendo manutenção em um hotel, lixando paredes e pintando. Depois, foi trabalhar em

Itaquera

 como ajudante de pedreiro. Foi ali que aprendeu o ofício que marcaria sua trajetória.


Com seis meses eu já sabia de muita coisa. Foi quando comecei a pegar esses conhecimentos e a levantar minha casa em Paraisópolis”


Antônio


pedreiro


Foi com o trabalho de pedreiro que Antônio sustentou os quatro filhos, entre eles Breno Tenório, 26, publicitário. Ainda criança, Breno percebia os efeitos da rotina do pai.


“Quando a gente é criança, não consegue traduzir muito essas coisas. Mas sempre senti a ausência dele em casa. Via meu pai chegando cansado e via meu pai saindo de madrugada, ainda escuro. Eu pensava: ‘Imagina como é difícil sair de casa às quatro ou cinco da manhã’”, lembra o publicitário.


A mesma realidade atravessou a trajetória de Naldo. Paraibano, ele chegou a São Paulo em 1995, aos 19 anos, para trabalhar na construção civil, em um emprego conseguido por primos. Iniciou a jornada como ajudante e aprendeu o ofício na prática. Foram mais de dez anos dedicados às obras, período em que também aprendeu pintura, encanamento e elétrica.


Gustavo Lira e o pai, Naldo, que trabalhou como pedreiro e atualmente é eletricista


“Quando comecei, não entendia de nada, mas fui aprendendo como ajudante. Era muito puxado. Porque a maioria das pessoas que vieram do Nordeste na minha época não tinha serviço além de coisas pesadas. Lá também é pesado o serviço, só que era diferente. Era agricultura, na roça”, relembra.


Durante os anos de obra, tijolos, concreto, pedras e sacos de materiais fizeram parte da rotina.


Carreguei muito tijolo, concreto, encher laje na mão. Você carrega pedra, carrega cimento, saco de 50 quilos praticamente. Não é fácil, exige muito do corpo da gente”


Naldo


eletricista


O filho, Gustavo Lira, 26, diretor de fotografia, cresceu vendo os efeitos dessa rotina.


“Meu pai chegava cansado, só tinha tempo de tomar banho, jantar e dormir para acordar cedo de novo. Durante anos, sempre vivi essa cena”, compartilha o jovem.


Outros caminhos


Breno acompanhou o pai levantar cada cômodo da casa da família. Mesmo assim, nunca se interessou pelo ofício. Quando criança, chegou a ajudar algumas vezes a carregar tijolos, mas logo corria para longe do trabalho pesado.


“Sempre corri, nunca quis ficar carregando peso não”, recorda, aos risos, enquanto conversa com o pai.


Com o tempo, Breno passou a enxergar que a escolha profissional também estava ligada às oportunidades que cada geração teve. Para ele, trabalhos essenciais para o funcionamento das cidades continuam concentrados entre populações mais pobres e migrantes, enquanto outros grupos têm mais possibilidades de escolha.


Breno, publicitário, afirma que busca oferecer uma vida melhor ao pai


Ele encontrou outro caminho por meio da educação. Antes de chegar à faculdade de publicidade, participou de cursos gratuitos de teatro e informática e de diferentes projetos sociais, que considera fundamentais para ampliar suas oportunidades.


Hoje, formado e trabalhando na comunicação, olha para a trajetória do pai, que continua atuando de forma autônoma na construção civil. Antônio teve carteira assinada apenas uma vez, em 1999. Para Breno, o custo desse trabalho não pode ser medido apenas …

author: Stelinsky
title: Υπόθεση Marfin vol.3
content:
Η υπόθεση Marfin «έτρεξε» για πρώτη φορά με τις διώξεις που ασκήθηκαν το 2011, έναν χρόνο μετά τον εμπρησμό της τράπεζας Marfin στο κέντρο της Αθήνας, στην απεργία της 5ης Μάη 2010. Ο εμπρησμός οδήγησε στον θάνατο 3 από τους εργαζόμενους στην τράπεζα. Πέντε χρόνια μετά, ο σύντροφος Θ. Σίψας αθωώθηκε πανηγυρικά στο Μικτό Ορκωτό Δικαστήριο (ΜΟΔ). Λίγα χρόνια μετά, το 2021, ο φάκελος της υπόθεσης «άνοιξε» ξανά, με την αστυνομική έρευνα να μην αποδίδει καρπούς.

Στο σήμερα, η ανακίνηση της υπόθεσης Marfin για 3η φορά σηματοδοτεί το πέρασμα σε μια νέα εποχή όσον αφορά τον εγχώριο κοινωνικό-ταξικό ανταγωνισμό. Η υπόθεση ήρθε στο προσκήνιο με αφορμή την «υπόθεση της Θεσσαλονίκης»: Οι δύο υποθέσεις, με χρονική απόσταση 16 ετών, όλως τυχαίως «εξιχνιάστηκαν» την ίδια μέρα. Συγκεκριμένα στις 10 Ιουλίου εκτελείται τριπλό ένταλμα σύλληψης, και διατάσσονται κατ’ οίκον έρευνες σε 5 άτομα. Συλλαμβάνονται οι σύντροφοι Θύμιος και Κώστας, και η συντρόφισσα Ελένη, κάτοικος εξωτερικού, που μεταφέρεται στα αγγλικά κρατητήρια.

Τα στοιχεία για την υπόθεση είναι ανύπαρκτα: Από την έκθεση της Διεύθυνσης Εγκληματολογικών Ερευνών, όπου αναλύεται το οπτικοακουστικό υλικό, δεν προκύπτει ταυτοποίηση των συντροφιών ως άτομα παρόντα στο σημείο μπροστά από την τράπεζα. Μοναδικά στοιχεία η ομοιότητα κάποιων κινητών αντικειμένων, και ένα ανώνυμο e-mail, το οποίο συνέταξε η Διεύθυνση Αντιμετώπισης Οργανωμένου Εγκλήματος (ΔΑΟΕ) που πραγματοποίησε τις συλλήψεις. Η δουλειά της αστυνομίας είναι πολύ πρόχειρη: Στο mail αναφέρεται ως μέλος στο «παρεάκι» που εμπλέκεται στην υπόθεση, άτομο που ήταν στη φυλακή εκείνη την ημέρα· ακόμα, η εκπρόσωπος τύπου της ΕΛ.ΑΣ., Κωνσταντία Δημογλίδου, αναφέρει στον ΣΚΑΪ πως το επίμαχο mail είναι στα χέρια της αστυνομίας ενάμιση χρόνο, ενώ αυτό έχει ημερομηνία αποστολής 08/04/2026, δηλαδή 3 μήνες πριν τις συλλήψεις.

Οι απολογίες διεξάγονται ενώπιον της ανακρίτριας Σμαράγδας Τασούλη, και της εισαγγελέως Βαρβάρας Γνεσούλη. Τα συντρόφια αρνούνται τις κατηγορίες, υπερασπίζονται την πολιτική τους θέση, όπως και τη συμμετοχή τους στη διαδήλωση, και ζητούν να διερευνηθεί ποιος έστειλε το e-mail.

Και τα 3 συντρόφια προφυλακίζονται παρά την απουσία στοιχείων. Απορρίπτονται και οι προσφυγές τους ενάντια στην απόφαση προφυλάκισης, καθώς τα αρμόδια Συμβούλια πλημμελειοδικών επικυρώνουν τις απορριπτικές προτάσεις των αρμόδιων εισαγγελέων, του αντιεισαγγελέα πρωτοδικών Ν. Λυμπερόπουλου, και των εισαγγελέων πρωτοδικών Ε. Μαρουδά και ο. Ηλιοπούλου. Έχει ενδιαφέρον πως στα σκεπτικά των προφυλακίσεων, όπως και στις απορρίψεις των προσφυγών, υιοθετείται η συλλογιστική από το διαβιβαστικό της αστυνομίας, εμπλουτισμένη με αναφορές σε «ενδείξεις ενοχής» αλλά και σε «οργανωμένη, συλλογική και προπαρασκευασμένη δράση». Σύμφωνα με τους δικαστικούς, υπάρχει ο κίνδυνος τα συντρόφια μας να τελέσουν τα ίδια αδικήματα, μιας και «εδώ και 16 χρόνια κρύβουν επιμελώς τη δράση τους». Τι πιο λογικό άλλωστε;

Η ΔΑΟΕ, κατ’ εντολή του υπουργού ΠΡΟ.ΠΟ, Μιχάλη Χρυσοχοΐδη, έκανε τη δουλειά της. Στο μαγείρεμα παίρνει θέση και η δικαστική εξουσία, έτοιμη να το αναβαθμίσει με την –όχι και τόσο– μυστική συνταγή της. Η υπόθεση μένει στην εποπτεία της ανακρίτριας Τασούλη για τις τελικές πινελιές και το ντεκόρ.

Η Σμαράγδα Τασούλη παίζει καθοριστικό ρόλο στην υπόθεση, όπως θα δούμε παρακάτω. Η ίδια, έχοντας συμπληρώσει κάποια χρόνια προϋπηρεσίας, μέσα στο καλοκαίρι θα προαγόταν για λόγους αρχαιότητας σε πρόεδρος πρωτοδικών σε μια κενή οργανική θέση. Αρχικά η προαγωγή της εξαιρέθηκε από τον τακτικό πίνακα των προαχθέντων, όπως αυτός δημοσιεύεται επίσημα στο Φύλλο Εφημερίδας της Κυβερνήσεως (14/08/2026). Αλλά και σε δεύτερο χρόνο, παρ’ όλο που στο ΦΕΚ στις 17/09/2026 τής ανατίθεται μια θέση στο Ναύπλιο, εκείνη εξακολουθεί να μην αναλαμβάνει καθήκοντα εκεί ως πρόεδρος πρωτοδικών. Αντιθέτως, με ρητή ειδική διαταγή του Υπουργού Δικαιοσύνης παραμένει στη θέση της ανακρίτριας, έχοντας κατ’ αποκλειστικότητα την ανακριτική έρευνα για την υπόθεση Marfin, απαλλαγμένη από κάθε άλλη υπόθεση. Αυτή η τελευταία εξέλιξη επιβεβαιώνει πως η συγκεκριμένη ανακρίτρια έχει αναλάβει την ευθύνη να φέρει εις πέρας μια ειδική αποστολή, που της έχει ανατεθεί απευθείας από το Υπουργείο Δικαιοσύνης: Την ποινική αναβάθμιση της καταστολής των κοινωνικών αντιστάσεων.

Οι νέες συνταγές, λοιπόν, δεν αργούν. Το μαγειρείο καλά κρατεί: Στις αρχές του Οκτώβρη, η ανακρίτρια επιστρατεύει την 1η παράγραφο του νόμου 187Α, αυτήν περί ατομικής τρομοκρατίας.* Μέχρι πρότινος τα 3 συντρόφια κατηγορούνταν για …

author: Bruce De La Cruz
title: ‘Where is the accountability?’: Nunavut’s child advocate says territory’s protection issues aren’t being addressed
content:
Another scathing report from the federal auditor general looking into Nunavut’s child protection system came as no surprise to Jane Bates, the territory’s child welfare advocate.

On Nov. 3, deputy auditor general Andrew Hayes released the latest in a series of damning reports outlining how Nunavut is failing to protect Inuit children in care of the state.

For Bates, who has already written extensively about the issue, it came as no surprise.

“These concerns have been reported on, recommendations have been made about them, and yet they remain unaddressed to the detriment of children, youth, and families,” Bates told APTN News, “which is really the fundamental issue that everyone should be really concerned about, is the lack of follow through.

“We’re not talking about buildings. We’re not talking about bicycles. We’re talking about children and youth and their families. And so it’s deeply concerning.”

Hayes’ report outlined found that “fundamental weaknesses” in Nunavut’s child welfare system and its handling of the territory’s most vulnerable “remain unresolved” in audits going back to 2011.

“When children are removed from their homes and are placed in foster care for protection, the department takes on responsibility for their safety and well being,” Hayes said at a news conference on Nov. 3. “Yet it could not consistently demonstrate that basic safeguards, intended to protect children and place them in safe environments, were being followed.”

According to the latest report, approximately 400 children and youth are in Nunavut’s foster care system; the majority are Inuit.

Hayes said his office reviewed 40 cases and found issues that go back more than a decade.

The major concerns included that Nunavut’s Department of Family Services didn’t maintain required monthly in-person contact in more than 90 per cent of the cases; only performed 52 per cent of required evaluations for home safety” and, in 75 per cent of the cases, failed to give important information about a child to caregivers.

“Where is the accountability here? And again, we’re hearing, ‘oh, yes, we accept all the recommendations and we’re going to make changes.’ Where have you been? This has been upwards of 15 years. And we shouldn’t still be having this conversation.”

One Inuk family services employee who spoke to APTN News on condition that we grant anonymity, said the lack of Inuit staffing is the biggest concern.

“There’s like 30 per cent Inuit employed by this department,” the employee said. “I think if we had an Inuk supervisor, it would make a difference. Someone who knows the culture.”

Clayton Greaves, assistant deputy minister of Family Services Wellness Division, oversees the operations for the child welfare system in Nunavut.

“When I reviewed the report, and I hear what’s happening, we accept the other general recommendations and we accept that there’s work that’s in front of us that we have to do,” he said.

Greaves emphasized the challenges in running the child welfare system and said they’re doing the best with what they have.

“When we look at the report, we have to be careful that we don’t draw the conclusion that the gaps that we see is directly related to children being harmed,” he said. “And I wanted to make sure that we’re able to emphasize that. Yes, there are challenges with our new information system. We recognize and accept, you know, the recommendation, like I said, from what the Auditor General reported.”

Auditor general funds Nunavut foster care continues to fail vulnerable children

According to Bates’ own report that was filed in September, harm is coming to children.

“In the Reviews of Critical Injuries and Deaths program, reports of sexualized violence increased significantly, from eight in 2024–2025 to 22 in 2025–2026, while the number of young people who died by suicide tragically increased to 13,” she wrote in a report tabled in the Nunavut legislature.

“Children and youth who grow up in care, there’s been numerous studies done on the trajectory for young people,” she told APTN. “The outcomes are not good for children who grow up in care. They’re away from their families. They’re away from their culture. They lose their language.

“Children have the right to grow up with their families. They have a right to be protected. These are their fundamental rights under the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. And currently, in Nunavut, that is not happening.”

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Trump Calls Immigration Policy “Too Tough,” Then Promotes Stephen Miller
content:
The new chief of staff has shaped some of Trump’s most draconian immigration policies, including family separation.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

In a “60 Minutes” interview that aired on Sunday evening, President Donald Trump admitted that Republicans’ massive defeats in the midterm elections resulted from widespread frustration with the war on Iran, as well as his immigration policies.

Reiterating that he “was not on the ballot” — as if to suggest that support would have been higher for him personally — Trump said that Americans “didn’t like the war” and “the fact that gasoline went up,” claiming he “had it down at a low” prior to launching the war. In Trump’s assessment, public opposition to his war on Iran is reducible to gasoline prices.

Trump also stated that Republicans’ massive losses during the midterm elections were due to “a great dislike, incredibly, for Israel” — characterizing growing opposition to the U.S.’s relationship with the genocidal state as mere “dislike.”

Trump then said that his immigration policies may have also affected the midterms, and that he may have been “too tough.”

“I think I got an A+ for closing up the border,” he said. “I get very high marks for getting the bad ones out. But I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs, that created one violation, or breaking of the law, and that was that they came into the country illegally. And there’s a large group of people [that] think they should be allowed to stay.”

“So you think your deportation policy went too far?” asked CBS News’s Ross Douthat.

“I think it might be too tough,” Trump replied.

In the interview, Trump acknowledged a central contradiction in his administration: that he is caught between the priorities of his far right base, who “would like everybody taken out” [of the country], and the general population, which rejects his brutal policies.

Shortly after his “60 Minutes” interview on Friday, Trump announced that he was promoting political advisor Stephen Miller to White House chief of staff — suggesting that he does not, in fact, plan to soften his approach to immigration enforcement. Miller is known as the hardline, white nationalist architect of Trump’s mass deportation policies, including his policy of family separation.

Over the past year of his administration, Trump has been forced to temper the most overt aspects of his immigration crackdown, after Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) brutal “Operation Metro Surge” in the Twin Cities brought about widespread resistance, particularly after immigration agents killed Minneapolis residents Renee Good and Alex Pretti. As a result of widespread opposition, mass protests, and even a general strike in the Twin Cities, Trump replaced Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Kristi Noem with Markwayne Mullin, who promised that DHS operations would be less visible and stay out of the headlines.

While subsequent ICE operations have not been as brazen as that of Operation Metro Surge, the agency’s strategy has not fundamentally changed. In New York City in July and August, ICE’s “Operation Rotten Apple” resulted in the arrests of some 2,200 people — more than the amount detained by ICE during Operation Metro Surge earlier in the year. The New York City operation, however, managed to evade the same level of pushback, as ICE agents remained less visible, arriving in unmarked cars and detaining and disappearing people quickly, before resistance could emerge.

Trump also stated in the “60 Minutes” interview that he would work with Democrats on immigration. Indeed, his categorization of immigrants as either hard workers or “rough,” “drug dealers” and “killers” echoes rhetoric that has been key to both Republicans’ and Democrats’ approach to immigration since the 1980s — and to bipartisan “comprehensive immigration reform” policies that have increasingly ceded ground to the right.

While voters rejected Trump’s policies in the midterm elections, it is little surprise that Trump has offered to work with Democrats on immigration, as they do not represent an actual alternative to the criminalization, deportation, and precarity offered to undocumented immigrants and asylum seekers.

Meanwhile, the president’s promotion of Miller suggests that even as Trump’s own popularity falls, his aggressive deportation tactics are likely to continue.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Se presentó en la Facultad de Psicología la sección de salud mental del Informe CPM
content:
La Facultad de Psicología de la Universidad Nacional de La Plata fue sede de la presentación de la sección de Salud Mental del Informe Anual 2026, elaborado por la Comisión Provincial por la Memoria en su calidad de Mecanismo Local de Prevención de la Tortura. A la jornada, que contó con la participación de la decana María Cristina Piro y el titular de la catedra de Psicología Forense Xavier Oñativia, asistieron mas de 180 estudiantes, docentes, investigadores y profesionales de la psicología, además de público general. El Informe da cuenta del trabajo de monitoreo e intervención que el organismo desarrolla en la provincia de Buenos Aires, donde se relevaron graves situaciones en comunidades terapéuticas clandestinas, clínicas psiquiátricas privadas y cárceles neuropsiquiátricas, así como también la letalidad que provoca la intervención policial en la vía pública ante casos de crisis subjetivas. Como positivo se destacó la profundización del proceso de desmanicomialización en neuropsiquiátricos públicos aunque persisten prácticas manicomiales en detrimento de los estándares de la ley nacional de salud mental.


“Celebro este espacio de encuentro entre academia y organismos de derechos humanos, porque estoy convencida que nuestra academia debe nutrirse de las alertas que el trabajo de la Comisión genera para transformar las políticas públicas en salud mental”, señaló en la bienvenida la decana de la Facultad de Psicología, María Cristina Piro. Y agregó: “Debemos entender que el sufrimiento no puede resultarnos indiferente a los profesionales de la salud mental y tenemos la obligación de fortalecer y construir un modelo de salud mental con dignidad para las personas”.


Este miércoles 4 se llevó a cabo, en la sede de esa unidad académica, la presentación pública de la sección Salud mental, correspondiente al Informe Anual 2026 de la CPM que sistematiza el trabajo del organismo -en su carácter de Mecanismo Local de Prevención de la Tortura- sobre lugares de encierro, políticas de seguridad, salud mental y niñez en la provincia de Buenos Aires.


Además de la CPM, junto a la Decana, integraron el panel el prosecretario de Salud Mental de la UNLP y titular de la cátedra de Psicología Forense, Xavier Oñativia y la auxiliar letrada del Juzgado de Familia 8 de Avellaneda, Belén Muñoz. ”Cuando analizamos cómo funcionan muchos de los dispositivos de salud mental nos encontramos con profesionales que no cumplen o no hacen cumplir los compromisos éticos con los que la academia los ha formado. Por eso creemos importante que ustedes, que serán los profesionales del mañana, incorporen y se comprometan con la perspectiva de derechos humanos”, afirmó el secretario de la CPM, Roberto Cipriano, ante un auditorio de la Facultad de Psicología de la UNLP con gran presencia de estudiantes y profesionales de la salud mental.


La directora del programa de Salud Mental, Melina Galeano, destacó que las prácticas manicomiales son reiteradas y sistemáticas, tienen un impacto subjetivo y generan sufrimiento por eso se constituyen como torturas y tratos crueles. También destacó la importancia de la interdisciplina para intervenciones integrales, situadas y contextuadas: “Cada entrevista con una persona con un padecimiento de salud mental se realiza generando las condiciones de privacidad e intimidad necesarias y basada en que su palabra no puede ser desestimada por su diagnóstico”.


“Vemos que una de las principales crisis del sistema de salud mental está relacionado con el abordaje sobre los jóvenes con consumos problemáticos: no existe un registro oficial de las comunidades terapéuticas que funcionan en la provincia sin habilitación del Ministerio de Salud; mucho menos se conoce cuántas personas permanecen alojadas en esos lugares ni cuántas muertes y por qué motivos se producen en esos escenarios. De hecho, en esos lugares hemos relevado una de las prácticas más gravosas: el secuestro de los usuarios”, amplió.


Luego Rodrigo Pomares, coordinador del área de Seguridad y Justicia de la CPM, se refirió a la continuidad de la violencia estatal en casos de crisis subjetivas en la vía pública: en 16 de 18 casos de personas fallecidas por  la intervención policial violenta relevados en el 2025, se redujo a la persona al piso con uso de violencia, intervinieron tres o más efectivos para reducir a una sola persona, les colocaron esposas a la víctima y en algunas situaciones utilizaron para esos fines la propia ropa de la persona.


En ese sentido …

author: David Swanson
title: Talk World Radio: How the Unprovoked War Was Provoked
content:
Russian aggression and any militarism should not be justified by any provocations. Russian leader, suppressing voices of dissent and antimilitarism, in a long multi-track conflict where tragic mistakes were made on all sides (background ignored in this conversation) decided to escalate by brutally invading Ukraine, killing thousands of innocent civilians, ruining and blackouting cities, not resorting to international courts or other mechanisms of pacific conflict resolution according to UN Charter, not building nonviolent action and nonmilitary peace protection institutions.

It is pity that alternative journalism, similarly to mainstream journalism, seek whom to blame instead of seeking peaceful solutions towards justice and reconciliation. Truth must be told, but in narrative of reconciliation: there were nasty CIA operations in response to nasty operations of Russian military intelligence, methods of both sides are wrong, it is wrong that some actors of Ukrainian independence movement partnered (rather than become stooges of) U.S. military intelligence, Nazi links of some Ukrainian, Russian and U.S. actors are outrageous, but there was also always the will of Ukrainian people and genuine grievances that matter much more than any covert operations attempting to ride the wave. As Kinzer recognizes, Ukrainians and the United States had many reasons to feel unsafe provoked by Russia, Soviet Union, Russian Empire. Responding in kind, they sustained the vicious circle of violence. But there is no truth about escalation ladder, mutual harm and mutual provocations, there is only blame of one side and no vision of reconciliation of rival stories and modus vivendi. In my view, it is not how you tell truth to achieve genuine peace.

Truth is that we need no corporations and tools of death and pain in Russia, in Ukraine, in United States, all peoples have a right to peace on common planet. People need to support each other seeking universal peace by nonmilitary means.

We need nonviolent interventionism of peace crowds everywhere in the world, protesting against war at Red Square and calling to protest against military dictatorship everywhere else, not stay aside when brutal dictator subjugates neighboring people and his own people out of imperialist ambitions. Violent mass arrests of youth in Moscow imposing military mobilization are disgusting, similarly to Ukrainian busification.

All civilians of the planet shall stay for peace together to get rid of all armies of NATO and CSTO, Russia and Ukraine, Israel and Palestine, United States and China. We need nonviolent governance of the world, representing all peaceful peoples, able to decide to disband all armies and make it happen by nonviolent action. Not recognizing this and continuing to debate who is guilty, who provoked whom where everyone provoke everyone, mean we allow great powers to generate endless wars by their rivalries and provocations. Ukrainian Helsinki Group, created to advocate human rights after the Helsinki Accords, sought democratic transformations, peaceful coexistence of independent democratic Ukraine and Russia, and nuclear disarmament. Members of the group were repressed, but they managed to send from Gulag an open letter to world leaders in 1980 saying: “The war of ideologies gives rise to a senseless arms race, so the disarmament of hearts and souls is necessary.” Let’s remember this call and disarm the world together.

title: La Justicia de Milei: Urgencias políticas detrás de los fiscales crédulos que defienden a quienes deberían acusar

Adorni encontró un defensor en Pollicita, como los Milei en Taiano. La ausencia de un vocero, la recesión y el “todos contra todos” en Casa Rosada. Rodrigo Sbarra, el antecedente gemelo de otro funcionario que se enriqueció sin darse cuenta y fue comprendido por el mismo fiscal.


Javier Milei, Manuel Adorni, Eduardo Taiano y Gerardo Pollicita


Por Sebastián Lacunza


El reacomodamiento de las piezas en el edificio de Comodoro Py ejecutado este año por los Hermanos Milei aporta una novedad sustancial: fiscales federales argumentan como si fueran abogados defensores de las personas a las que deben investigar.


No importa que los planteos esgrimidos por los acusados sean un insulto a la inteligencia de tan absurdos. Los fiscales aceptan el argumentario con candidez ilimitada y procuran cerrar la causa. Una condición: los imputados deben orbitar en los planetas del mileísmo y el macrismo.


La diferencia que se huele en estos meses con respecto a los largos años de impunidad de los que goza el entorno político y económico de Mauricio Macri radica en la celeridad del proceso y la nitidez de un fiscal y/o un juez dispuestos a inmolarse con su firma.


En los tiempos de dominio plenipotenciario de la trama compuesta por el PRO, el Grupo Clarín y la SIDE, los tribunales penales federales de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires alternaron la técnica estelar del adormecimiento con un ida y vuelta más movidito entre juzgados e instancias superiores, cambios de radicación del expediente y otros ardides procesales.


De esa manera, transcurrieron años hasta gestar un sobreseimiento a hurtadillas cerca de Año Nuevo, un Mundial, o en un cambio de Gobierno, o simplemente se optó por dejar que el expediente languideciera en un cajón, sin morir del todo. Ejemplos emblemáticos de esto último son las causas del soterramiento del ferrocarril Sarmiento, que tiene a Ángelo Calcaterra como uno de los grandes beneficiados por decisiones tomadas por su primo y Cristina en Casa Rosada, o el presunto fraude cometido por Sociedades Macri (Socma) en la gestión privada del Correo Argentino. Ambos expedientes llevan una eternidad en el edificio de Comodoro Py, lo que motivó alguna precipitación ansiosa de Macri que le terminó jugando en contra para dar vuelta la página definitivamente.


El mecano de Juan Bautista


El dato clave de 2026 es la coronación de Juan Bautista Mahiques y Santiago Viola como números 1 y 2 del Ministerio de Justicia. Pocos despachos de Comodoro Py se resisten al llamado del primero, un artífice de la Mesa Judicial del macrismo y representante de una familia multiempleada en el fuero federal. Su amigo Viola, en tanto, sobrelleva un currículum de operaciones de Inteligencia, otro factor de empoderamiento en el edificio de Retiro. Ese dúo heredado del corazón del macrismo y entronizado por Karina Milei fue el motor de la reciente aprobación en el Senado del pliego de 180 jueces y fiscales,

y va por más

El mecano armado por Mahiques y Viola eliminó riesgos y acortó plazos. author: Joe Mullin
title: Why Fewer People Are Challenging Bad Patents
content:
The number of petitions being filed at the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) has collapsed. That’s not reason for celebration. The PTAB is an important line of defense against low-quality software patents being used in lawsuits against people and companies.

The drop didn’t happen because suddenly patents have become higher quality. It’s simply because USPTO leadership is increasingly refusing to consider good challenges to patents, for reasons unrelated to the merits. The process has become so unreliable that many would-be patent challengers aren’t even trying.

Inter partes review (IPR) is a process that allows people to challenge patents at the Patent Office, rather than having to fight an expensive lawsuit in federal court. It’s one of the most important ways to get bad patents out of the system.

In the third quarter of 2026, July through September, only 97 IPR petitions were filed at the PTAB, compared to 327 petitions during the same period in 2025. Similarly, only 37 IPR petitions were filed in September 2026, compared to 129 petitions in December 2024—the last full month before the current USPTO leadership began reshaping how the Board handles patent challenges.

This dramatic decline shouldn’t just concern patent lawyers. EFF has fought bad patents because so many software and internet patents make claims to the basic tools of free expression online, like sending email, using online ads, or publishing web pages. When bad patents go unchallenged, they affect everyone who cares about the freedom to write new code and make new technology.

That’s why EFF has defended IPR since it came on the scene more than a decade ago. It provides a faster and less expensive way to challenge patents that should never have been granted. Congress created IPRs because the Patent Office makes mistakes. District court litigation is an extraordinarily expensive way to correct them. Without a meaningful administrative review process, bad patents remain powerful weapons in the hands of patent trolls and others seeking to extract settlements from companies that often did nothing wrong.

Now, USPTO leadership is dismantling that safeguard.

Since Congress created the IPR patent challenge process in 2012, the PTAB has always had some discretion in deciding which petitions deserve review. But institution rates today are much lower than their typical historical range.

Between fiscal years 2022 and 2024, the PTAB instituted between 66% and 68% of IPR petitions. In fiscal year 2026, which concluded in September 2026, the institution rate fell to 41%. And institution is only the first step of an IPR—it means the PTAB has agreed to hear the challenge, not that the challenger won, and the patent will be invalidated.

That decline helps explain why fewer petitions are being filed in the first place. Preparing an IPR petition takes substantial time and money. While cheaper than federal court, it’s still a complicated administrative process. Before filing, a challenger typically needs to search for prior art, hire experts, and develop detailed technical and legal arguments about why the patent never should have been granted.

Companies were willing to pay for IPRs because, historically, they could expect a predictable process. Petitions that met the statutory standard generally had a reasonable prospect of being heard and decided on the merits. But the USPTO has made it harder to get petitions heard and is throwing them out for reasons that have nothing to do with the merits of the challenges. Faced with these odds, many potential challengers aren’t filing at all.

When the PTAB decides to hear an IPR case, that means the petition has been “instituted”—but that has never meant that the petitioner will definitely win. It means the PTAB has determined the challenge warrants a full merits review, and the parties could expect the proceeding to continue toward a final written decision. But under the current USPTO leadership, that expectation has disappeared. The PTAB’s institution decisions are being repeatedly vacated by the Director.

USPTO Director John Squires has vacated at least 29 decisions granting institution of IPR proceedings, and subsequently denied the petitions, terminating those proceedings before a final written decision. These include cases that PTAB judges had already agreed to hear, as well as proceedings that Squires himself had previously allowed to proceed. This level of retroactive intervention is unprecedented.

In some …

author: Administrador
title: A QUÉ VAMOS. QUÉ SÍ Y QUÉ NO
content:
Atención Familias Buscadoras, sin o con colectivo: Atención quienes acompañan a familias buscadoras:

Éste es el primero de varios textos donde iremos aclarando algunas dudas que hemos recibido, responder a algunas ofensas e insultos, e irles dando a conocer poco a poco parte de la agenda de la delegación. Por favor les pedimos estar pendientes de éste y los siguientes escritos.

A.- Hemos detectado una serie de confusiones, malhabladas e intentos de manipulación sobre los objetivos, fechas, lugares y actividades de la delegación de la Comisión Sexta Zapatista para estos meses de diciembre, y la primera semana de enero del 2027.

Se habla y se malinforma de una supuesta reunión nacional entre familias buscadoras y la delegación zapatista en la llamada “Glorieta de los Desaparecidos” el 6 de diciembre, y de otras actividades públicas de la Comisión Sexta Zapatista en otros lugares y fechas.

Esto es falso, compañeras y hermanas buscadoras. Tal vez sí tengan una su reunión quienes se convocan en ése o en otros sitios como referentes a su justa lucha, pero nosotros no participaremos ahí.

No sólo porque la “invitación” que recibimos de ahí refleja ignorancia, mala fe y grosería. A nadie se le invita insultándolo. En su oportunidad explicaremos más sobre eso. También porque no vamos a reuniones masivas con familias buscadoras.

Los grupos, colectivos, colectivas y familias buscadoras que se reúnen en las glorietas o donde sea, pueden reunirse EN PRIVADO con nosotros, grupo por grupo, en la sede de la delegación en la Ciudad de México y en las sedes que se harán públicas, registrándose vía el Frayba, en la fecha y hora que les convenga, si así lo desean.

B.- Miren, ustedes y nosotros, los pueblos zapatistas, sabemos que tienen no sólo diferencias sino francas rivalidades y disputas, mismo entre colectivos de buscadoras, entre redes y movimientos. Incluso hasta llegar a tratar de vetar a ciertos colectivos y a decretar quién sí y quién no se reúne con la delegación zapatista. Tal vez por eso crece el número de familias buscadoras que no están en ningún grupo o colectivo, y que nos contactan directamente.

Nosotros no vamos a juzgar a nadie. No vamos a decir cuál estrategia es correcta o errónea, cuál es legítima y cuál no, cuál es buena y cuál es mala.

Consideramos que, quien busca verdad y justicia y tiene el objetivo de encontrar a quien le hace falta a causa de una desaparición forzada, puede y debe recorrer todos los caminos y tocar todas las puertas para aliviar su dolor.

Sea que hacen búsqueda de campo con pico y pala; sea que recurren a las instancias judiciales locales, estatales y federales; sea que quieren reunirse con la titular del ejecutivo federal o con su pirámide de funcionarios; sea que hacen campañas internacionales y nacionales; sea que sólo alcanzan a pegar las fotos de sus ausentes en sus calles y barrios, sea que recurren a Organizaciones No Gubernamentales de Derechos Humanos; sea que solicitan el apoyo de especialistas en búsqueda de desaparecidos y análisis de restos humanos; sea que recurren a marchas, mítines, plantones, tomas de edificios y bloqueos de calles y carreteras; sea rezar; sea maldecir; sea todo lo anterior.

Y siempre con la memoria como motor.

Sea lo que sea que decidan y hagan, es una decisión de ustedes, de quienes cargan ese dolor y sufren esa angustia, y de nadie más.

Entonces no vamos a decirles qué hacer ni a hacerlo por ustedes. Vamos a conocerlas, a escucharlas, a abrazarlas.

Ni vamos a decir cuál red o colectivo es mejor que el otro.

C.- Por eso nuestro viaje no privilegia actos de masas, ni mediáticos, ni asambleas generales ni creación de alianzas, frentes o cosas parecidas, ni una nueva organización que englobe o incluya a todos los colectivos y familias buscadoras, o a parte de ellas.

Tampoco vamos a discutir o a debatir el número de personas desaparecidas, si son 135 mil o son más o son menos, porque esos números tienen un nombre, una historia, una tragedia, un dolor, y un deber: el de buscar a quien se ama, a quien hace falta y, no pocas veces, a quien es sangre de su sangre.

D.- La principal intención de esta iniciativa es escuchar a cada familia o grupo de familias buscadoras que quiera contarnos su historia y, sobre todo, la historia de su ausente.

Porque nosotros hemos visto y escuchado su caminar, sus esfuerzos, sus sacrificios, si no rendirse en la búsqueda, su no vender a su ser ausente, su no claudicar en la memoria.

author: Brett Wilkins
title: Past 4 Years Have Been Hottest on Record, UN Meteorological Organization Finds
content:
The alarming climate report was released on the opening day of the COP31 climate conference.

The alarming climate report was released on the opening day of the COP31 climate conference.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

The Earth is hurtling deeper into a climate emergency, with 2026 on track to be one of the four hottest years ever recorded, ocean temperatures and sea levels hitting record highs, and glacier melt accelerating at an alarming pace, according to a report released Monday by the World Meteorological Organization as the United Nations Climate Change Conference kicked off in Türkiye.

The WMO’s “State of the Climate” report “shows that the past 12 years have individually been the warmest on record, with the past four years being the top four,” according to a summary of the 25-page publication.

WMO further noted that “the global average surface temperature for January – September 2026 was about 1.47°C above the preindustrial average,” or right on the brink of the 1.5°C of warming beyond which scientists say the risks of catastrophic and potentially irreversible climate impacts increase substantially.

2026 is on track to be one of 4 warmest years on record, marked by exceptional global temperatures, melting ice, rising sea levels, and a very strong El Niño that will unleash more heat & extreme weather into 2027.New WMO #StateOfClimate #COP31 Update↪️ https://bit.ly/stateofclimateCOP31pr

UN scientists said last month that the Paris Agreement’s goal of limiting warming to 1.5°C this century is no longer achievable without an overshoot.

The 1.47°C figure “is likely to rise through the end of the year because of the warming effect of El Niño, which has been intensifying since August and is expected to be the strongest on record by December,” the report’s summary states. El Niño is the warm phase of a pattern in the Pacific Ocean whose impact on disrupts weather, ecosystems, and economies.

Earth’s energy imbalance is rising… The imbalance reached its highest level since monitoring began, as greenhouse gases trap unprecedented amounts of heat and upset the equilibrium between incoming energy from the sun and outgoing energy. The ocean absorbs 90% of this excess heat, and 2026 is on track to be the 10th successive year of record ocean warmth.

Sea level is the highest on record, and sea-surface temperatures hit monthly records during 2026. The long-term retreat of glaciers continuesv— the annual mass loss of ice in 2025 would have filled five Olympic pools every second of the year. Freshwater storage has been dwindling since 2014.

“Extreme weather has made headlines throughout 2026. Behind the headlines and the statistics in this report are people who suffered the loss of loved ones, threats to their health and safety, flooded homes, failed harvests, empty shelves, lack of water, and choking air,” WMO Secretary General Celeste Saulo said in the report.

“The past four years have been the warmest in the 177-year observational record, and the heat in the oceans is breaking records for the 10th year in a row,” she continued. “The ongoing El Niño is forecast to be one of the strongest on record, and the heat it releases from the ocean will continue to fuel high temperatures and extreme weather into 2027.”

“El Niño and indeed the state of the global climate in 2026 gives new meaning to the phrase off the charts,” Saulo added. “El Niño doesn’t add new heat to the planet. It releases heat from the ocean, which is the warmest ever measured. There is simply more heat available to release.”

Indeed, climate scientists are warning that the planet is closer than previously thought to tipping points leading to hellish feedback loops and a “hothouse Earth.”

United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres responded to the WMO report in a statement, saying: “We have entered a new age of climate extremes. A supersized El Niño is colliding with a planet already superheated by manmade climate change. Climate records keep falling. The human costs keep rising. And those least responsible are suffering first and worst.”

“Leaders must get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels, and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need,” he added.

The “State of the Climate” report was released on the first day of the UN summit, or COP31, in Antalya …

author: Ciudong Ng
title: Aggression Against Iran Has Been Bipartisan. Will Midterm Results Change That?
content:
The US and Israel repeatedly subverted Iranian sovereignty, threatened nuclear war, and destabilized the Middle East.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

The Republican Party’s staggering losses in the November midterm elections have prompted speculation about the future of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, which is overwhelmingly unpopular with voters. Democratic leaders have portrayed President Donald Trump’s military offensive as an unconstitutional fiasco and an economic disaster driving inflation.

But their choreographed outrage conceals a long tradition of bipartisan support for aggression, which President Masoud Pezeshkian of Iran denounced in his UN address this September. For decades, the United States and Israel have referred to Iranians as terrorists, “but we are the victims of terrorists,” Pezeshkian underscored. His speech outlined a record of hypocrisy: U.S. and Israeli officials talk about peace, but plot to assassinate political leaders and negotiators. Most notably, both states command nuclear arsenals, yet impose debilitating sanctions on Iran’s atomic energy program.

As Pezeshkian emphasizes, the war is the latest episode in a turbulent history of energy and imperial assertion that contradicts U.S.-Israeli claims about proliferation risks and regional security. During the Cold War, Western powers shattered Iran’s democracy, before consolidating a brutal petromonarchy to guarantee access to its oil reserves. While undercutting Iranian energy sovereignty, they allowed Israel to become a nuclear-armed occupier, spreading dirty weapons and armed conflicts across the Middle East. This tangled history of oil and atoms is essential to understanding the war’s causes and contradictions, as two rogue states with thermonuclear weapons attack Iran under the pretext of nonproliferation.

Since the nineteenth century, Western powers have attempted to curb Iran’s sovereignty or seize its vast energy reserves. By 1914, Great Britain controlled its oil industry, after extorting concessions from the Iranian government. Over the following decades, the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company (AIOC) turned its refinery in the southwestern city of Abadan into the main energy supplier for the British Empire. Winston Churchill called the gushing wells “a prize from fairyland.” Yet AIOC officials warped Iran’s economic development by handpicking politicians and shamelessly exploiting workers. British personnel at Abadan lived in segregated splendor with swimming pools and servants, while local laborers inhabited parched slums.

After World War II, Iran attempted to improve its contract with the AIOC in order to raise government revenue and living standards. But company officials refused to compromise. In April 1951, Mohammad Mosaddegh became prime minister and initiated a series of ambitious reforms, which included nationalizing the oil industry.

Privately, the U.S. government lambasted the AIOC for behaving like a “typical nineteenth-century colonial exploiter,” while dealing “ineptly and disastrously” with Iran. Secretary of State Dean Acheson was scathing: “Never had so few lost so much so stupidly and so fast.” Nevertheless, U.S. leaders colluded with Britain to undermine nationalization. They feared that Mosaddegh’s policy set a destabilizing precedent, sapping British imperial power, upending the Cold War balance, and compromising Western control over strategic resources.

“I fought the fascists and Nazis,” one CIA adviser ruminated. “My lesson was that we were becoming just like them.”

Posing as a mediator, the State Department pressed Iranian leaders to make concessions, yet privately conceded that Britain’s demands were unreasonable. British negotiators advocated paying “lip service” to the principle of nationalization, while “keeping effective power … in our hands.” Ratcheting up pressure, the United States and Britain organized an oil embargo to suffocate Iran’s economy. Officials also bribed dozens of legislators, who physically assaulted Mosaddegh’s allies in parliament. And they launched a global propaganda campaign, pumping what one British operative called “a steady supply of suitable poison” into the press.

author: CNT Galiza
title: La CNT inicia un conflicto contra la academia de inglés This Way
content:
Leer en

Castellano

Galego


Castellano

La CNT inicia un conflicto contra la academia de inglés This Way en Vigo: ¡Ese no es el camino!


Las academias y centros de formación de inglés siguen agravando la precariedad del sector, aprovechándose fraudulentamente del modelo de contrato indefinido. El caso más reciente se sitúa en Vigo, donde la CNT acaba de iniciar un conflicto sindical contra la empresa This Way.


La táctica de esta empresa es tan antigua como perversa: en lugar de respetar la ley y conceder a nuestra afiliada la baja temporal de verano para luego reincorporarla, optaron por despedirla directamente. Esta es una práctica habitual en un sector que convierte la estabilidad laboral en una quimera, jugando con la vida y el sustento de quienes se dedican a la enseñanza.


Desde la CNT no toleraremos que se siga despidiendo a docentes al llegar el verano para ahorrar costes, tratándolos como mercancía desechable. Los docentes son fundamentales para el desarrollo y el futuro de nuestra sociedad; su trabajo es esencial y merece condiciones dignas, un reconocimiento real y una garantía de estabilidad.


Este no es el primer conflicto al que nos enfrentamos en el ámbito de los centros de formación. Ya hemos librado batallas sindicales contra otras academias de inglés que intentaban imponer estos mismos abusos, y las hemos ganado.


Las y los trabajadores nos organizamos y las victorias se consiguen gracias a la unidad de todas y a la lucha sindical. Ante el abuso individual, la respuesta colectiva. No daremos un paso atrás hasta que se respeten los derechos de nuestros compañeros y se ponga fin a estas prácticas abusivas en el sector educativo.


Si tú también sufres el fraude de los contratos temporales, si te dejan en la calle al terminar el curso o si quieren hacerte creer que no hay nada que hacer, recuerda que la solidaridad es nuestra mejor arma. ¡Organízate con la CNT!


Galego

A CNT inicia conflito contra a academia de inglés This Way en Vigo: Ese non é o camiño!


As academias de inglés e os centros de formación continúan profundando na precarización do sector, aproveitándose de maneira fraudulenta da figura do contrato fixo-descontinuo. O último caso ten como escenario a cidade de Vigo, onde a CNT ven de iniciar un conflito sindical contra a empresa This Way.


A táctica desta empresa é tan vella como perversa: en lugar de respectar a lei e pasar á nosa afiliada ao período de inactividade estival para reincorporala despois do verán, decidiron directamente despedila. Trátase dunda práctica habitual nun sector que converte a estabilidade laboral nunha quimera, xogando coa vida e co pan de quen se dedica ao ensino.


Desde a CNT non imos tolerar que se siga desbotando ás docentes cando chega o verán para aforrar custos, tratando ao persoal como mercadoría de descarte. As profesoras son fundamentais para o desenvolvemento e o futuro da nosa sociedade; a seu labor é esencial e merece unhas condicións dignas, un recoñecemento real e a garantía de estabilidade.


Este non é o primeiro conflito que enfrontamos no ámbito dos centros de formación. Xa mantivemos batallas sindicais contra outras academias de inglés que pretendían impoñer estes mesmos abusos, e ganámolas.


As traballadoras nos organizamos e as vitorias conséguense grazas á unidade de todas e á loita sindical. Fronte ao abuso individual, a resposta colectiva. Non imos dar un paso atrás ata lograr que se respecten os dereitos da nosa compañeira e se poña fin a estas prácticas abusivas no sector do ensino.


Se ti tamén estás a sufrir a fraude dos contratos fixos-descontinuos, se che botan á rúa cando remata o curso ou se queren facerche crer que non hai nada que facer, lembra que a solidariedade é a nosa mellor arma. Organízate coa CNT!

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: John Amagoalik seeks funding to stay in Nunavut while case winds through court
content:
Lawyers for John Amagoalik are scheduled to appear in court Friday in the hope of securing emergency funding that would allow him to stay in his home while his lawsuit against the Nunavut government proceeds.


Last month, the retired politician filed an

application for a judicial review

 in response to the Department of Health’s refusal to fund his medical care and housing in Iqaluit.


Amagoalik is revered by many as the “Father of Nunavut.” He dedicated decades of his life to advancing Inuit rights.


He had been living at the Embassy West long-term care home in Ottawa before returning to Iqaluit this summer. While his goal is to

live his final days

 in the territory he helped create, his family says they can’t afford to make that happen without funding from Nunavut’s Health Department.


The department has stated this type of funding

does not fall

 under its authority.


Nunavut Chief Justice Susan Cooper is scheduled to preside over Friday’s hearing, said Andrew Morrison, among the lawyers that represent Amagoalik. She’s set to decide whether to grant funding that would allow Amagoalik to remain in Nunavut during the judicial review process.


The hearing for a judicial review of the Health Department’s decision not to fund Amagoalik’s care will happen at a later date, Morrison said.


“The government was willing to pay for his care in Ottawa,” he said in an interview Monday. “We don’t think that Inuit elders should have to have to chose between going south for their health and their homeland.”


Nunavut’s Health Department did not immediately respond when reached for comment.


Spokesperson Charmaine Deogracias has previously stated that the Health Department does not have the legislative authority to fund independently arranged private care and can not make exceptions in individual cases.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Revives Election Fraud Claims Days After Pledging to Accept Midterms
content:
“Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest?” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

President Donald Trump issued a Truth Social post on Monday morning casting doubts on the “honesty” of the 2026 midterm elections, less than one week after initially stating he would accept the results.

“Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest?” Trump wrote in his latest missive about the midterms.

He went on to reprise grievances from past elections, in which he errantly claimed that results that came in later (often due to absentee ballots being counted after polls closed) were somehow suspicious.

“How could the Polls be so wrong??? Some early voting ‘dumps’ were so large that it was impossible to win, no matter how many people went to vote,” Trump wrote. Contrary to Trump’s objections, polls widely predicted Democratic gains this midterm season.

Trump also expressed doubts about the security of voting machines, a familiar but debunked claim he frequently used to suggest that his 2020 presidential election loss was somehow rigged.

“It’s all about the machines, which are far more important than the voter!” Trump said.

Trump’s Monday morning post comes just six days after he told The New York Times that he would respect the results of the midterms, telling the publication he was “absolutely willing” to accept the outcome after Republicans were routed by Democrats in races determining control of both houses of Congress. Trump also said he was “look[ing] forward to working with” Democrats when they take office in January.

At multiple points over the past year — including in late October, just weeks before the elections took place — Trump said he would only accept the results of the midterms if he deemed them “honest.”

Trump’s initial statement declaring that he’d accept the results likely surprised millions of Americans. In polling conducted last month, 7 in 10 Americans said they didn’t believe the president would accept the results, while fewer than 3 in 10 respondents said they believed he would.

It’s unclear whether Trump is planning to demand that Republicans take action to address his false claims of “dishonesty” within the election results. One theory worrying political observers is that Trump and Republicans could attempt to demand that the House Clerk refuse to seat newly elected lawmakers in January, justifying the action by citing unfounded claims of election fraud. That move could create a constitutional crisis, as it would be unclear as to who would be in control of Congress, the outgoing session or the incoming one, and would likely require judicial intervention.

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we need $50,000 in the next 10 days. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference.

author: Hend Salama Abo Helow
title: Israel Is Rapidly Turning the Yellow Line Into a Permanent Border in Gaza
content:
Israel is building an earthen wall along the line that marks the ever-expanding territory within Gaza that it controls.

Israel is building an earthen wall along the line that marks the ever-expanding territory within Gaza that it controls.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

During a creative and journalistic writing training program I joined in Gaza City to nurture the skills of emerging writers, one seat remained empty, session after session. It belonged to Sarah, whose name has been changed to protect her identity, and who never managed to escape the brunt of Israeli violence long enough to attend a single session.

Sarah currently lives with her family in a half-demolished home just a few meters from the “Yellow Line” — the ever-shifting, poorly demarcated boundary marked by yellow concrete blocks that is intended to separate areas under Israeli military control from the rest of the Gaza Strip.

Her family was forced to return there after enduring the grim realities of life in displacement camps. Caught between two impossible choices, Sarah lamented, “Venturing outside my home may cost me my life.”

When I reached out to her, curious to know why she had been unable to attend a writing program that remains a distant dream for hundreds of writers, she replied in a grieving voice: “I live beside the Yellow Line in the south, while the sessions are held in Gaza City, and the killing machine is waiting outside my home.”

She described the incessant rattling of drones overhead, the deafening echoes of explosions, the ever-present threat of being targeted by a quadcopter, and the anguished cries of grieving mothers, bereaved fathers, and frightened children.

“Together, these sounds, mingled with deep-seated fear, have turned even the most mundane activities indispensable to our survival into perilous undertakings.”

Meanwhile, the rumbling of bulldozers and the scraping of earth intruded upon Sarah’s daily life. From her window, she watched as a new earthen berm gradually took shape, rising higher and stretching farther with each passing day.

“The Yellow Line keeps creeping forward, while a new earthen berm rises day by day, obscuring our view of what lies beyond it,” Sarah said.

Citing satellite imagery supplied by Planet Labs PBC in July 2026, an Associated Press investigation revealed the construction of a new earthen barrier, resembling a physical border, along stretches of the Yellow Line — a supposedly temporary demarcation separating Israeli-controlled territory from the rest of Gaza pending further withdrawals under the U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement — and in some places beyond it.

These tall sand embankments cut through demolished Palestinian communities, further entrenching Israel’s expanding area of control.

According to the investigation, the earthen berms have been constructed near Rafah, across Khan Younis, and stretch northward toward Gaza City. By July 2026, they extended for more than 23 kilometers (14 miles), equivalent to more than half the length of Gaza’s approximately 40-kilometer coastline.

These tall sand embankments cut through demolished Palestinian communities, further entrenching Israel’s expanding area of control. According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, access-restricted areas had grown to encompass 65 percent of the Gaza Strip by June 2026. Meanwhile, Israeli forces continue clearing and demolishing Palestinian land and homes, in what humanitarian experts describe as a scorched-earth policy and ethnic cleansing.

“My neighborhood was once marked by greenhouses, towering green trees, and flourishing gardens. But it truly breaks my heart to scan the horizon and not catch sight of even a centimeter of greenery anymore,” Sarah said, her voice quivering. “My life is now colored only in grey and blood.”

It appears that Israel has been constructing this barrier since February 2026, justifying its construction on security grounds and equipping it with intelligence and technological assets. Yet this justification is flatly contradicted by the mounting death toll among Gazans near the Yellow Line and its designation as a killing zone for Palestinians attempting to check on their homes or salvage the remnants of their belongings.

author: Natalia Viana
title: As Big Techs saíram perdedoras das eleições nos EUA?
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Xeque na Democracia, enviada toda segunda-feira, 12h. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui.


Foram pelo menos US$ 800 milhões. Juntos, os bilionários das Big Techs e Criptomoedas

fazem

 parte dos 20 maiores doadores de campanhas para as eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA. Sozinho, Elon Musk doou quase meio bilhão de dólares. Os investidores Marc Andreessen e Ben Horowitz criaram seu próprio Super Pac – comitê de apoio eleitoral regado a dinheiro privado – chamado Leading the Future apenas para defender pouca regulação federal sobre a IA; arrecadaram US$ 100 milhões.  


Mesmo assim, a campanha eleitoral norte-americana foi repleta de promessas como essa, de Gina Hinojosa, que derrotou o governador republicano no Texas de maneira histórica – o estado não elegia um governador democrata desde 1988. 


“Quando eu for governadora vou propor uma moratória de todas as aprovações de data centers até os legisladores aprovarem leis que protegem os texanos, para dar aos texanos um assento na mesa para decidir se e como os data centers chegarão às suas comunidades”. Uma das suas propostas é fazer uma auditoria sobre os data centers que pediram autorização para usar a rede elétrica do Texas.   


Em especial,

o embate em torno da construção de data centers tornou-se um dos principais temas de campanha em diferentes regiões dos EUA

. Três dos estados em que a cadeira do Senado mudou de republicano para democrata têm um problema de rápida expansão de data centers: além do Texas, Ohio e Iowa chegam a ter de duas a dez vezes o número médio de data centers por estado.  


Fato é que os eleitores não estão convencidos de que a construção de data centers vai beneficiar suas comunidades.

 E as pesquisas têm apontado para essa insatisfação. 


Uma pesquisa feita pela Ipsos com o Washington Post descobriu que 2/3 dos americanos se opõem à construção de novos data centers, enquanto 57% dizem que a IA é um mal para a sociedade e 67% desaprovam a política de “liberou geral” abraçada pelo governo Trump.


Além dos data centers, a percepção negativa da população quanto à IA, resultado das demissões massivas que já estão ocorrendo, fizeram com que, hoje, defender a desregulação tenha se tornado uma medida pouco popular. 


Portanto, os investimentos dos tech bros não renderam os votos esperados. Eles foram derrotados nas urnas. Parece que essas eleições marcaram a primeira vez que as Big Techs se tornaram uma pauta tóxica.  


Os resultados desta derrota foram sentidos na própria semana eleitoral. Com a resistência à construção desenfreada de infraestrutura necessária para a IA nos EUA, expressa em votos, a perspectiva de uma redução da corrida desenfreada derrubou as bolsas pelo mundo; Wall Street levou um tombo – perdeu 3 trilhões de valor em apenas um dia. A CEO da Meta já reconheceu que será mais difícil construir novos data centers, e a empresa deve se concentrar em ampliar a capacidade dos já existentes.   


Espera-se uma nova onda regulatória, impulsionada pelos democratas eleitos em diferentes estados e também no Congresso. 


Na Câmara dos Deputados, há um projeto de lei proposto por deputados democratas que prevê supervisão federal sobre modelos de IA mais poderosos e impedir que os estados tenham poder de fazer leis livremente. No Senado, um grupo bipartidário está articulando a criação de um padrão federal de segurança para inteligência artificial (IA) que permitiria ao governo federal proibir o lançamento de produtos considerados inseguros.     


O provável futuro presidente da Câmara dos Deputados, Hakeem Jeffries – que deve ser o primeiro negro a assumir o cargo – tem prometido que o Congresso tem que agir para criar uma regulação para a IA. 


“Nós queremos garantir que os empreendedores norte-americanos e empresas possam continuar liderando neste espaço e não ser superados pelo Partido Comunista Chinês. Mas, por outro lado, temos que garantir que o povo americano de fato goze dos benefícios da inteligência artificial sem ser sujeito às suas desvantagens muito reais, muito graves e perigosas”, afirmou em um evento de campanha.


Ele já disse que concorda com a ideia de uma moratória no desenvolvimento de IA, algo que já foi aprovado em diferentes estados. 


“É [um perigo] muito real, em que pese o que o Donald Trump diga sobre o assunto, e requer ação imediata de modo consistente com o que algumas das vozes mais …

author: Sharon Lerner
title: Trump Admin Awarded $40M in Federal Contracts to Firm Linked to President’s Sons
content:
Donald Jr. and Eric Trump work as advisers for a firm that invested in the awardee’s parent company in February.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The Trump administration awarded a small biosecurity company nearly $40 million to screen for Ebola and other infectious diseases just months after a firm linked to President Donald Trump’s elder sons invested in its parent company, according to records and interviews.

The contracts, one to screen for Ebola in several U.S. airports and the other to respond to disease outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo, are seven times the total value of government contracts the company had directly received before.

The company, XpresTest, has years of experience monitoring for COVID-19 and other diseases for the government at U.S. airports. That makes its parent, XWELL, an unusual hybrid, selling both spa treatments and biosecurity services. Last year, it made most of its money from waxing salons and airport spas that offer manicures, massages and “chakra beds.”

The contracts are the latest example of the president’s family benefiting financially from his administration’s actions. And the stakes for these deals are particularly high. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, an Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,000 people this year, and the federal government is trying to stop the pathogen from coming to the U.S.

XpresTest has never worked with Ebola or provided biosecurity services abroad, let alone in the kind of volatile locales it’s now expected to work in. The CEO of its parent company, Ezra Ernst, said XpresTest won both contracts in a competitive bidding process and pointed to its years of experience doing screening for COVID-19 and other pathogens at American airports. But even he acknowledged that working internationally is “a new thing for us” and expressed uncertainty about being able to complete the work in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

“This is a risky contract. I’m not sure we can do it,” Ernst said in an interview.

Jeremy Konyndyk, who helped oversee the U.S. government’s response to a 2014 Ebola outbreak in West Africa, said there are some parallels between monitoring for COVID-19 and Ebola at airports, but he said it’s concerning that the government would award such a lucrative contract to a company that has no experience in Africa.

“There are countless organizations in the world that have decades of experience doing this work,” Konyndyk said. “I have to wonder why the hell they’re not going with someone who has actually done this before.”

Under previous administrations, the U.S. government addressed international disease outbreaks in partnership with the World Health Organization. But Trump withdrew from the group last year, dismantled the U.S. Agency for International Development, which handled much of this work, and dramatically scaled back the global presence of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

At the same time, the State Department launched the America First Global Health Strategy, which calls for the U.S. to use aid to foreign countries to “promote American companies and American innovations abroad.” This March, the State Department announced it would be giving up to $4.5 billion in funding for various purposes, including responding to infectious disease outbreaks.

Under that program, XPresTest was awarded $20 million. Other funding went to better-known global aid nonprofits, including International Medical Corps, Save the Children and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, whose awards ranged from $25 million to $35 million.

The CDC also awarded XPresTest a contract, for $18.8 million.

In response to questions from ProPublica about XPresTest and its parent company, XWELL, the State Department noted the firm’s previous work screening for diseases at airports under a contract with the CDC and said its own award was made “through a competitive process that builds on this successful model.”

The CDC did not respond to a request for comment.

A spokesperson for the president’s sons Donald Jr. and Eric Trump said that they are “merely passive, minority investors in a fund that invested in this company,” and that they had no “involvement in or knowledge regarding the negotiation or procurement of any of its contracts, including any government contracts.”

author: Sophia Cope
title: U.S. Supreme Court Deals Final Blow to Corporate Human Rights Accountability
content:
For the past two decades, the U.S. Supreme Court has been slowly weakening the Alien Tort Statute (ATS), a key human rights law that allows foreign nationals to sue persons or entities in civil court for harms resulting from violations of international law. The court’s recent ruling in Cisco Systems, Inc. v. Doe I dealt the law a final blow, foreclosing—absent new legislation by Congress—any future ability by plaintiffs to use the law to hold technology companies accountable for aiding and abetting human rights abuses. EFF filed multiple amicus briefs in the case, including most recently in the Supreme Court.

The ATS was passed by the very first Congress in 1789 and in just a few words gives U.S. federal courts jurisdiction to hear civil claims brought by foreign nationals against defendants who violated “the law of nations or a treaty of the United States." There has been a longstanding question about what counts as a valid civil claim under “the law of nations.”

In Sosa v. Alvarez-Machain (2004), the Supreme Court had noted three historical international law claims that the First Congress likely had in mind: violation of safe conducts, infringement of the rights of ambassadors, and piracy, collectively known as the Blackstone Three.

The Sosa court also held that federal courts may recognize other substantive causes of action under the ATS if they reflect international norms that are “specific, universal, and obligatory,” stating that this “door is still ajar subject to vigilant doorkeeping, and thus open to a narrow class of international norms today.”

Thus, the Sosa court recognized that the ATS could be used to bring claims related to historical violations of international law as well as select newer claims reflecting modern concepts of human rights.

In Cisco, the Supreme Court overruled the second Sosa holding. The majority held that the current case, a technology company aiding and abetting torture and other human rights abuses, was beyond the scope of the original three ATS claims and it was not for the court to create new ways of enforcing international law. The court said:

[W]e close the door that Sosa cracked to judicially created ATS liability. We do not disturb Sosa’s holding that the ATS is a jurisdictional statute; nor do we revisit its assumption that causes of action are available for torts corresponding to the Blackstone three. We conclude only that Sosa was overly optimistic in its prediction that there might be a narrow class of cases in which courts may create ATS actions without infringing on the prerogatives of the political branches. In truth, this class is a null set.

What result for this case? Cisco argues that the Ninth Circuit erred in holding that aiding-and-abetting liability exists under the ATS for the torts alleged by the plaintiffs. Cisco is correct. Courts cannot create new rights of action to remedy violations of international law, so there is necessarily no liability for aiding and abetting such violations. Plaintiffs’ ATS claims against Cisco must be dismissed.

The Supreme Court’s ending of the plaintiffs’ case against Cisco is hugely disappointing given that the case has been going on since 2011 and the Ninth Circuit in 2023 allowed the case to move forward in an excellent and well-reasoned opinion. The court held, in part:

We conclude that Plaintiffs’ allegations, accepted as true, are sufficient to state a plausible claim that Cisco provided essential technical assistance to the douzheng [violent struggle] of Falun Gong with awareness that the international law violations of torture, arbitrary detention, disappearance, and extrajudicial killing were substantially likely to take place.

The plaintiffs sued Cisco for the company’s role in building and deploying the “Golden Shield,” also referred to as “The Great Firewall of China”—a vast surveillance system that Cisco began building in the late 1990s and that the company customized to enable the Chinese government to target disfavored minorities, including members of the Falun Gong religion.

The thirteen plaintiffs—Falun Gong practitioners—alleged arrest, detention, and torture, including of themselves and family members, at least one of whom died by beating while being detained. The allegations were horrific: the plaintiffs were placed in forced labor camps, beaten with steel rods, shocked with electric batons, and endured sleep deprivation and violent force-feeding.

Importantly, the plaintiffs also alleged that …
